**[CHAR-1]** E — Exultation does not bypass cognition in this corpus; it builds on it. The pattern is consistently: know God's act → exult in response. There is no instance of exultation preceding or bypassing the knowledge of its grounds. The characteristic deepens rather than impairs cognitive engagement with divine reality — the jubilant exultation of Psa 89:16 ("exult in your name all the day") suggests that sustained exultation sustains the attentiveness to God's character that produced it.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Joy deepens cognition in its healthy form: Psa 97:8 (joy at God's judgments reinforces the understanding of divine justice); Neh 8:12 (joy following understanding sustains the engagement with God's word). Joy can momentarily disrupt cognitive function in intense encounters: Luk 24:41 ("while they still disbelieved for joy" — joy so overwhelming that it temporarily outpaces belief); Act 12:14 (Rhoda's joy overrides practical reasoning). These disruptions are not presented as failures but as expressions of Joy's intensity exceeding cognitive capacity momentarily.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Suffering-Joy enables cognition by clarifying value hierarchy: the person who genuinely rejoices amid suffering has cognitively apprehended that eschatological reality is more determinative than present circumstance. This reordering of cognitive priority — the eternal over the temporal — is itself a form of cognitive clarity that Suffering-Joy both requires and reinforces.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Gladness deepens cognition: sustained correct evaluation of what is genuinely good trains and sharpens the cognitive-moral faculty (the wisdom literature's training purpose). Misdirected Gladness (Isa 41:7's craftsman; Num 14:3's fear-evaluation) bypasses or distorts cognition — the person reaches a "good" verdict without actually exercising careful moral reasoning. The Psa 119:68 pattern ("you are good and do good; teach me your statutes") explicitly requests continued cognitive formation in divine goodness.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Delight enables and deepens cognition: Psa 1:2 (sustained meditation driven by Delight); Psa 111:2 (study driven by Delight); Psa 119:24 (testimonies as counselors — Delight in them producing cognitive guidance). In its distorted form Delight can bypass cognition: Pro 18:2 (the fool takes pleasure only in expressing his opinion — self-directed Delight short-circuiting the cognitive engagement with understanding); Rev 13:3 (marveling at the beast — perceptive captivation bypassing cognitive assessment of the beast's true nature).

**[CHAR-5]** E — Genuine Pleasure in wisdom deepens cognition: Pro 2:10's "knowledge will be pleasant to your soul" — when wisdom is in the heart, the soul's Pleasure in knowledge reinforces the desire to know more; pleasantness in knowledge sustains cognitive engagement. Distorted Pleasure (Pro 9:17 — stolen bread) bypasses honest cognition by making the wrong thing feel pleasant, thereby short-circuiting the evaluation that would recognise its true character.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Wonder simultaneously deepens and disciplines cognition: it deepens by motivating sustained meditation and inquiry into God's acts (Psa 119:27; 145:5); it disciplines by restraining overreach (Psa 131:1 — I do not occupy myself with things too marvellous for me). Wonder-as-epistemological-humility is the most distinctive cognitive-Wonder interaction: the person in genuine Wonder is cognitively active (meditating, considering, studying) but not overconfident (acknowledging the limits of comprehension).

**[CLUSTER]** E — The most analytically significant cluster-level finding on cognition: (1) **Delight (Char 4) is the most powerful cognitive-driver in the cluster** — it produces sustained meditation and study as natural overflow of being delighted in a subject; the person's deepest Delight determines what they most consistently think about and explore; (2) **Gladness (Char 3) is the most cognitively-constituted** — but it deepens cognition by exercising it rather than by producing it; sustained moral evaluation forms the evaluative faculty itself; (3) **Wonder (Char 6) both deepens and disciplines** — it deepens by motivating meditation (Psa 119:27; 145:5) and disciplines by restraining overreach (Psa 131:1); Wonder-as-epistemological-humility is the unique Wonder-cognition interaction in the cluster; (4) **Joy (Char 2) can temporarily exceed cognitive function** (Luk 24:41 — "while they still disbelieved for joy"; Act 12:14 — Rhoda's joy overriding practical reasoning) — the most intense Joy momentarily surpasses cognitive capacity; this is not presented as failure but as evidence of the affective capacity exceeding the cognitive; (5) **Suffering-Joy (Char 7) enables a specific cognitive clarity** — the reordering of cognitive priority (eternal over temporal) is both what Suffering-Joy requires and what it produces.

**[CHAR-1]** E — In its cognitive-collapse form (idolatry exposed, confident belief destroyed), shame **impairs** cognition — the shamed idol-maker "goes in confusion." In its corrective form, shame **deepens** cognition: after instruction-and-shame (Jer 31:19), the person comes to a clearer self-knowledge. The conscience-awakening passages (1Cor 6:5; 15:34) show shame *enabling* cognitive clarity: Paul directs shame at the Corinthians' failure to produce a wise person for disputes — shame is the tool for awakening cognitive wisdom. Thus shame's cognitive effect mirrors its perceptive effect: destructive in its paralysing form, constructive in its corrective form.

**[CHAR-2]** E — CHAR-2 collapses confident cognition: the defeated "go in confusion" — their ability to think through their situation and act effectively is destroyed. Cognitive paralysis accompanies military defeat (Jer 49:23 — "melting in fear, troubled like the sea"). In VCG-03, God's abasement targets the cognitive self-assessment of the proud.

---

**[CHAR-3]** E — The cognitive worth-assessment process is engaged and distorted in CHAR-3: the dishonorer makes a wrong cognitive judgment about worth. The structural-dishonour mode (VCG-02) is more cognitively neutral — it is the result of sovereign assignment rather than a cognitive failure.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — CHAR-4 is a cognitive operation — the conscience assesses against a standard (God's sight, created order, community norms) and produces a judgment. The cognitive faculty is CHAR-4's primary operating mode. VCG-03 shows cognitive corruption: the evaluative judgment is produced but by a wrong standard.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — The contempt-er's cognitive faculty is engaged: the worth-assessment judgment ("this person is of no account") is a cognitive act. 1Cor 6:4's cognitive assessment about standing; Rom 14:3/10's cognitive-evaluative judgment about a brother's worth before God — these show the cognitive faculty producing CHAR-5. For the recipient, the cognitive dimension is engaged in the ongoing self-assessment that contempt-shame distorts.

---

**[CHAR-6]** E — Cognition is engaged in CHAR-6 through the moral self-assessment that innocence requires. Abimelech's appeal to his innocence (Gen 20:5) involves cognitive self-assessment: he knows he acted in ignorance and moral intention. Psa 73:13's lament involves cognitive evaluation: the psalmist has cognitively assessed his own moral maintenance and found it, in his experience, to have been in vain. The cognitive faculty is engaged in CHAR-6's self-assessment and moral accounting.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — Cognition is engaged across all six with varying prominence. Char 4 is primarily cognitive (the evaluative judgment is a cognitive act). Chars 1, 3, 5 engage cognition in self-assessment and worth-assessment functions. Char 2 engages it in the cognitive collapse of the humiliated (confusion, dismay). Char 6 engages it in the cognitive self-assessment that constitutes the innocence-claim. Cluster-level cognitive theme: the shame-field is irreducibly cognitive — it involves ongoing assessment of standing, worth, and moral quality across all six characteristics. The cognitive faculty is the site where worth-assessments originate and where the shame-field's distortions begin. The correction of the shame-field therefore requires cognitive correction as one of its components.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — CHAR-1 impairs cognition in two registers. First, wisdom/discernment: Eze 28:17 (vc=34047, M08-A1-VCG-02) — "you corrupted your wisdom for the sake of your splendour" — CHAR-1 directly corrupts the highest cognitive faculty, so that what the person discerns and understands is distorted by the self's elevation. Second, self-assessment: Rom 12:16 (vc=60877, M08-A4-VCG-01) — "never be wise in your own sight" — pride produces an inflated and inaccurate self-assessment; 1Sa 2:3 (vc=12084, M08-A4-VCG-05) — "the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed" — pride misjudges its own standing before the divine cognitive standard. The impairment is not of all cognition but of the self-directed cognitive assessment that would give the person an accurate picture of where they stand before God and others.

**[CHAR-2]** E — CHAR-2 impairs cognition through self-deception: Obd 3 (vc=34108, M08-B-VCG-02) and Jer 49:16 (vc=34115) both name deception as the cognitive consequence — the person genuinely believes they are secure or right when they are not. Mal 3:15 (vc=34106, M08-B-VCG-02): the arrogant "seem to prosper" — an inverted cognitive evaluation of moral-consequential reality. Luk 3:8 (vc=55578, M08-B-VCG-03): the cognitive claim "we have Abraham as our father" is a self-justifying miscalculation of one's standing before God.

**[CHAR-3]** E — CHAR-3 impairs cognition through: (a) attribution failure — 1Cor 4:7 (vc=33871): misattributing received goods as self-generated; (b) self-comparison distortion — 2Cor 10:12: "without understanding" — the self-comparison process generates a cognitive picture of the self that lacks genuine understanding. For VCG-02 examined boasting: 2Cor 1:12 (vc=33912, M08-C-VCG-02): conscience's testimony as the cognitive ground of legitimate self-commendation — conscience-based cognition enables accurate examined boasting.

**[CHAR-4]** E — CHAR-4 impairs cognition in two specific registers: (a) Self-knowledge — Rom 12:3 (vc=60866): thinking above one's warranted measure; (b) General epistemic capacity — 1Ti 6:4 (vc=33925): "understanding nothing" — the inflation corrupts the entire cognitive apparatus so that nothing is accurately understood. The impairment is self-reinforcing: the inflated self-picture is generated by the cognitive faculty, and then that same inflated picture corrupts the cognitive faculty's operation for all subsequent assessment.

**[CHAR-5]** E — CHAR-5 impairs cognition through self-deception: Obd 3 (vc=65674): "the pride of your heart has deceived you" — the cognitive assessment of invulnerability is a deception; the person's actual vulnerability before God is the reality that CHAR-5's cognitive inflation conceals. Isa 47:8 (vc=9563): the self-sufficiency claim ("I am, and there is no one besides me") is cognitively false — Babylon's structural power is finite and reversible, but CHAR-5 generates a cognitive picture of ontological self-completeness.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All five characteristics impair cognition, but through different mechanisms. CHAR-1 displaces God from the cognitive awareness. CHAR-2 generates self-deceptive overconfidence. CHAR-3 produces misattribution of received goods. CHAR-4 generates the most comprehensive cognitive impairment — "understanding nothing" (1Ti 6:4, M08-D-VCG-02). CHAR-5 generates the cognitive ontological self-sufficiency claim. The cluster comparison reveals a severity gradient: CHAR-4's cognitive impairment is the most comprehensive (understanding nothing), while CHAR-2's and CHAR-5's are more directionally specific (self-deception about vulnerability, not about everything). The cluster-synthesis: cognitive impairment in M08 ranges from the directionally-specific (CHAR-2, CHAR-5) to the comprehensively-total (CHAR-4), with CHAR-4 representing M08's most catastrophic cognitive endpoint.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Submission *rightly orders and deepens* genuine cognition. Taking every thought captive to Christ (2Cor10:5) is not the suppression of thinking but its reorientation under a legitimate authority — it enables more accurate cognition by placing it under a reliable epistemic authority (Christ) rather than leaving it to self-generated "lofty opinions." Rom16:19 — Paul redirects the Romans' obedient disposition toward "wisdom as to what is good" — submission enables the discernment that pure self-generated reasoning cannot produce. The absence of genuine submission is linked to cognitive self-deception: the "lofty opinions" of 2Cor10:5 are the cognitive dysfunction that resists the knowledge of God.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Contrition *enables accurate cognition* of one's moral condition. The person in genuine contrition is one who has arrived at a truthful cognitive assessment of their own failure — the breaking is, in part, the cognitive-experiential event of genuine self-knowledge before God. The characteristic deepens cognitive honesty by validating it: the person who genuinely confronts their failure rather than defending against it is engaging the cognitive faculty most accurately. The structural opposite (self-justification, pride, hardening) impairs accurate moral cognition by distorting the person's self-assessment.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Meekness/gentleness *enables more accurate cognition* of others' conditions by removing the distorting lens of assumed superiority. The high priest who genuinely knows his own weakness (Heb5:2) cognises the erring other's condition more accurately — without the distortions that self-protective pride introduces. The characteristic thus deepens the cognitive capacity for accurate social and moral perception by grounding it in genuine self-knowledge.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Semnotēs *deepens credible cognition* in the teaching and leadership registers. Tit2:7 — teaching authenticated by dignity — enables hearers to receive the instruction as genuinely credible, enhancing their cognitive reception of the content. The characteristic enables the cognitive function of teaching to be received as weighty rather than dismissed as ungrounded performance.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Willing-heartedness *enables wholehearted cognitive engagement*. 1Ch28:21 — "every willing man who has skill" — willingness enables the full deployment of skill; the unwilling would bring their skill under compulsion without genuine engagement. The characteristic enables the cognitive faculty to be applied with genuine investment rather than with the distracted half-engagement of reluctant compliance.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Humility *enables and deepens* genuine cognition. Pro11:2 establishes the enabling connexion: the humble possess wisdom, the proud gain disgrace — the cognitive capacity for genuine understanding is linked to the posture of humility. This is consistent with the perceptive pattern (T3.1.2): the self-enclosure of pride distorts cognition, while the openness of humility enables accurate perception and therefore accurate understanding. The Colossian critique of false humility (Col2:18) shows that distorted self-assessment (cognitive pride operating within an outwardly humble practice) impairs rather than enables genuine understanding. Genuine humility enables cognition by removing the self-protective filter that keeps the person from accurately knowing themselves, God, and others.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All six characteristics enable and deepen cognition; none bypass or impair it. The enabling mechanisms differ by characteristic in analytically significant ways. Humility (CHAR-1) enables cognition as an epistemic virtue — Pro11:2 (humility → wisdom) establishes the structural connexion; the humble person's openness enables accurate perception and therefore accurate understanding. Submission (CHAR-2) rightly orders cognition — 2Cor10:5 (taking thoughts captive reorients the mind under legitimate epistemic authority); the absence of genuine submission is linked to cognitive self-deception (lofty opinions raised against the knowledge of God). Contrition (CHAR-3) enables accurate moral cognition by allowing genuine self-knowledge to register rather than being blocked by self-justification. Meekness and Gentleness (CHAR-4) enables more accurate cognition of others' conditions by removing the distorting lens of assumed superiority. Dignity (CHAR-5) enables the cognitive reception of authority and teaching by providing the character-ground that authenticates content (Tit2:7 — integrity + dignity enables reception). Willing-heartedness (CHAR-6) enables wholehearted cognitive engagement — 1Ch28:21 (skill deployed alongside willingness) confirms that genuine skilled service requires willing-heartedness as its motivational ground. Cluster-level pattern: CHAR-1 and CHAR-2 are the most distinctively cognition-enabling (epistemic virtue; cognitive reordering); the other four enable cognitive engagement in their specific relational registers.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — Wilful sinning *bypasses* cognition in the act of commission: the will proceeds despite the available cognitive awareness that the act is wrong. The evidence for bypassing: 1Sa 15:24 — Saul knew the command (he had received it from Samuel); he bypassed it under social pressure. Jos 7:20 — Achan confesses knowing what he did ("Truly I have sinned against the Lord God of Israel, and this is what I did") — the cognitive knowledge preceded the act. The VCG-03 deterrence corpus suggests that sinning is prevented when cognition is *amplified* (Exo 20:20 — divine display is cognitive input; Psa 119:11 — word stored = cognitive reservoir). Where cognition is bypassed or insufficient, sinning proceeds.

**[CHAR-10]** E — Different patterns per mechanism. (1) *Enticement bypasses cognition*: Jam 1:14 — enticement operates through desire ("his own desire") which precedes deliberate cognitive engagement — the luring occurs before the will has made a reasoned choice. (2) *Hypocrisy distorts cognition*: Gal 2:13 — acting hypocritically alongside others requires cognitive assessment of the social situation ("what will others think?") but produces a distorted moral output; (3) *Apostasy operates through cognitive-instructional distortion*: Act 21:21 — teaching that allegedly redirects the Jews' cognitive understanding of their covenantal obligations.

**[CHAR-11]** E — The condition *distorts* cognition while simultaneously being what the law enables cognition to recognise. (1) *Distortion*: Heb 3:13 — "deceitfulness of sin" — the condition operates through cognitive deception, producing false self-assessment; (2) *Activation by law*: Rom 7:8/9 — "sin, seizing an opportunity through the commandment, produced in me all kinds of covetousness" — the law's cognitive content is seized by the condition to *activate* the very desire the law prohibits; the cognitive-law framework becomes the mechanism of the condition's arousal. The condition thus both evades correct cognition (deception) and exploits the cognitive framework (law) as the occasion for its full expression.
**[CHAR-12]** S — No direct evidence. The enslaving power's relationship to cognition is not addressed in the 9-verse corpus.

**[CHAR-13]** E — The record *impairs accurate self-cognition* while being fully known to God. Job 13:23 — Job cannot know the extent of his own record without divine disclosure; the cognitive faculty's self-assessment is inherently limited. Jer 16:10 — the people's cognitive question ("What is our iniquity?") under judgment shows the record has accumulated beyond their cognitive self-awareness. Pro 24:9 — conversely, the cognitive act of devising folly creates the record: active scheming is morally registered even if the schemer does not cognise it as sin.

**[CHAR-14]** E — The characteristic *reorients* cognition (Act 2:38 — metanoeō is a cognitive turning) and *is enabled by* cognitive testimony (Act 10:43 — the prophets' witness). The cognitive faculty is not merely passive but actively reoriented: the repentant person's mind has changed direction toward God. The forgiveness received does not bypass cognition (it is not a mystical bypassing of the rational faculty) but operates through it (the prophetic testimony → belief → forgiveness — Act 10:43).

**[CHAR-15]** E — The generational pattern *impairs* the cognitive integration of divine evidence into faith. Psa 78:32 — "despite his wonders, they did not believe" — the cognitive faculty received the evidence (wonders witnessed) but failed to produce the correct output (belief). The generational unbelief pattern short-circuits the cognitive pathway from evidence to trust: the inherited disposition toward not-believing overrides the cognitive faculty's normal evidence-processing function.

**[CHAR-16]** E — The sinner-identity *distorts* cognition at the self-assessment level. Amo 9:10 — "who say, 'Disaster shall not overtake or meet us'" — the habitual sinner's cognitive self-assessment is wrong; the sinner-identity produces a false cognitive conclusion about the self's safety. Joh 9:24 — "we know that this man is a sinner" — the authoritative religious establishment's cognitive verdict is wrong; the sinner-identity-label is misapplied with cognitive certainty. Conversely, Rom 7:13 — the commandment deepens cognitive understanding of sin's true nature: the cognitive faculty is sharpened by the law's disclosure of what is "sinful beyond measure."

**[CHAR-17]** E — The guilt-state *clarifies retrospective moral cognition* and can *distort prospective cognition*. Gen 42:21 — the brothers' current guilt-distress clarifies their cognitive understanding of their past act's moral significance. Conversely: Eze 21:23 — "to them it will seem like a false divination" — the guilt-bearing community misinterprets divine judgment as false prophecy; the accumulated guilt distorts the cognitive capacity to correctly interpret what God is doing. Guilt thus has a bi-directional cognitive effect: retrospective clarity, prospective distortion.

**[CHAR-18]** E — Iniquity *distorts* cognition at the self-assessment level and *clarifies* it when conscience operates correctly. Psa 36:2 — the flattering self-cognitive distortion: the mind generates false conclusions about the self's moral condition. Hos 12:8 — the cognitively confident "I am rich... no iniquity in me" is the distorted verdict. Conversely: 2Sa 24:10 — David's cognitive recognition "I have sinned greatly" is accurate; the conscience's correct functioning produces clear cognitive self-assessment. The iniquity distorts cognition in proportion to the suppression of conscience.

**[CHAR-19]** E — Transgression *bypasses and suppresses* cognition in the sustained transgressor. Isa 46:8 — transgressors must be commanded to "recall it to mind" — their cognition has ceased to retain what they know. Pro 28:24 — "that is no transgression" — the deliberate cognitive reframing that suppresses accurate moral knowledge. Jer 2:29 — the people "contend" with God despite having all transgressed — their cognition has inverted, producing self-justifying reasoning instead of accurate self-assessment. Conversely, the cognitive faculty is deployed accurately by the penitent: Psa 51:3 — "I know my transgressions" — precise cognitive self-assessment.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Unintentional sinning operates through the *absence* of relevant cognition at the moment of the act — not through impairment of the cognitive faculty but through its lack of the morally necessary information. The cognitive faculty is intact; the sin occurs because it was not informed. The *realisation phase* then shows cognition activated and functioning: Lev 5:5 ("realizes"), Num 22:34 ("I did not know... now I know"). Cognition drives the transition from sinning-unknowingly to confessing-with-full-knowledge. The characteristic thus maps the cognitive faculty's before-and-after: uninformed → sinning; informed → confession and remedy.

**[CHAR-20]** E — Faithlessness *distorts* cognition at the self-assessment level. 2Ch 28:22 — Ahaz becoming "yet more faithless" under distress — the cognition fails to identify faithlessness as the cause of suffering and therefore misreads the corrective signal; Jer 12:6 — "though they speak friendly words to you" — the treacherous family's cognition generates a false presentation of loyalty while planning betrayal, showing treachery's cognitive deception-mode. The double cognitive movement: the faithless person's cognition produces false appearances of loyalty (Jer 12:6) while blinding itself to its own faithlessness (2Ch 28:22).

**[CHAR-21]** E — Perversion *corrupts* the cognitive faculty at its root. 1Ti 6:5 — "depraved in mind and deprived of the truth" — the two go together: mind-depravity produces truth-deprivation; the cognitive faculty cannot access truth when it is depraved. Isa 29:16 — the cognitive inversion is so complete the creature can say of its maker "He did not make me" — the most basic cognitive relationship (creature knowing its creator) is perverted. 2Cor 11:3 — the serpent-deceived leading astray of thoughts parallels Eve's deception — the cognitive faculty is corrupted by a deceptive external agent operating on it from outside.

**[CHAR-22]** E — Injustice *misdirects and impairs* cognition. Psa 64:6's "diligent search" for injustice shows cognition misdirected — the analytical capacity deployed toward planning wrong rather than right. Psa 53:1's heart-atheism shows cognition impaired at the foundational level: the mind that denies God cannot accurately perceive the moral order; Job 18:21 — the unjust person "knows not God" — the cognitive God-knowledge deficit produces the inner condition that enables injustice.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Confession *deepens* cognition: the act of naming sin precisely articulates what the cognitive faculty has understood. Dan 9:5's taxonomy of failure ("sinned... done wrong... acted wickedly... rebelled... turning aside from your commandments") is a cognitive achievement — the confessor has differentiated the multiple dimensions of what went wrong. Confession in this extended mode is simultaneously a cognitive act (understanding the sin more fully) and a communicative act (naming it). Hollow confession (Deu 1:41) shows that cognition can be present without producing the deepening effect — the people knew they had sinned but did not engage cognitively with what that meant for their next action.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Conscience suppression *impairs* cognition in the moral domain: the mind's capacity for accurate moral knowledge about itself is degraded. 1Cor 15:34 — the call to "wake up from your drunken stupor" implies that the cognitive faculty is currently impaired (stupor = reduced alertness and accuracy). Jer 16:10 — "what sin have we committed?" — the cognitive faculty produces an answer ("none that we can identify") that is incorrect. The impairment is specifically in the self-directed moral-cognitive capacity: the person can think about other things but cannot accurately cognize their own sinful state.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Refusal to repent *bypasses* cognition in the Heb 10:26 mode: the knowledge is present but the will acts against it. In the minimisation mode (1Ki 16:31), it *distorts* cognition by producing a false moral evaluation that enables continued refusal. Over time, sustained refusal may impair cognition by entrenching the false evaluation (minimisation) as the habitual cognitive framework, making accurate moral assessment progressively harder.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Habitual defection *impairs* the cognitive faculty in the domain of God-knowledge: 1Jo 3:6 — "never... known him" — the knowing of God that the cognitive faculty would normally enable is absent in the habitual sinner. 1Sa 2:25's non-listening impairs the cognitive-receptive function: the corrective input that should update the cognitive framework is refused. The cognitive impairment in habitual defection is thus in the knowledge-of-God dimension specifically: the general cognitive faculty may remain functional, but its capacity for the relational-theological knowing that would correct the sinning pattern is impaired.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Contagious sin *corrupts* the cognitive faculty by feeding it sinning content through authoritative channels. Deu 20:18 — the teaching of abominable practices — corrupts the community's moral-cognitive framework: what they come to know (their cognitive content about worship and conduct) is the Canaanite sinning practices. The corruption is systematic: once the cognitive framework has been reshaped by the transmitted sinning content, the community's moral reasoning operates within a corrupted reference system, making further sinning the natural cognitive output.

**[CHAR-8]** S — The corpus does not evidence how political revolt affects the cognitive faculty of the revolting party. The focus is on the political facts (the revolts occurred, the revolts are permanent) rather than the cognitive processes of those involved.

**[CHAR-9]** E — Sinful speech *impairs and distorts* cognition. 1Ti 6:4's "understands nothing" — the person who practices slander from conceit has a cognitive faculty that cannot accurately process reality; the speech is both evidence of the impairment and an agent of its deepening. The beast's constitutive blasphemy (VCG-03) represents the extreme: the creature whose cognition is entirely oriented against God — not merely distorted but wholly captured by anti-God orientation.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Wickedness-as-settled-person-identity impairs cognition by corrupting the deliberative faculty (Pro 12:5), generating morally alien reasoning (Job 21:16), systematically excluding God from the thought-life (Psa 10:4), and progressively closing the capacity for moral understanding (Dan 12:10). It also bypasses discernment — the wicked person acts without the cognitive check of moral discernment (Isa 5:23). The characteristic does not enable or deepen cognition in any positive sense; it subverts cognition by replacing truth-oriented reasoning with deception-oriented deliberation.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The characteristic impairs cognition by corrupting its evaluative and relational functions. Col 1:21 (vc=14424 — VCG-06) shows cognition becoming hostile — the mind evaluates others and God through a lens of enmity rather than receptivity. 1Ti 6:4 (vc=14470 — VCG-06) shows cognition producing "evil suspicions" — a cognitive state that generates false, damaging assessments of others. The characteristic does not eliminate cognitive capacity (the person still thinks, still reasons) but it redirects and corrupts cognitive output toward hostile and suspicious assessments. Mat 9:4 (VCG-03) shows the cognitive faculty actively generating "evil thoughts" — the cognitive engagement is active, not passive.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The characteristic impairs the cognitive faculty's evaluative function by inverting it (Pro 17:15 — VCG-01: perverted judgment) and bypasses reflective cognition in those who proceed into abomination without consideration (Isa 44:19 — VCG-05). Pro 15:26 (vc=1679 — VCG-02) shows the cognitive faculty actively generating abominable content — the thoughts themselves are corrupt — showing cognition operating but producing wrong output. Luk 16:15 (vc=21 — VCG-02) reveals the self-justifying cognitive construction ("justifying yourselves before men") as itself an abomination — the abominable condition has co-opted the reasoning faculty to produce self-justification rather than honest assessment.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The characteristic impairs cognition in two specific functions: (1) the evaluative function — the capacity to assess moral gravity (Eze 8:17 — VCG-05: abomination treated as light matter); (2) the memorial function — the capacity to recall covenantal history (Eze 16:22 — VCG-05: not remembering the days of youth). The characteristic does not enhance cognitive capacity in any direction; it specifically degrades the cognitive functions that would enable the person to recognise the gravity of their idolatrous attachment and recall the covenantal relationship it betrays.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The characteristic corrupts the cognitive faculty by redirecting its capacity for deliberate planning toward evil production. The deliberative-planning function is not impaired in its operational capacity — the nocturnal deviser (Mic 2:1 — VCG-02) and the counsel-giver (Eze 11:2 — VCG-02) are cognitively active and skilled. The characteristic bypasses the cognitive faculty's evaluative function: Psa 14:4 (vc=38229 — VCG-03): "no knowledge" — the cognitive evaluation of moral reality is absent. The planning capacity is enabled and deepened for scheming purposes; the moral-evaluative function is bypassed.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The characteristic impairs and bypasses the higher cognitive faculties. Jude 10 (vc=14355 — VCG-01): "blaspheme all that they do not understand, and they are destroyed by all that they, like unreasoning animals, understand instinctively" — the cognitive faculty of rational understanding is bypassed; instinctual understanding replaces rational comprehension. The characteristic reduces cognitive operation to the pre-rational instinctual level, below the level of the image-bearing rational speech-capacity. Rom 3:8 (VCG-02): the false attribution requires active cognitive distortion — the cognitive faculty is engaged but producing false outputs (misrepresenting another's position).

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster reveals systematic cognitive corruption across all six characteristics: co-optation (Char 5 — planning faculty deployed for evil), bypass (Char 6 — contempt substituting for understanding), inversion (Char 3 — false verdicts; Char 6 VCG-02/03 — misrepresentation), suppression (Chars 1, 2, 4 — moral blindness and gravity-assessment failure). The shared element: none of the six characteristics impairs the cognitive faculty's operational capacity (the person can still think, plan, and assess) but all six corrupt the faculty's orientation and output — from good-producing to evil-producing cognitive activity.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The characteristic deepens cognition through the categorical training effect noted at T3.2.1. The purity system is a comprehensive training curriculum for the perceptual and categorical cognitive faculty. However, it can also impair cognition in the NT sense: Peter's deep categorical knowledge, formed through lifelong observance, initially prevents him from perceiving what God is doing in the vision (Act 10:14/28, M10c-B-VCG-05). The formed cognitive framework becomes a resistance to new revelation. The characteristic thus shows cognition as both enabled (through systematic categorical formation) and potentially impaired (when the formed category becomes an inflexible inner resistance to divine revision).

**[CHAR-2]** E — Impairs cognition in the advanced state: the Tit 1:15 reference (VCG-03) — "to the defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure" — names a condition where the cognitive faculty cannot correctly categorise moral reality; the instrument of moral cognition is compromised. Mat 23:27 (VCG-04): the hypocrites' self-cognition is distorted — they appear to themselves as righteous while "within full of... uncleanness." The advanced moral-inner defilement-state thus produces cognitive distortion of self-assessment and moral categorisation.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The characteristic impairs cognition specifically in the domains of self-assessment (Jer 2:23 — self-deception) and categorical moral discernment (Eze 22:26 — failure to distinguish holy from common). These two cognitive failures are both symptoms of and contributors to the corporate defilement-state: when the community cannot correctly assess its own moral condition or the sacred/common distinction, the defilement can persist without self-corrective response.
**[CHAR-4]** S — Not evidenced within the 21-verse corpus. The characteristic suppresses specific faculties (will, speech/hearing) but does not explicitly address the cognitive faculty.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's cognitive impact varies: enabling/deepening in Characteristic 1, impairing in Characteristics 2 and 3, bypassing in Characteristic 4. Characteristic 1 deepens cognition through the categorical training effect of the purity system; the same categorical knowledge can resist new revelation (Act 10:14 — Peter's formed cognitive framework initially blocking divine instruction). Characteristic 2 impairs cognition in its advanced form — the defiled mind cannot correctly assess moral reality (Tit 1:15 reference). Characteristic 3 impairs cognitive self-assessment (Jer 2:23) and reveals that institutional cognitive failure enables the defilement's propagation (Eze 22:26 — when priests fail to teach the clean/unclean distinction, the community loses the cognitive equipment to resist defilement). Characteristic 4 bypasses the cognitive faculty entirely.

questions.question_text: Across the verses, what does the pattern of engagement and non-engagement with cognition indicate about the characteristic's nature?

findings.session_b_note:
The cognitive engagement pattern reveals that forgiveness operates on cognition primarily as a **liberator and terminator** rather than a builder:

- It terminates the cognitive holding of the debt-record (Jer 31:34 — "remember no more")
- It removes the cognitive barrier to direct knowing of God (Jer 31:34 — "they shall all know me")
- It requires accurate cognitive understanding as a precondition (Mar 2:7 — misunderstanding blocks reception)

Forgiveness does not primarily produce new cognitive content — it clears, releases, and opens cognitive space. The characteristic's relationship to cognition is **subtractive and liberating** rather than additive. This distinguishes it from characteristics whose primary function is to build cognitive capacity (wisdom, understanding).

findings.session_b_note:
Grace produces a particular cognitive form — reasoned assurance, not merely experienced certainty. Grace can be the ground of inner confidence even when experiential feeling is absent. This distinguishes grace's cognitive engagement from purely affective reception.

*Adds precision: grace operating cognitively independently of affect is a significant finding not previously stated in these terms.*

findings.session_b_note:
The pattern reveals that compassion is not a cognitively-initiated characteristic — it does not begin with a reasoned assessment of need that then produces a feeling. It begins in the body and the heart (gut-stirring, heart-recoiling) and then engages the cognitive faculty as a co-operating and moderating agent. This is constitutionally significant: compassion is not a conclusion of moral reasoning but an inner-being event that moral reasoning then shapes, directs, and — in judicial contexts — can override.

The metriopatheō evidence adds nuance: compassion can be cognitively shaped without being cognitively initiated. Understanding of the other's condition (shared weakness — Heb 5:2) produces a calibrated, appropriate compassion rather than a raw, undirected one. Cognition here is a forming agent, not an originating one. This distinction is analytically important for T5 (formation and development).

findings.session_b_note: The pattern reveals that contrition is grounded in cognitive truth-telling about oneself. It is not an irrational or sub-cognitive state — it arises from and is constituted by honest cognitive engagement with one's moral condition. This distinguishes it from generalised emotional distress (which may be non-cognitive) and aligns it with the conscience (T3.9), which is the faculty that provides the cognitive content that drives the contrite condition. The cognitive engagement of contrition has a specific object: not abstract knowledge but self-knowledge before God.

findings.session_b_note: The pattern confirms that fellowship is not primarily cognitive, but it engages cognition at the level of knowing-as-participation (Phili 3:10) and discernment-of-boundaries (2Cor 6:14). Cognition serves fellowship rather than constituting it: the mind discerns who to be in fellowship with, and knowing-Christ is the highest form of fellowship-entering cognition. But the deepest operations of fellowship (wounding, ontological participation) are not primarily cognitive in mode.

findings.session_b_note: The cognitive engagement reveals that goodness is not ethically naive or merely affective — it requires intellectual content. The wisdom literature's comparative evaluations demand a capacity for moral reasoning. The pairing of goodness with knowledge (Rom 15:14) suggests that genuine goodness has a cognitive substrate — the person who is good knows what is good and why. This is consistent with the Mic 6:8 revelatory frame ("He has told you what is good") — goodness is disclosed knowledge, not merely felt impulse. The pattern further reveals that goodness in its distorted form (calling evil good) specifically corrupts the cognitive faculty — which implies that genuine goodness and genuine cognition are structurally coherent. (OBS-067-OBS-012, OBS-067-OBS-027, OBS-067-OBS-025)

findings.session_b_note: The cognitive engagement pattern reveals that love is the programme's primary access-condition for relational knowledge. This is not the knowledge available through observation or reason alone — it is the knowledge that flows within the love-relationship: what the Father tells the Son, what the Son tells his friends (Joh 15:15). The pattern also reveals that love and knowledge are not rivals but partners: Hos 6:6 places them as co-equal priorities above ritual. The eschatological vision (Jer 31:34) confirms that love's fullness and knowledge's fullness coincide — in the final state, perfect love produces direct knowledge. The nature of love is therefore partly epistemic: it is not merely emotional but a structural condition for the deepest form of knowing.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-003: T3 reveals two structurally distinctive findings about compassion's faculty engagement. First, creativity is entirely silent (three S ratings) — the most informative absence in the tier: compassion re…
findings.finding_value: T3 reveals two structurally distinctive findings about compassion's faculty engagement. First, creativity is entirely silent (three S ratings) — the most informative absence in the tier: compassion responds, it does not originate or create. It is the most responsive of the faculties-engaging characteristics. Second, affect and moral action are structurally unified in compassion — not sequentially related but simultaneous. Affect is the mechanism of movement (splanchnizō is both the felt inner event and the cause of the action), not a precursor or accompaniment. This is unique among the characteristics reviewed: in most other registries, affect and volition are distinguishable stages; in compassion, the felt movement is already the morally motivated action beginning. A third distinctive finding: compassion converts moral knowledge into motivated action — it is the motivational ground of conscientiousness, not a product of it. The conscience faculty engagement reveals compassion as conscience-healing: it addresses the pitiable condition that conscience perceives as a moral claim, resolving the tension between moral knowledge and moral incapacity. The three relational modes (building/sustaining — chesed; restoring/repairing — splanchnizō; extending across difference — Good Samaritan) are a new finding not in the instruction typology.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-003: T3 produces four structurally significant findings about grace's faculty engagement. First, grace is agency-constituting rather than agency-replacing: 1Cor 15:10 holds in explicit paradox — "I worked …
findings.finding_value: T3 produces four structurally significant findings about grace's faculty engagement. First, grace is agency-constituting rather than agency-replacing: 1Cor 15:10 holds in explicit paradox — "I worked harder than any of them, though it was not I but the grace of God that is with me." Agency is not displaced but constituted by grace. This relationship holds in paradox that the T3.6 prompt options (enable/deepen/bypass/impair) cannot accommodate — a prompt design limitation noted for catalogue revision. Second, grace produces moral clarity (T3.8 — sharpens moral evaluation rather than bypassing it): the person who recognises grace has made a precise moral evaluation (they know they received what they did not deserve). Third, grace and conscience are mutually necessary: grace is the condition within which conscience can operate fully without destroying the person; conscience without grace produces condemnation; grace without conscience produces presumption (T3.9). Fourth, grace is the primary relational faculty developer in the registry's evidence — it reaches every relational register (vertical access, horizontal forgiving, speech-grace) and enables each one. Creativity (T3.5) is the one genuinely silent faculty — not an impairment but a non-engagement: grace receives and constitutes, it does not create.

findings.session_b_note: The pattern reveals that cognition is not merely a secondary consequence of covenant but one of its primary targets and products. The new covenant's stated aim is a cognitive one — "they shall all know me." This means that covenant is oriented toward producing a transformed cognitive relationship with God as its telos. The pattern also reveals a fundamental asymmetry between old and new covenant cognitive effects: the old covenant engages cognition but can produce hardening and veil; the new covenant engages cognition and produces knowing by God's own interior action. Cognition, in covenant terms, is not human achievement (study, comprehension) but covenant gift — it is what the covenant produces in the person, not what the person brings to the covenant. This is a structurally important finding: the cognitive dimension of covenant runs from God's action to human knowing, not from human knowing to covenant engagement.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-034-003: T3 as a whole reveals that covenant comprehensively engages the inner faculties but with a specific structural bias: the faculties it most deeply and richly engages are those oriented toward the Other…
findings.finding_value: T3 as a whole reveals that covenant comprehensively engages the inner faculties but with a specific structural bias: the faculties it most deeply and richly engages are those oriented toward the Other (relational capacity, memory, cognition as knowing-God, moral evaluation, conscientiousness) rather than those oriented inward (creativity, which is notably absent). This faculty-engagement pattern is coherent with covenant's relational-disposition primary classification — covenant is constitutively Other-oriented and therefore engages the Other-oriented faculties most richly. The deepest T3 finding is the developmental one: the old covenant calls for volition from outside (demands obedience); the new covenant transforms volition from inside (liberates and enables faithfulness through Spirit). This volitional trajectory is confirmed across T3.6 (volition) and T3.7 (agency) and is the faculty-level expression of the same transformation that T2 identified at the constitutional-movement level and T5 identifies at the mechanism level. All three tiers point to the same inner-being reality from different analytical vantage points.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-014: T2 locates covenant in the constitutional organs (heart, mind, soul, mouth, body). T3 reveals which inner faculties operate within and through those locations. The T2 × T3 synthesis: the constitutiona…
findings.finding_value: T2 locates covenant in the constitutional organs (heart, mind, soul, mouth, body). T3 reveals which inner faculties operate within and through those locations. The T2 × T3 synthesis: the constitutional location (T2) and the faculty operation (T3) are not separate realities but different analytical views of the same inner-being reality. The heart (T2) is where the integrating functions of willing, knowing, moral evaluation, and affect operate (T3.6 volition, T3.2 cognition, T3.8 moral evaluation, T3.4 affect). The mind (T2) is where cognition (T3.2) and memory (T3.3) operate. The soul-totality (T2) corresponds to the conscientiousness and relational capacity (T3.10, T3.11) that engage the whole person. The constitutional location and the faculty operation are two descriptions of the same inner reality: location is where the faculty is housed; faculty is what the location does. The new covenant writes on the heart/mind (T2) and thereby transforms cognition toward knowing God (T3.2) — the constitutional location is the mechanism for the faculty transformation.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-020: T3 identifies the new covenant's faculty-level effect as the transformation of volition (from called-for to liberated — Q&A-085) and the production of covenantal knowing (Q&A-073). T5 identifies the d…
findings.finding_value: T3 identifies the new covenant's faculty-level effect as the transformation of volition (from called-for to liberated — Q&A-085) and the production of covenantal knowing (Q&A-073). T5 identifies the developmental sequence through which this transformation occurs (failure → inscription → belonging → knowing — Q&A-128) and the mechanism change (letter to Spirit — Q&A-131). The T3 × T5 synthesis: the faculty transformations identified in T3 (volition liberated, cognition/knowing produced) are the outcome of the developmental sequence and mechanism identified in T5. The sequence "inscription → belonging → knowing" (T5) describes how the specific faculty transformations of T3 are produced. The mechanism shift from letter to Spirit (T5) is the developmental mechanism that produces the volitional liberation (T3.6) and cognitive knowing (T3.2) that the new covenant delivers. T5 is the developmental story; T3 is the faculty-level outcome of that story.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-022: T3 shows that memory is one of the most structurally prominent inner faculties in covenant — divine memory of covenant is the guarantee of its continuing operation; human memory is the activating cond…
findings.finding_value: T3 shows that memory is one of the most structurally prominent inner faculties in covenant — divine memory of covenant is the guarantee of its continuing operation; human memory is the activating condition for faithfulness (Q&A-074, Q&A-076). T7 shows that the primary verse evidence spans four literary forms (legal-narrative, prophetic oracle, epistle-argument, liturgical — Q&A-181), all of which are forms that require and shape memory. The T3 × T7 synthesis: the memory-faculty centrality (T3) and the literary form analysis (T7) converge on the same insight: covenant is constitutively a narrative and liturgical reality — it is held active through storytelling, declaration, and ritual re-enactment. The Eucharistic "do this in remembrance of me" (Q&A-075) is the liturgical instantiation of memory's role in covenant (T3), and it is carried by the liturgical literary form (T7). Memory and liturgy are co-constituting — covenant is kept alive through the practice of remembering performed in narrative and liturgical forms.
