findings.session_b_note:
Yes — affect is the most directly and extensively evidenced faculty in the compassion data. The characteristic is constitutively affective: its primary vocabulary names the felt quality of the inner experience.

**Splanchnizō as the paradigmatic affective term:** The gut-stirring named by splanchnizō is an affective event — something felt, not merely cognised or willed. The abdominal location of the term in ancient anthropology (the entrails as the seat of the deepest emotions) confirms that this is affect at its most visceral and pre-reflective.

**Ni.chum as affective warmth:** Hos 11:8 — "my compassion grows warm and tender" — names the felt quality of compassion in temperature terms. Warmth is an affective quality: it names how the inner experience of compassion feels, not merely what it does or produces.

**Ra.cha.mim (plural) as accumulated affective depth:** The plural form of ra.cham (ra.cha.mim — compassions/mercies) names the affective quality as multiple, accumulated, and deep. Lam 3:22 — "his mercies never come to an end" — uses the plural to convey that this is not a single felt impulse but an inexhaustible reservoir of affective compassion.

**The maternal imagery:** The womb vocabulary carries deep affective resonance — the bond between mother and carried child is among the most affectively charged relationships in human experience. When Scripture uses this to describe divine compassion, it is reaching for the deepest available affective language.

findings.session_b_note:
Yes — contrition is a deeply affective phenomenon. The registry's primary dimension is Affective/Emotional (legacy label) and two of its three modes are affective:

- **Penitential-relational mode**: the "interior grief" of the registry description is an affective state — grief, sorrow, anguish arising from moral self-recognition. Psa 38:8 — "I groan because of the tumult of my heart" — is explicitly affective: groaning, inner tumult.
- **Experiential-anguish mode**: anguish (Psa 143:3), corporate desolation (Psa 44:19), and terror/panic (Jer 46:5) are all affective states.

The substitutionary mode (Isa 53:5) carries affective content implicitly — the Servant's crushing is a suffering event — though the verse focuses on outcomes (peace, healing) rather than the Servant's inner affective experience.

findings.session_b_note:
Yes. The affective dimension is engaged primarily through the fellowship-products rather than as the primary mode of fellowship's operation.

**Hope:** Ecc 9:4 — *he who is joined with all the living has hope* — fellowship produces hope as an affective forward-orientation. Being in community is the affective ground of hope.

**Comfort:** The co-occurrence with R192 (comfort, 3 shared verses) suggests that fellowship and comfort are closely adjacent. Comfort is an affective experience produced by or co-present with fellowship.

**Sorrow:** The co-occurrence with R151 (sorrow, 3 shared verses) and the shared anchor Isa 53:5 (SP-062-002) suggest that fellowship through suffering engages sorrow — the fellowship of Christ's sufferings (Phili 3:10) is not emotionally neutral.

**Isolation-fear:** Ecc 4:10 — *woe to him who is alone when he falls* — the absence of fellowship produces a condition of vulnerability and implied inner distress. Fellowship's absence has affective consequence.

The inner well-being group (884-009) is predominantly affective: tov-lev (glad of heart, Est 5:9) and the associated inner state of gladness, prospering, and well-being are emotional-experiential states. The experiential group (884-003) as a whole is oriented toward inner satisfaction and well-being — an affective register of goodness. (OBS-067-OBS-029, OBS-067-OBS-035, OBS-067-OBS-041)

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-067-003: T3 reveals that goodness is the most comprehensively faculty-engaging characteristic in the programme's current analytical record. Every faculty except creativity (T3.5 — silence confirmed) shows subs…
findings.finding_value: T3 reveals that goodness is the most comprehensively faculty-engaging characteristic in the programme's current analytical record. Every faculty except creativity (T3.5 — silence confirmed) shows substantive engagement: perception (tasting and seeing goodness), cognition (moral evaluation and ranking), memory (covenantal knowing and moral reckoning), affect (stable rooted gladness vs fragile surface gladness), volition (reconstituted toward the good), agency (active expression required and enabled), moral evaluation (goodness as the normative anchor of the evaluative faculty), conscience (goodness calibrates the conscience's standard), conscientiousness (integration of all faculties into sustained moral expression), and relational capacity (dual-directional overflow). The tier as a whole reveals that goodness is not a specialist characteristic — it is an integrating one. The person who possesses genuine goodness has every faculty engaged and aligned. This comprehensive faculty-engagement is what distinguishes genuine goodness from its surface forms: surface goodness (the Haman problem) engages affect without engaging conscience or volitional alignment; genuine goodness integrates all.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-067-020: T3 identified three faculty engagements that are particularly significant for transformation: memory (Eze 36:31 — memory activates moral recognition, Q&A-072), affect (stable vs fragile gladness diagn…
findings.finding_value: T3 identified three faculty engagements that are particularly significant for transformation: memory (Eze 36:31 — memory activates moral recognition, Q&A-072), affect (stable vs fragile gladness diagnostic, Q&A-077), and moral evaluation (conscience calibration, Q&A-089-090). T5's three transformation mechanisms (encounter, Spirit-infusion, recognition-confrontation — Q&A-129) map onto these faculty engagements. The recognition-confrontation mechanism (Eze 36:31 / Rom 2:4) operates specifically through the memory faculty (recall of deeds) and the conscience-moral evaluation faculty (recognition as not-good and self-loathing). The encounter mechanism operates through the perceptive faculty (tasting — Q&A-066) and the affective faculty (trust, gladness — Q&A-075). The Spirit-infusion mechanism produces faculty-level transformation: it reconstitutes the volitional faculty (Q&A-082), enables agency (Q&A-085), and generates stable affect (Q&A-076). T5's mechanisms are faculty-specific operations — each mechanism transforms the person by engaging specific faculties in specific ways. This is the most analytically precise inter-tier connection so far.

findings.session_b_note: Yes. Psa 27:13 (OBS-103-080): 'I believe that I shall look upon the goodness of the Lord in the land of the living' — the psalmist's forward vision of God's love/goodness sustains the present inner life. The love-vocabulary consistently generates forward orientation (OBS-103-006, Q&A-006 — eschatological trajectory of love). Jer 31:3 (OBS-103-093): 'I have loved you with an everlasting love' — the everlasting qualifier generates an imagined future of permanent love. Song 2:16 (OBS-103-061): 'my beloved is mine' — the possession formula is also anticipatory: the belovedness extends into the imagined future. Imagination engages as love's visionary faculty — projecting the love-relationship into the future and sustaining the present through that projection.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-103-003: Love engages all eleven inner faculties, but five show the richest engagement: (1) Identity and self-understanding — love is the primary faculty through which the person knows who they are: being-love…
findings.finding_value: Love engages all eleven inner faculties, but five show the richest engagement: (1) Identity and self-understanding — love is the primary faculty through which the person knows who they are: being-loved (agapētos) constitutes identity from the outside; what-one-loves constitutes identity from the inside. The person is doubly defined by love. (2) Relational capacity — love is the faculty's active content: it builds (Joh 13:34), sustains (Lam 3:22), and restores (Luk 15:20) relational capacity. (3) Memory — love's sustaining faculty: love without memory cannot maintain itself through absence (Jer 31:20 — 'I do remember him still'). (4) Moral sensitivity — love calibrates what the inner person registers as morally significant; the love-of-God requirement generates the hate-evil requirement (Psa 97:10). (5) Attention — love determines what the person perceives as worth attending to (Phili 4:8 — think on what is lovely). The weaker engagements: creativity (indirect, evidenced through Song-form) and conscience (inferred, not directly named). Overall: love is the faculty-most-engaged characteristic in the programme, operating through perception, reason, memory, imagination, desire, emotion, moral sensitivity, conscience (indirectly), identity, and relational capacity simultaneously.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-013: Formation in T5 operates through the same faculties identified in T3, producing their development. Memory is formed through the covenantal story — Israel's memory of God's love (Jer 2:2 — 'I remember …
findings.finding_value: Formation in T5 operates through the same faculties identified in T3, producing their development. Memory is formed through the covenantal story — Israel's memory of God's love (Jer 2:2 — 'I remember the devotion of your youth') is the ground for love's formation in both directions; formation requires knowing the love-history. Imagination is formed through eschatological vision: the forward-projection of love's fullness (Psa 27:13, Jer 31:34) orients present formation toward its goal. Identity formation is the T3.10/T5 overlap: being-named-beloved (Mat 3:17, Rom 1:7) is the formation's constitutive moment — identity received through love is the ground from which love-acts are exercised. The relational capacity faculty (T3.11) is the faculty that formation produces: the formation process (Spirit infusion, obedience-purification, training) produces a person with increasing relational capacity for love's three directional axes. The community's role in formation (Q&A-097) corresponds to the relational capacity faculty's communal engagement: the faculty cannot develop in isolation because love cannot exist without a beloved.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-111-003: Reading T3 as a whole reveals mercy as a faculty-activating characteristic — it does not primarily engage one or two faculties but activates the inner-being faculty system comprehensively. The pattern…
findings.finding_value: Reading T3 as a whole reveals mercy as a faculty-activating characteristic — it does not primarily engage one or two faculties but activates the inner-being faculty system comprehensively. The pattern: mercy enables perception (face-access), opens cognition in both directions (upward to divine knowledge; downward to self-knowledge), creates an asymmetric memory structure (divine forgetting / human remembering), engages affect as its native register, expands volition (received mercy increases mercy-capacity), demands agency, reframes moral evaluation (mercy as higher-order moral evaluation), presupposes and deepens conscience, enables conscientiousness, and constitutes relational capacity. The single faculty not evidenced is creativity (T3.5.2 — S status). Reading T3 together: mercy is characterised by faculty-comprehensiveness; its absence (mercilessness in Rom 1:31) appears alongside affective incapacity (*astorgos*) and other faculty-failures — confirming that mercy's presence is correlated with full faculty activation and its absence with faculty contraction.

The affective dimension is inseparable from contrition — it is not a purely cognitive or volitional state. OBS-030-001, OBS-030-038, OBS-030-055.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-030-003: Reading T3 as a whole reveals that contrition engages virtually every inner faculty — with one exception (creativity, T3.5 — data silent). The pattern across the engaged faculties is consistent: contr…
findings.finding_value: Reading T3 as a whole reveals that contrition engages virtually every inner faculty — with one exception (creativity, T3.5 — data silent). The pattern across the engaged faculties is consistent: contrition deepens and opens rather than impairs or bypasses. It deepens perception (opens to divine address), deepens cognition (enables accurate self-knowledge), deepens affect (makes grief and longing both fuller), redirects volition (from self-assertion to God-direction), converts agency (from self-directed to God-seeking), deepens moral evaluation (requires and enables accurate self-assessment), deepens conscience (allows conscience's verdict to reach the spirit/heart), deepens conscientiousness (grounds it in inner reality rather than performance), and enables relational capacity (specifically for divine nearness). The single thread running through all faculty engagements is: contrition removes self-protective barriers — it is the inner-being event in which every protective reflex is dissolved, leaving the person fully exposed and open. This is why it enables rather than impairs every faculty: openness is the condition in which all faculties function most truthfully.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-030-014: The constitutional tier (T2) establishes that contrition's primary loci are spirit and heart; the faculty tier (T3) shows that the faculties most engaged by contrition are precisely those associated w…
findings.finding_value: The constitutional tier (T2) establishes that contrition's primary loci are spirit and heart; the faculty tier (T3) shows that the faculties most engaged by contrition are precisely those associated with these loci. The spirit-level location (T2) corresponds to the deepest faculty engagements: conscience (at the spirit-heart interface), moral evaluation (heart-based), and perception of divine address (spirit-receptive). The heart-level location (T2) corresponds to the affective and volitional faculty engagements. Together T2 and T3 reveal that contrition's constitutional depth (reaching spirit and heart as primary loci) determines the depth of its faculty engagement: because it reaches the innermost constitutional levels, it engages the innermost faculties most profoundly.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-062-003: Reading T3 as a whole reveals that every faculty engagement with fellowship runs in both directions — right fellowship deepens and enables; wrong fellowship degrades and constrains. Perception, cognit…
findings.finding_value: Reading T3 as a whole reveals that every faculty engagement with fellowship runs in both directions — right fellowship deepens and enables; wrong fellowship degrades and constrains. Perception, cognition, moral evaluation, conscience, conscientiousness, and relational capacity are all deepened by rightly directed fellowship and progressively impaired by wrongly directed fellowship. The single exception is creativity (T3.5 — data silent). The pattern is systematic: fellowship is not merely a relational characteristic but a faculty-shaping characteristic — it progressively shapes every inner faculty in conformity with its object. This makes the choice of fellowship objects one of the most consequential inner-being decisions a person makes: the consequences extend through every faculty across time.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-064-003: T3 reveals forgiveness as uniquely faculty-comprehensive — it engages more named faculties with greater specificity than any other characteristic reviewed in this revision series. Memory is explicitly…
findings.finding_value: T3 reveals forgiveness as uniquely faculty-comprehensive — it engages more named faculties with greater specificity than any other characteristic reviewed in this revision series. Memory is explicitly named (Jer 31:34 — divine memory as the content of forgiveness) and distinctively: forgiveness transforms memory in both directions — God's memory of sin is set aside permanently; the human forgiver releases the active use of memory against the offender. Affect is bidirectionally engaged: as prerequisite (somatic compassion, Mat 18:27) and as product (love, Luk 7:47; reverence, Psa 130:4). Conscience is addressed and purified by forgiveness (Heb 9:14). Volition is constitutive (the heart-level release is chosen). Cognition is enabled (Jer 31:34 — forgiveness → knowing God). The single silence is creativity (T3.5). T3's synthesis: forgiveness is the most faculty-comprehensive characteristic in the current review set — it reaches every major faculty with specific evidenced content, most strikingly in the memory domain.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-009: T1's four modes explain T3's faculty engagement pattern. The covenantal-objective mode (no inner-being prerequisite) corresponds to T3's absence of any faculty requirement for that mode. The divine re…
findings.finding_value: T1's four modes explain T3's faculty engagement pattern. The covenantal-objective mode (no inner-being prerequisite) corresponds to T3's absence of any faculty requirement for that mode. The divine relational-personal mode (faith, repentance, confession as access-postures) engages volition, conscience, and cognition. The human horizontal mode ("from your heart") requires volition, conscience, and moral evaluation. The intercessory mode requires the dependence-posture that engages cognition (accurate assessment of the grounds of the plea — God's character, not human merit) and volition. T1's definition of forgiveness as transitional (not terminal) is confirmed by T3's finding that every faculty engaged by forgiveness is deepened toward further engagement — not closed by the act but opened by it.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-014: T2's constitutional locations map onto T3's faculty engagements. The heart-locus (T2.3 — Mat 18:35) corresponds to T3's volition, moral evaluation, and conscience faculties — all heart-level. The cogn…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional locations map onto T3's faculty engagements. The heart-locus (T2.3 — Mat 18:35) corresponds to T3's volition, moral evaluation, and conscience faculties — all heart-level. The cognition-locus (T2.4 — Jer 31:34) corresponds to T3's cognition and memory faculty engagements. The somatic-compassion locus (T2.5 — splagchnizomai) corresponds to T3's affect faculty at its somatic depth. The constitutional movement (T2.10 — guilt-bearing → forgiveness → love) is the sequence in which T3's faculties are engaged: conscience identifies the guilt → volition releases the claim → affect produces the love-response. Constitutional location determines faculty engagement sequence.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-019: T3's faculty engagements all point in the same relational directions that T4 identifies as primary. Conscience (T3.9) is engaged in both the seeking-forgiveness direction (human-to-God: confession as …
findings.finding_value: T3's faculty engagements all point in the same relational directions that T4 identifies as primary. Conscience (T3.9) is engaged in both the seeking-forgiveness direction (human-to-God: confession as conscience's public verdict) and the giving direction (human horizontal: the conscience that recognises the offence to be released). Memory (T3.3) is engaged in the God-to-human direction (divine "remember no more" — Jer 31:34) and the human-giving direction (releasing the memory's active use against the offender). Volition (T3.6) drives the giving direction (heart-level release is chosen). The vertical-horizontal interdependence (T4 structural claim) is the relational expression of T3's conscience-and-volition faculty account: the person whose conscience has accurately received the magnitude of divine forgiveness has the volitional capacity to extend horizontal forgiveness.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-020: T3's faculty deepenings (cognition enabled — Jer 31:34; love produced — Luk 7:47; conscience purified — Heb 9:14; volition redirected) are T5's formation products described at the faculty level. The f…
findings.finding_value: T3's faculty deepenings (cognition enabled — Jer 31:34; love produced — Luk 7:47; conscience purified — Heb 9:14; volition redirected) are T5's formation products described at the faculty level. The formation sequence (T5) is the longitudinal account of which T3's faculty engagements are the synchronic snapshots. The commanded forgiveness as sanctification discipline (T5.5 — Eph 4:32) is the formation vehicle through which the volitional faculty (T3.6) is habituated and the moral evaluation faculty (T3.8) is deepened. T3 and T5 together reveal the full formation arc: T3 shows what happens to each faculty in the moment of forgiveness; T5 shows what sustained habitual forgiveness does to the person over time.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-021: T3's memory faculty finding (Jer 31:34 — divine "remember no more") explains the R160 thought/knowledge co-occurrence at that verse: the divine cognitive act of non-remembering and the human cognitive…
findings.finding_value: T3's memory faculty finding (Jer 31:34 — divine "remember no more") explains the R160 thought/knowledge co-occurrence at that verse: the divine cognitive act of non-remembering and the human cognitive outcome of knowing God meet in the same verse because they are structurally connected — the guilt-barrier's removal (forgiveness) enables the cognitive-relational access (knowing God). T3's affect-faculty finding (love produced — Luk 7:47) explains the R103 love co-occurrence (8 shared verses) — love is the affective downstream product of forgiveness. T3's conscience faculty finding confirms the R073 guilt structural partnership — guilt is what conscience identifies as the prior condition that forgiveness addresses. Faculty engagements (T3) and structural co-occurrences (T6) are mutually explanatory.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-022: T7's literary forms explain why T3 finds different faculty engagements in different evidential contexts. The cultic-legal corpus (Lev 4:20) — covenantal-objective mode — requires no named faculty enga…
findings.finding_value: T7's literary forms explain why T3 finds different faculty engagements in different evidential contexts. The cultic-legal corpus (Lev 4:20) — covenantal-objective mode — requires no named faculty engagement (T3 finds no faculty requirement for this mode). The prophetic corpus (Jer 31:34) primarily engages cognition and memory (T3.2, T3.3). The Synoptic narrative corpus (Luk 7:47, Mat 18:27, Mat 18:35) engages affect, volition, and conscience most richly. The apostolic letter corpus (Eph 1:7, Eph 4:32) grounds the formation dimension (T3.10 conscientiousness, T5.5 sanctification). Each literary form carries specific faculty registers — T7's literary analysis explains T3's faculty engagement distribution.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-003: T3 reveals two structurally distinctive findings about compassion's faculty engagement. First, creativity is entirely silent (three S ratings) — the most informative absence in the tier: compassion re…
findings.finding_value: T3 reveals two structurally distinctive findings about compassion's faculty engagement. First, creativity is entirely silent (three S ratings) — the most informative absence in the tier: compassion responds, it does not originate or create. It is the most responsive of the faculties-engaging characteristics. Second, affect and moral action are structurally unified in compassion — not sequentially related but simultaneous. Affect is the mechanism of movement (splanchnizō is both the felt inner event and the cause of the action), not a precursor or accompaniment. This is unique among the characteristics reviewed: in most other registries, affect and volition are distinguishable stages; in compassion, the felt movement is already the morally motivated action beginning. A third distinctive finding: compassion converts moral knowledge into motivated action — it is the motivational ground of conscientiousness, not a product of it. The conscience faculty engagement reveals compassion as conscience-healing: it addresses the pitiable condition that conscience perceives as a moral claim, resolving the tension between moral knowledge and moral incapacity. The three relational modes (building/sustaining — chesed; restoring/repairing — splanchnizō; extending across difference — Good Samaritan) are a new finding not in the instruction typology.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-009: T1's four kinds explain T3's most distinctive finding: that affect and moral action are structurally unified rather than sequential. In T1 terms, compassion-as-inner-event (splanchnizō) and compassion…
findings.finding_value: T1's four kinds explain T3's most distinctive finding: that affect and moral action are structurally unified rather than sequential. In T1 terms, compassion-as-inner-event (splanchnizō) and compassion-as-externalised-act are not two separate kinds but a continuous movement — the felt-movement is the beginning of the act. T3 confirms this: affect is the mechanism of movement, not its precursor. T1's finding that compassion converts moral knowledge into motivated action (the unique position as motivational ground of conscientiousness) maps onto T3.10's finding of the same: the definitional claim (T1) that compassion is constitutively outward-facing explains T3's finding that it is the driving faculty between moral knowledge and moral action.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-014: T2's four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) maps directly onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The somatic-arousal s…
findings.finding_value: T2's four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) maps directly onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The somatic-arousal stage (T2.6 — gut stirring, splanchnizō) corresponds to T3.1's perceptive-trigger stage (sight activates the somatic response) and T3.4's affect stage (the stirring is the affective movement). The soul-engagement stage (T2.2 — chesed as soul-character) corresponds to T3.8 moral evaluation (the soul assesses the need) and T3.9 conscience (the conscience activates the response). The volitional-engagement stage (T2.3 — heart-locus as deliberative site) corresponds to T3.6 volition (the will directs the action). The outward-action stage corresponds to T3.7 agency. T2 and T3 describe the same movement sequence from two perspectives: T2 maps the constitutional levels; T3 maps the faculties active at each level.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-019: T3's perceptive-trigger finding (compassion is activated by sight — splanchnizō is perceptively dependent) and T4's scope-by-need finding (scope is determined by perceived need, not covenantal standin…
findings.finding_value: T3's perceptive-trigger finding (compassion is activated by sight — splanchnizō is perceptively dependent) and T4's scope-by-need finding (scope is determined by perceived need, not covenantal standing) are the same finding from two analytical perspectives. T3 names the faculty (perception) and its function (triggering compassion by seeing the pitiable condition); T4 names the relational consequence (scope defined by what is seen). The cross-boundary extension in T4 (Nineveh, Samaritan/Jew) is the relational expression of T3's merit-independence: compassion is perceptively dependent (it must see the need) but merit-independent (it does not assess the moral standing of the one seen). The three relational modes in T3.11 (building/sustaining, restoring/repairing, extending across difference) correspond precisely to T4's chesed/splanchnizō/cross-boundary structure.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-020: T3's affect-moral-action unity (affect is the mechanism, not the precursor) and T5's formation finding (compassion is simultaneously character target and motivational ground) are structurally connecte…
findings.finding_value: T3's affect-moral-action unity (affect is the mechanism, not the precursor) and T5's formation finding (compassion is simultaneously character target and motivational ground) are structurally connected. T5 names compassion as the motivational ground that makes the sanctification arc survivable through failure and return — but T3 has already established that affect is the mechanism of this motivational ground: the character formation that T5 describes is accomplished through the affective mechanism that T3 identifies. The person who is formed into compassionate character (T5) is the person whose affective faculty has been trained to respond immediately and morally to perceived suffering (T3). T3's finding that affect and moral action are unified is T5's mechanism of formation: the person becoming compassionate is the person in whom the affective-moral unity is deepening and stabilising.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-021: T3's finding that compassion is the motivational ground of conscientiousness explains the co-occurrence pattern in T6. Conscience (T3.9) and moral evaluation (T3.8) are the faculties that register the…
findings.finding_value: T3's finding that compassion is the motivational ground of conscientiousness explains the co-occurrence pattern in T6. Conscience (T3.9) and moral evaluation (T3.8) are the faculties that register the pitiable need as a moral claim; compassion is the affective-motivational response that converts that moral knowledge into action. The co-occurrence of will (R173 — 25 verses) and surrender (R156 — 21 verses) in T6 is the co-occurrence expression of T3's volitional faculty finding: compassion engages and redirects the will toward the suffering other. The sequential relationship confirmed in T6 (compassion → mercy — constitutionally causal) is the relational expression of T3's finding that compassion converts moral knowledge into motivated action: the mercy-act is the action that compassion's motivation produces.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-022: T3's perceptive-trigger and affect-mechanism findings are grounded in T7's primary anchor evidence. The Synoptic pattern of splanchnizō — always triggered by sight, always preceding action — is the te…
findings.finding_value: T3's perceptive-trigger and affect-mechanism findings are grounded in T7's primary anchor evidence. The Synoptic pattern of splanchnizō — always triggered by sight, always preceding action — is the textual ground for T3.1's finding (compassion is perceptively dependent) and T3.4's finding (affect is the mechanism of movement). T7's argument structure finding (Matt 9:36 — compassion as the theological engine of missional response) is the evangelist's literary expression of T3.10's analytical claim (compassion converts moral knowledge into motivated action). T7's framework divergences (human science frameworks failing at sovereignty, cross-boundary extension, and purposive suffering) correspond to the three areas where T3's faculty analysis finds its most distinctive results: the sovereign freedom of divine compassion exceeds the natural automaticity of empathic response; the cross-boundary extension exceeds natural empathic scope; the purposive suffering (T5.4/T5.5) requires the teleological frame that T7.3 identifies.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-003: T3 produces four structurally significant findings about grace's faculty engagement. First, grace is agency-constituting rather than agency-replacing: 1Cor 15:10 holds in explicit paradox — "I worked …
findings.finding_value: T3 produces four structurally significant findings about grace's faculty engagement. First, grace is agency-constituting rather than agency-replacing: 1Cor 15:10 holds in explicit paradox — "I worked harder than any of them, though it was not I but the grace of God that is with me." Agency is not displaced but constituted by grace. This relationship holds in paradox that the T3.6 prompt options (enable/deepen/bypass/impair) cannot accommodate — a prompt design limitation noted for catalogue revision. Second, grace produces moral clarity (T3.8 — sharpens moral evaluation rather than bypassing it): the person who recognises grace has made a precise moral evaluation (they know they received what they did not deserve). Third, grace and conscience are mutually necessary: grace is the condition within which conscience can operate fully without destroying the person; conscience without grace produces condemnation; grace without conscience produces presumption (T3.9). Fourth, grace is the primary relational faculty developer in the registry's evidence — it reaches every relational register (vertical access, horizontal forgiving, speech-grace) and enables each one. Creativity (T3.5) is the one genuinely silent faculty — not an impairment but a non-engagement: grace receives and constitutes, it does not create.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-009: T1's immediate response pattern (fear → mourning → prostration as the creaturely recognition response) is the affective-volitional expression of T3's faculty engagement at the moment grace arrives. T3…
findings.finding_value: T1's immediate response pattern (fear → mourning → prostration as the creaturely recognition response) is the affective-volitional expression of T3's faculty engagement at the moment grace arrives. T3.4 (affect is the first named faculty engaged by grace) and T3.6 (the agency-constituting paradox of 1Cor 15:10) together explain why T1.5 finds the creaturely recognition response before positive states settle: grace first produces the affective recognition (fear, mourning) before constituting the agency through which the person responds (prostration as the body enacting the inner posture that grace has produced). T1's finding that grace requires creaturely recognition to complete its operation (T1.7) is T3.1's finding at the faculty level: grace requires and enables perception simultaneously.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-014: T2's constitutional movement (spirit reception → soul standing → capacity → character expression) maps onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The spirit-reception stage (T2.1) corresponds to T3.1 (per…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional movement (spirit reception → soul standing → capacity → character expression) maps onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The spirit-reception stage (T2.1) corresponds to T3.1 (perception — grace enabling the inner sight and hearing that receives it). The soul-standing stage (T2.2) corresponds to T3.9 (conscience — grace as the condition within which conscience can operate without destruction) and T3.8 (moral evaluation — the standing produces the clarity of moral self-assessment). The capacity-gifting stage (T2.1 — spirit level) corresponds to T3.7 (agency — capacity given constitutes agency for the task). The character-expression stage (T2.7 — outward through body-soul) corresponds to T3.10 (conscientiousness — the integrated moral-action expression of received grace-character). T2 maps the constitutional space; T3 maps the faculties active at each spatial level; the two tiers describe the same movement from orthogonal perspectives.

T5's formation arc (sustained work producing character-quality) is the longitudinal development of T3.9's finding (conscience operating fully within grace) into T3.10's finding (conscientiousness as the integrated moral character that grace constitutes over time). findings.finding_value: T3's faculty findings are grounded in and confirmed by T7's primary anchor evidence. This is the methodological divergence T7.3 identifies and T3.6 establishes as the operative finding.

findings.session_b_note: Yes — and substantively. The evidence shows kindness engaging the affective faculty in multiple directions. (a) Receiving divine chesed produces affective states: Psa 63:3 — "your steadfast love is better than life; my lips will praise you" — the receipt of divine chesed generates an affective orientation of praise and joy [XREG: H2617A, OBS-099-084]. Psa 23:4 — "I will fear no evil, for you are with me" — the displacement of fear by security is an affective change produced by the experience of divine kindness-as-presence [OBS-099-066]. (b) Kindness involves an affective orientation in the giver: Eph 4:32 — "tenderhearted" (eusplanchnoi — literally "good-bowelled," an affective visceral term) is placed immediately alongside kindness, suggesting that genuine kindness carries an affective warmth component — it does not operate as cold duty [OBS-099-077]. (c) The absence of kindness produces grief: Gen 44:29 — Jacob's anticipatory grief at losing Benjamin — the possibility of losing the object of kindness generates profound affective distress [OBS-099-062]. The affective faculty is engaged at all three interfaces: receiving kindness (produces joy/security), giving kindness (accompanied by tenderheartedness), and threatened absence of kindness (produces grief/distress).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-060-003: T3 as a whole reveals that this characteristic engages virtually every inner faculty in the programme's 11-faculty model — the only consistent gap is creativity (T3.5, S across three prompts). The pat…
findings.finding_value: T3 as a whole reveals that this characteristic engages virtually every inner faculty in the programme's 11-faculty model — the only consistent gap is creativity (T3.5, S across three prompts). The pattern of engagement is not uniform: perception is engaged as precondition (God hears before giving); cognition is constituted (wisdom is given, not generated); memory is deepened (the narrative-temporal dimension of covenantal giving); affect is the source of giving (compassion, anger) and the target of transformation (mourning→gladness); volition is called forth and elevated (genuine giving cannot be coerced); agency is the bridge between disposition and act; moral evaluation both produces and is produced by the characteristic; conscience is engaged indirectly through Spirit-forming and prophetic warning; conscientiousness at the human apex is the full integration of all three (moral awareness, will, act). Relational capacity is intrinsic — every mode is two-party. What T3 reveals as a whole: faithfulness-as-giving is not a faculty-specific characteristic but a whole-person characteristic — it recruits and integrates all active faculties into a unified inner-being act. The creativity silence is the only dimension where the data cannot confirm engagement.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-007: The constitutional locations (T2 — spirit, heart, soul, hidden inner parts, body) and the inner faculties (T3 — perception, cognition, memory, affect, volition, agency, moral evaluation, relational ca…
findings.finding_value: The constitutional locations (T2 — spirit, heart, soul, hidden inner parts, body) and the inner faculties (T3 — perception, cognition, memory, affect, volition, agency, moral evaluation, relational capacity) are not independent — they occupy the same inner-being territory from two different analytical perspectives. T2 asks where; T3 asks which faculty. Reading them together reveals: the heart (leb, T2.3) is the location of affect-volition integration (T3.4, T3.6) — where compassion (affect) determines giving (volitional act). The hidden inner parts (tukhoth, T2.5) are the constitutional home of the cognitive-formative faculty (T3.2 — the wisdom that is given there). The body (T2.6-7) is the somatic site of agentive expression (T3.7 — agency expresses through the body). The spirit (ruach, T2.1) is both the object of constitutive giving and the faculty whose depletion the eschatological giving addresses — connecting to the agency and relational capacity faculties that cannot operate from a faint spirit. What this pair reveals: constitutional location and faculty engagement are two descriptions of the same inner-being event. The characteristic is located constitutionally precisely where the relevant faculties operate.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-012: The faculty engagement pattern (T3 — perception, affect, volition, relational capacity all engaged) and the relational interface structure (T4 — God-to-human, human-to-God) reveal a faculty-interface …
findings.finding_value: The faculty engagement pattern (T3 — perception, affect, volition, relational capacity all engaged) and the relational interface structure (T4 — God-to-human, human-to-God) reveal a faculty-interface correspondence. In the God-to-human direction: divine hearing (T3.1 — perception) precedes compassionate giving (T4.1 — responsive basis); divine affect (T3.4 — rahamim, leb) determines the direction of giving (T4.1 — basis of extension); divine relational capacity (T3.11) is the prior orientation that makes the giving possible. In the human-to-God direction: human perception (Q2 — recognising divine sovereignty), human affect (blessing under loss), human volition (choosing to give glory), and human relational capacity (genuine correspondence) are all required for the giving to be genuine (T4.2 — inner posture). What this pair reveals: the relational interfaces are not external channels through which giving flows; they are relational events in which the inner faculties of both parties are engaged simultaneously and correspondingly. The correspondence is not mechanical but genuinely personal.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-014: The full-person faculty integration (T3 — all major faculties engaged) and the producing/produced-by structural position (T6) reveal that the characteristic's hub position is sustained by its faculty-…
findings.finding_value: The full-person faculty integration (T3 — all major faculties engaged) and the producing/produced-by structural position (T6) reveal that the characteristic's hub position is sustained by its faculty-integration property. It produces worship (R121, R176) because worship is the proper faculty response to received giving (T3 — perception of divine giving → affect of gratitude → volition of blessing → relational act of worship). It is produced by love (R103) and trust (R059) because love and trust are the inner-being sources from which the giving proceeds (T3 — affect motivates, volition commits, agency enacts). The causal sequences (T6.2) are faculty sequences in disguise: each sequential step is a faculty transition (suffering perceived → compassion moved → giving enacted). What this pair reveals: the structural network of this characteristic in the inner-being landscape is held together by faculty transitions. The characteristic is a hub because it is where multiple faculty-driven causal sequences converge and produce giving as their common expression.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-015: The faculty engagement pattern (T3 — hearing precedes giving, memory is narrative-temporal, affect is at source and target, conscientiousness is the apex) and the methodological-evidential analysis (T…
findings.finding_value: The faculty engagement pattern (T3 — hearing precedes giving, memory is narrative-temporal, affect is at source and target, conscientiousness is the apex) and the methodological-evidential analysis (T7 — virtue ethics illuminates, attachment theory illuminates, both diverge at critical points) converge in an analytically productive way. Virtue ethics (T7.3) addresses the same faculties that T3 identifies: moral evaluation, volition, agency, conscientiousness are the virtue-ethics faculties. The virtue-ethics framework illuminates T3 findings precisely because both are addressing the same inner-being territory. The divergence (T7.3.3 — virtue ethics cannot account for the constitutive primacy of received divine giving) maps onto the T3 finding that cognition is constituted by endowing giving (Q&A-071) rather than generated by the person. Attachment theory illuminates the hearing-precedes-giving pattern (T3.1 — God hears inner suffering) and the restoration of relational responsiveness (T3.11 — relational capacity restored). What this pair reveals: the human-science frameworks are useful precisely because they address the same inner-being faculties, and limited precisely where they diverge from the biblical account of those faculties' grounding.
[T3.4.1 Affect] M01: 1036/1036 answered, 0 silent, 0 unresolved. Top: affect (fear engages the affective faculty)×1036.

Yes, substantially. 2Sa 13:15: "Amnon hated her with very great hatred" — the intensity qualifier "very great" names the affective weight. Psa 25:19: "with what violent hatred they hate me" — violent names the affective character. Job 16:9 (sa.tam): "he has gnashed his teeth at me" — the somatic expression signals the affective intensity beneath. Ecc 9:6: hatred is listed alongside love and envy as one of the constitutive affective orientations of the living person. The affective dimension is present across all groups, though it varies in intensity.

Characteristically affectively cool rather than hot. Job 12:5: "in the thought of one who is at ease" — the ease is the affective register: contempt is comfortable, relaxed, indifferent. Est 1:18 (biz.za.von) pairs contempt with wrath ("contempt and wrath in plenty") — but the wrath is a separate phenomenon. The distinctive affective register of contempt is cold indifference or comfortable dismissal, not heated hostility.

The strongest affective register in M06 up to this point. The bdelussomai root (stench-based) and the ta.av root both carry physical resonance — the inner recoil has a quasi-somatic quality. The affective register of abhorrence is moral disgust — the moral equivalent of physical nausea. Strong, visceral, pulling away from its object.

Pro 27:4: "wrath is cruel (akh.ze.riy.yut), anger is overwhelming" — cruelty is named as the quality that wrath possesses when unrestrained by mercy. The affective register is the heat of wrath without the cooling of mercy. It is not the cool indifference of contempt — it is affective intensity (wrath, anger) operating without the limiting counterweight.

M06-E has the most extensive affective evidence in the cluster. Psa 69:20: "broken my heart...in despair" — not sadness but despair. Psa 31:11: "an object of dread to my acquaintances" — the reproached person produces dread in others; their affective condition is visible externally. Neh 1:3: "great trouble and shame." Jer 51:51: "we are put to shame, for we have heard reproach" — shame as the inner-affective response to received reproach. The affective register of M06-E is despair, shame, and fear.

Mat 5:25: "come to terms quickly" — urgency is the dominant affective register. 1Pe 5:8's watchfulness implies alert attentiveness rather than fearful anxiety. Job 22:20: relief at the adversary's defeat names the affective release when the adversary relationship ends. The affective register is urgency → vigilance → relief.

The most precisely named affective content in M06: "rejoiced" (Eze 25:6), "wholehearted joy" (Eze 36:5). The affective register is positive in quality — malice feels like joy to the one who holds it. This is what makes it distinctive and self-reinforcing: it is not an unpleasant inner state that might motivate its own cessation but a pleasurable one. The soul rejoices; the rejoicing deepens the malice.

**[A1 — God Righteousness]** Yes — alarm (Act 24:25, VSG M26-A1-006: Felix was alarmed when righteousness was discussed), guilt and shame (the repeated pattern of "you are righteous; we are in guilt," Neh 9:33; Ezr 9:15; Dan 9:7), and the awe of the heavens declaring God's righteousness (Psa 50:6; 97:6). Encountering God's righteousness produces affective states in those who hear it.

**[A2 — Human Righteousness]** Yes — and richly. VSG 3246-003 (the immediate response group for A2) is explicitly affective: gladness, exultation, and praise are the inner affective responses to righteousness. Hunger and thirst (Mat 5:6, VSG M26-A2-006) are affective-desire states. The palm tree image (Psa 92:12, VSG M26-A2-001) and flourishing imagery convey a positive affective state associated with righteous living. Bold as lions (Pro 28:1, VSG M26-A2-013) names the emotional affect of security and confidence in the righteous person.

**[B — Moral Uprightness]** Yes — "my inmost being will exult when your lips speak what is right" (Pro 23:16, VSG 1212-002). The word me.shar (uprightness in speech) produces an exultation in the speaker's inmost being. Uprightness generates an affective response in the person who hears or expresses it.

**[C — Justification]** Yes — hope (Tit 3:7: "heirs according to the hope of eternal life"). Hope is an affective-anticipatory state. The justified person's characteristic affect is hope — the forward-looking orientation of the one who knows their standing before God.

**[D — Avenging Justice]** Yes — 2Cor 7:11 (VSG 945-001) explicitly names the affective states produced by the righteous grief that issues in the desire for justice: "earnestness, eagerness to clear yourselves, indignation, fear, longing, zeal, punishment." The D-group surfaces a rich affective vocabulary. The cry for justice (Luk 18:3, VSG 944-001) is itself an affectively-charged act — the persistence of the widow is driven by affective engagement (longing, urgency, determination).

**[E — Condemnation]** Yes — the weight of condemnation is an affective state (the burden of being under verdict). The release of freedom from condemnation (Joh 8:10–11, VSG 4846-002) is an affective relief. The Ninevites who repented at the preaching of Jonah (Mat 12:41) responded with an affective-repentance (metanoeo: a change of mind and heart with emotional dimension).

**[F — Moral Reckoning]** Yes — indirectly. The reckoning act of weighing suffering against future glory (Rom 8:18, VSG 3410-001) is not emotionally neutral: it is an act of reorienting the affective response to suffering by placing it in a larger framework. The counting produces a changed relationship to the affective experience of suffering — not denial of the affect but its recontextualization through deliberate reckoning.

**[G — Structural Opposites]** Yes — the hardened and impenitent heart (Rom 2:5, VSG 3207-001) names an affective state: the absence of fear, the absence of compunction. The wicked person "stores up wrath" (Rom 2:5) — an accumulative judicial state that will produce affective experience at the day of judgment. Wickedness is associated with an affective deficit: the inability to feel the weight of what righteousness requires.

**[CLUSTER — T3.4]** E. The affective faculty is richly engaged across the cluster. The signature affects of righteousness in M26 are: gladness and exultation (A2), hope (C), earnestness and zeal (D), relief from condemnation's weight (E), and the recontextualization of suffering (F). These are not incidental emotional responses — they are constitutive of what it means to live righteously. Righteousness in M26 is affectively textured throughout.

findings.finding_value: Yes — extensively. Multiple affective registers: (1) Joy: Job 33:26 (795-002): the person accepted by God "sees his face with a shout of joy" — grace-received produces immediate joy. (2) Gratitude/warm positive affect: the science extract (Section 1 — Emmons/McCullough) confirms this is the psychological structure of received undeserved benefit — warm expansive positive affect directed toward the benefactor. (3) Anguish: Psa 77:7 (795-003): "will the Lord spurn forever, and never again be favorable?" — the absence of ra.tsah produces existential anguish. (4) Fear/awe: Psa 147:11: "the Lord takes pleasure in those who fear him" — reverent fear is the affective orientation that draws divine ra.tsah. (5) The grace-root and joy-root are shared (CHAR/chairo) — grace is etymologically joyful giving.

findings.finding_value: M46-B has rich affective content. Grief: the merchants weep and mourn (Rev 18:15-19) at the loss of Babylon's goods — deep affective engagement with material goods. Restlessness: "the full stomach of the rich will not let him sleep" (Ecc 5:12) — the affective-physical restlessness of abundance. The grief of the rich young ruler: "he became very sad" (perilupos, Luk 18:23) — deep sorrow produced by the threat to his wealth.
