**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes, partially. The triumphing cry (re.na.nah) and the association with singing (Psa 100:2; Isa 49:13; Zep 3:17 — God exulting with singing) suggest that exultation naturally generates creative expression — song, poetry, and vocal art. The Psalms themselves are creative acts that arise from and give shape to exultation.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes. The consistent association of Joy with music, poetry, and song is the primary creative evidence: 1Ch 15:16 (David appointing Levites to raise "sounds of joy" with instruments — organised creative music in service of Joy); Psa 30:11 (mourning turned to dancing — the creative-bodily form of joy); Jer 31:13 ("young women rejoice in the dance; young men and old shall be merry") — dance as Joy's creative-bodily expression; Neh 12:27 (gladness expressed through singing, cymbals, harps, lyres at the dedication); Isa 55:12 ("you shall go out in joy… the mountains and the hills before you shall break forth into singing, and all the trees of the field shall clap their hands") — creation's Joy expressed in personified creative response. The Psalms themselves are creative products of joy-oriented engagement with God.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Yes, in specific forms. Luk 1:47's Mary's exultation immediately moves into the Magnificat — a creative poetic-prophetic work generated from the agalliao state. Act 2:26 (Peter's appropriation of Psalm 16 in a Spirit-exultation context) shows the creative-interpretive act of applying past creative work (David's Psalm) to a new Spirit-context. M04-F's ba.lag-seeking also has a creative dimension: Job 9:27's deliberate attempt at cheerfulness ("I will put off my sad face, and be of good cheer") is a self-directed creative act of inner-state engineering.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Partially. The M04-L-VCG-01 ki-tov declarations produce and are embedded in the Psalms — creative works generated from the inner recognition of divine goodness. Isa 52:7 (the good-news herald) is a creative-prophetic image (the beauty of the messenger's feet). The doxological praise tradition that grows from the ki-tov recognition involves creative expression (song, poetry, communal liturgy). However, creativity is not the dominant faculty of Gladness in this corpus — it is secondary to the cognitive and affective.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes: (1) **Pro 8:30–31** — Wisdom as God's daily delight, "rejoicing before him always, rejoicing in his inhabited world and delighting in the children of man" — Wisdom's creative delight in the world and in humanity; this is the most creatively-charged delight in the corpus; the creation itself is the object of Wisdom's sha.a.shu.im; (2) **Ecc 12:10** — "the Preacher sought to find words of delight" — creative-literary work driven by the desire to find language that carries genuine pleasure; (3) **Psa 119's Delight in God's law as poetic corpus** — the entire Psa 119 sha.a.shu.im series is itself a creative work generated from Delight in the law; Delight in God's word produces the creativity of the psalmist's literary meditation.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes: (1) **Psa 45:1** — "my heart overflows with a pleasing theme; I address my verses to the king; my tongue is like the pen of a ready scribe" — the pleasantness of the creative-poetic impulse arising from the heart; Pleasure in the subject-matter (the king's beauty and virtue) generates creative expression; (2) **Pro 16:24's gracious words** — the crafting of genuinely pleasant speech is a creative act; the one who produces words that are "like a honeycomb" engages the creative faculty in service of Pleasure; (3) **Pro 3:17** (wisdom's ways as pleasantness) — wisdom's creative work produces a life-path characterised by pleasantness.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Yes: (1) **The Psalmic proclamatory tradition** — the entire VCG-01 wonder-proclamation corpus represents creative acts: songs, psalms, and hymns generated from Wonder at God's acts (Exo 15:11's Song of the Sea is a primary creative-Wonder text; Psa 98:1 — "sing a new song" because "he has done marvellous things"); (2) **Psa 40:5** ("yet they are more than can be told") — Wonder's exceeding quality motivating the attempt at ever-new creative expression; (3) **2Ch 2:9** (the temple as "great and wonderful") — the creative work of the temple as wonder-architecture; (4) **Isa 9:6** ("Wonderful Counselor") — the prophetic creative act of naming the coming child's wonder-quality.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All seven engage the creative faculty; all seven produce creative expression as a natural overflow. The most significant patterns: (1) **Most creatively generative**: Joy (Char 2) — the feast commandments institutionalise the creative forms of rejoicing (song, dance, music, communal festivity); Joy and creative expression are mutually reinforcing throughout the corpus; Wonder (Char 6) — the inexhaustibility of its object (God's wonders "more than can be told" — Psa 40:5) perpetually motivates new creative attempts; Wonder generates the "new song" (Psa 98:1); (2) **Most foundationally creative**: Delight (Char 4) — Pro 8:30–31 (Wisdom's sha.a.shu.im in creation before the world existed) frames Delight as constitutive of the creative act itself — God and Wisdom delight in creating; Delight is the inner source from which authentic creativity flows; (3) **Creatively generative through overflow**: Exultation (Char 1) — the triumphing cry becomes the Psalm; Gladness (Char 3) — the ki-tov recognition produces the doxological tradition; Pleasure (Char 5) — Psa 45:1's heart overflowing with a pleasing theme generating poetic praise; Suffering-Joy (Char 7) — the Magnificat (Luk 1:46–55) as Suffering-Joy's most immediate creative overflow.

**[CHAR-6]** E — 1Ch28:21 evidences a connexion: "every willing man who has skill for any kind of service" — the "any kind of service" implies creative/skilled engagement; the temple craftsmen's willing-hearted participation in building enabled the creative deployment of diverse crafts. Cluster-level: M09 is not primarily a creative cluster — only one characteristic (CHAR-6) evidences creative-faculty engagement, and even there, willing-heartedness is the enabling condition for creativity rather than being itself creative. findings.finding_value: T3 reveals two structurally distinctive findings about compassion's faculty engagement. First, creativity is entirely silent (three S ratings) — the most informative absence in the tier: compassion responds, it does not originate or create. It is the most responsive of the faculties-engaging characteristics. Second, affect and moral action are structurally unified in compassion — not sequentially related but simultaneous. Affect is the mechanism of movement (splanchnizō is both the felt inner event and the cause of the action), not a precursor or accompaniment. This is unique among the characteristics reviewed: in most other registries, affect and volition are distinguishable stages; in compassion, the felt movement is already the morally motivated action beginning. A third distinctive finding: compassion converts moral knowledge into motivated action — it is the motivational ground of conscientiousness, not a product of it. The conscience faculty engagement reveals compassion as conscience-healing: it addresses the pitiable condition that conscience perceives as a moral claim, resolving the tension between moral knowledge and moral incapacity. The three relational modes (building/sustaining — chesed; restoring/repairing — splanchnizō; extending across difference — Good Samaritan) are a new finding not in the instruction typology.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-003: T3 produces four structurally significant findings about grace's faculty engagement. First, grace is agency-constituting rather than agency-replacing: 1Cor 15:10 holds in explicit paradox — "I worked …
findings.finding_value: T3 produces four structurally significant findings about grace's faculty engagement. First, grace is agency-constituting rather than agency-replacing: 1Cor 15:10 holds in explicit paradox — "I worked harder than any of them, though it was not I but the grace of God that is with me." Agency is not displaced but constituted by grace. This relationship holds in paradox that the T3.6 prompt options (enable/deepen/bypass/impair) cannot accommodate — a prompt design limitation noted for catalogue revision. Second, grace produces moral clarity (T3.8 — sharpens moral evaluation rather than bypassing it): the person who recognises grace has made a precise moral evaluation (they know they received what they did not deserve). Third, grace and conscience are mutually necessary: grace is the condition within which conscience can operate fully without destroying the person; conscience without grace produces condemnation; grace without conscience produces presumption (T3.9). Fourth, grace is the primary relational faculty developer in the registry's evidence — it reaches every relational register (vertical access, horizontal forgiving, speech-grace) and enables each one. Creativity (T3.5) is the one genuinely silent faculty — not an impairment but a non-engagement: grace receives and constitutes, it does not create.

In the disordered register: distorts — channels the creative capacity into destructive planning and deceptive self-presentation. In the righteous register: no evidence of creativity being engaged; righteous hatred is more receptive (downstream of understanding) than creative.

No evidence that M01-A either enables or impairs creativity distinctively.

Fear's engagement with the creative faculty is primarily distorting in the disordered sub-groups: the imagination is captured by anticipated threat (M01-F) or negative scenario-construction (M01-B-VCG-05). Ordered fear (M01-A) does not appear to engage or impair creativity.

Possessing rage instrumentalises creativity — it uses the creative planning capacity for destructive purposes. The evidence does not show creativity being deepened by anger in its possessing form; rather, creativity is co-opted and driven toward the anger's object.

Grief can enable and channel creativity into lament expression — the prophet's weeping producing the lament poems (Jer 9:1 — M03-A-VCG-04) and the prophetic sign-act (Eze 21:6 — M03-E-VCG-01). However, grief can also impair ordinary creative expression: mourning so total it transforms music (Job 30:31 — M03-B-VCG-01) — grief colonising creative capacity rather than generating new forms.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Exultation enables and generates creative expression — it is the affective-volitional pressure that produces song and poetry. The Psalms in this corpus are themselves evidence of this: exultation pressed into creative literary form (Psa 21:1; 32:11; 89:16; 149:2).

**[CHAR-2]** E — Joy enables and generates creative expression: 1Ch 15:16 shows David's Joy producing organised creative music-making as its institutional form; the Psalms of this corpus are creative literary works produced from the inner experience of Joy-in-God. Joy does not bypass creativity but pressures it toward expression — the inner gladness seeks a form adequate to itself.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Suffering-Joy generates a specific form of creativity: the Spirit-produced exultation in adversity naturally seeks expression through prophetic poetry (the Magnificat; the tradition of lament-moving-into-praise in the Psalms). The creative act is both the expression of the inner state and the means of its consolidation.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Gladness enables creativity in its doxological expression: recognising divine goodness naturally produces the impulse toward praise-expression (the ki-tov formula moving into singing). Gladness does not bypass creativity but gives it its content and occasion.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Delight enables creativity specifically by directing it toward its proper object: Wisdom's sha.a.shu.im in creation (Pro 8:30–31) produces the creative work of the inhabited world as an object of Delight; the Preacher's search for words of delight (Ecc 12:10) produces the literary creativity of Ecclesiastes. Delight in God's word produces the psalm's creative-poetic meditation. Misdirected Delight (M04-P) does not produce creative works evidenced in the corpus — it produces destructive captivation instead.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Pleasure in a worthy subject (Psa 45:1 — the king's beauty) enables creative expression: the heart overflows, the tongue becomes agile. Pleasure functions as the creative motivating force when the object is genuinely pleasant — the pleasantness of what is experienced generates the impulse to express it in beautiful form.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Wonder enables and generates creativity: the inexhaustibility of God's wonders (Psa 40:5 — "more than can be told") motivates continued creative expression in new attempts to capture what cannot be fully told. The "new song" (Psa 98:1; 96:1) — the creative response to each new wonder — shows Wonder as the generative source of fresh creative expression. Wonder cannot be adequately expressed in existing forms, so it generates new ones.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's characteristics consistently enable and generate creativity rather than bypassing or impairing it. The common pattern: the positive inner state seeks a form adequate to itself, and the inexhaustibility of the object motivates continued creative attempts. Wonder is the most theoretically significant: because God's wonders "are more than can be told" (Psa 40:5), Wonder perpetually motivates new creative expression — no existing creative form is fully adequate to its object. This confirms the cluster's creativity as constitutively inexhaustible: as long as God's acts, character, and beauty are the object, the cluster's creative production will not exhaust itself. The only impairing exception: misdirected Delight (M04-P) does not produce creative works in the corpus — the creative faculty is captured into captivation and destructiveness rather than generative expression.
**[CHAR-1]** S — Not evidenced. The evidence is silent on creativity.

**[CHAR-2]** S — The 72-verse CHAR-2 corpus does not evidence engagement with the creative faculty. Silent.

**[CLUSTER]** S — All six characteristics are silent on the creative faculty. M07's shame-field does not engage imagination or the capacity to originate in any evidenced way across the entire corpus. This cluster-wide silence is analytically significant: the shame-field is oriented toward withdrawal, concealment, and moral assessment — not toward creative origination. Shame closes; it does not open. This is a genuine cluster-level characteristic and not merely a data gap. Its significance: M07 may represent one of the most creativity-suppressing fields in the programme, which would make its eschatological resolution (Char 1's shame permanently removed) a necessary precondition for the full exercise of the image-bearer's creative capacities.

**[CHAR-1]** S — Silent. No evidence in the 149-verse corpus addresses CHAR-1's relationship to the creative/imaginative faculty in either direction — neither enabling, deepening, bypassing, nor impairing it.
**[CHAR-2]** S — Silent. No evidence on CHAR-2's relationship to the creative faculty in §3.A.
**[CHAR-3]** S — Silent. No evidence on CHAR-3's relationship to the creative faculty in §3.B.
**[CHAR-4]** S — Silent. No evidence on CHAR-4's relationship to the creative faculty.
**[CHAR-5]** S — Silent. No evidence on CHAR-5's relationship to the creative faculty in §3.D.
**[CLUSTER]** S — Silent across all five characteristics. See T3.5.1.

**[CHAR-2]** S — The evidence is silent on any direct connexion between submission and creative or imaginative capacity. The characteristic operates in the authority-relationship register rather than the creative-generative register.
**[CHAR-3]** S — The evidence is silent on any relationship between contrition and creative or imaginative capacity.
**[CHAR-4]** S — The evidence is silent on any relationship between meekness/gentleness and creative or imaginative capacity.
**[CHAR-5]** S — The evidence is silent on any relationship between semnotēs and creative or imaginative capacity.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Willing-heartedness *enables* creative faculty deployment. 1Ch28:21 — "willing man who has skill for any kind of service" — the pairing of willingness with skill-across-all-kinds implies that the willing person brings their full creative and skilled repertoire to the service. The characteristic enables rather than constrains the creative faculty by removing the reluctance-friction that would limit creative engagement to the minimum required.

**[CHAR-1]** S — The evidence is silent on any direct connexion between humility and creative or imaginative capacity. Analytically, one might infer that the epistemic-virtue function of humility (enabling accurate perception and cognition — see T3.1.2 and T3.2.2) might indirectly free the creative faculty from self-referential constraints, but this is inference beyond the corpus.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Only Willing-heartedness (CHAR-6) directly evidences a creative-faculty enabling connexion: 1Ch28:21 — "every willing man who has skill for any kind of service" — the willing-hearted person deploys their full creative and skilled repertoire. The other five characteristics are silent on direct creative-faculty effects. Analytically, the epistemic-virtue function of Humility (CHAR-1) might indirectly free the creative faculty from self-referential constraints, but this remains inference beyond the corpus. Cluster-level: CHAR-6 is the cluster's sole explicitly creativity-enabling characteristic, and even there it enables rather than constitutes creativity — willing-heartedness removes the reluctance-friction that would limit creative engagement to the minimum required. The cluster's primary creative-enabling characteristic is CHAR-6.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — The evidence from Hos 13:2 suggests that wilful sinning *misdirects* creativity — the creative faculty produces increasingly elaborate substitutes for God (skillfully crafted idols) rather than what it was designed to produce. The creative capacity is not impaired (the idols are skillfully made) but its direction is perverted by the sinning orientation. This is the characteristic's effect on creativity: not suppression but misdirection.
**[CHAR-10]** S — No evidence. The corpus is silent on the creative faculty's engagement with these mechanisms.

**[CHAR-11]** S — No direct evidence. The condition's relationship to creativity is not addressed in the corpus. The condition's primary modes (enslaving power, standing debt, passions-capture) are not creative-faculty operations.
**[CHAR-12]** S — No evidence. The corpus is silent on the creative faculty's engagement.

**[CHAR-13]** E — The record *captures and misdirects* the creative faculty. Pro 24:9 — the devising (creative cognitive act) of folly is itself sin; the creative capacity is deployed toward the wrong object and generates a record entry. Isa 30:1 — the plan-making faculty (creative will) that pursues alliances not of God's Spirit adds to the sin-record. The creative faculty's operation against God produces record entries; it is captured by sinful purpose rather than creative goodness.
**[CHAR-14]** S — No direct evidence. The corpus is silent on the creative faculty's engagement with forgiveness sought and received.
**[CHAR-15]** S — No evidence. The corpus is silent on the creative faculty's engagement with generational sin.
**[CHAR-16]** S — No direct evidence. The corpus is silent on the creative faculty's engagement with the sinner-identity.
**[CHAR-17]** S — No direct evidence. The corpus is silent on the creative faculty's engagement with guilt as inner-being state.
**[CHAR-18]** S — No direct evidence. The corpus is silent on the creative faculty's engagement with iniquity as accumulated moral crime.
**[CHAR-19]** S — No direct evidence. The corpus is silent on the creative faculty's engagement with transgression as deliberate boundary-crossing.
**[CHAR-2]** S — No evidence. The corpus is silent on creativity in the context of unintentional sinning.
**[CHAR-20]** S — No direct evidence. The corpus is silent on the creative faculty's engagement with faithlessness.

**[CHAR-21]** E — Perversion *misdirects* the creative faculty toward evil's devising. Pro 6:14 — "continually devises evil" — the creative-cognitive capacity is captured and deployed toward schemes of harm and discord. The "continually" (*kol-hayyôm* — all the time) confirms that the perverted heart's creative capacity is perpetually directed toward evil rather than occasionally. The creative faculty is thus not eliminated by perversion but redirected — the perverted person can be diligently creative in scheming harm.

**[CHAR-22]** E — Injustice *misdirects* the creative faculty toward unjust ends. Psa 58:2's "devise wrongs" and Psa 64:6's "diligent search for injustice" show the creative-analytical capacity engaged toward planning wrong. Hab 2:12's city-building on iniquity shows the constructive faculty deployed toward civic injustice. The creative capacity is not eliminated but redirected from creative right-order building to creative wrong-order building.
**[CHAR-3]** S — No evidence. The corpus is silent on creativity in connection with confession.
**[CHAR-4]** S — No evidence. The corpus is silent on creativity in connection with conscience suppression.
**[CHAR-5]** S — No evidence. The corpus is silent on creativity in connection with refusal to repent.
**[CHAR-6]** S — No evidence. The corpus is silent on creativity in connection with habitual defection.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Contagious sin *misdirects* the creative-constructive faculty: Jer 32:35's high places of Baal are creative acts whose product is the vehicle for child sacrifice ("to offer up their sons and daughters to Molech"). The creative capacity to build and design is engaged in constructing the structures that transmit and institutionalise the sinning direction. The creative faculty remains fully operative but is deployed in the service of the contagious sinning pattern rather than in the service of God-directed worship.

**[CHAR-8]** E — Political revolt *channels* the creative-constructive faculty toward political institution-building: 2Ki 8:20 — "set up a king of their own" — the creative capacity to establish governance is exercised in the service of the revolt's positive assertion of independence. The characteristic does not impair creativity but deploys it in the construction of alternative political authority.

**[CHAR-9]** E — Sinful speech *misdirects* the creative faculty toward fabrication and false claim construction. Rev 2:9's false identity claim shows the creative capacity for self-definition being used to produce a false identity that slanders what is genuinely God's (the true community). The creative capacity to speak and define is directed toward false speech rather than true.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The characteristic co-opts the creative faculty for destructive ends rather than impairing it. The wicked person plans (Psa 37:12), constructs traps (Jer 5:26), generates deceptive counsel (Pro 12:5), and weaponises speech (Pro 12:6) — all creative operations. The faculty is operational but redirected. The impairment is of the faculty's orientation toward its designed purpose (the creation of good, the building of just community), not of the faculty itself. The evidence does not show the wicked person as creatively disabled; rather, their creative capacity is fully deployed in the service of wickedness.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The characteristic co-opts the creative faculty for evil production rather than impairing it. The evil person "brings forth evil" (Mat 12:35 — VCG-03) — the bringing-forth is the creative act. The characteristic does not disable origination but redirects what is originated. 3Jo 10 (vc=14454 — VCG-04) shows creative energy directed toward domineering community control — active, organized, and persistent social harm requiring the creative deployment of speech and obstruction. The characteristic enables and directs the creative faculty toward evil; it does not empty or disable it.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The characteristic co-opts the creative faculty for the production of concealment and deception rather than impairing it. Pro 26:25 (vc=1694 — VCG-02): the gracious speech covering seven inner abominations requires considerable creative social performance — the creative faculty is fully operational in the service of masking the abominable inner state. The characteristic does not eliminate creativity but redirects it toward concealment and moral inversion. The act of making idols (Deu 27:15 — VCG-04) shows creativity deployed in abominable service — the craftsman's skill is present, but the product is an abomination.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The characteristic redirects and energises the creative faculty toward idolatrous production. The Eze 7:20 (VCG-05) example is most revealing: the person takes "beautiful ornament" — already a product of creative care — and converts it into idol-material, showing creative repurposing in the service of abomination. The creativity is fully present and resourced; it is not impaired but redirected. The energy and ingenuity of idol-making (Deu 29:17 — VCG-02: wood, stone, silver, gold — diverse material engagement) show creative capacity fully deployed in the characteristic's service.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The characteristic redirects and enables the creative faculty for evil production. The nocturnal deviser (Mic 2:1 — VCG-02: lying on the bed devising wickedness) is exercising sustained imaginative planning; the counsel-giver (Eze 11:2 — VCG-02) is producing creative social strategies. Psa 64:2 (vc=38244 — VCG-03): "secret plots of the wicked" — the secrecy implies creative concealment alongside the scheming. The creative faculty is not impaired but fully operational and redirected toward harm-generation. Isa 10:1 (vc=38191 — VCG-02): "writers who keep writing oppression" — the professional creative act of writing is co-opted for institutional harm.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The characteristic redirects the creative faculty toward misrepresentation and false narrative construction. Rom 3:8 (VCG-02): the creative capacity deployed to construct a falsely attributed teaching. Joh 18:30 (VCG-03): the creative capacity deployed to construct a justificatory false charge. In VCG-01 (the direct blasphemy register), the creative faculty appears less prominently — the hardened will expressing contempt through cursing does not require the same creative construction as false attribution. The characteristic thus engages creativity differently by VCG: VCG-01 is more directly hostile without requiring creative fabrication; VCG-02/03 require active verbal construction of false representations.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster consistently enables and redirects the creative faculty toward evil production rather than impairing it. Char 5 (Mic 2:1 — elaborate nocturnal devising deployed at dawn), Char 4 (elaborate idol-crafting from valuable materials), Char 6 (carefully constructed false attributions). The cluster reveals M10b as characteristically creative in its evil production — not a crude, impulsive failure but a sophisticated, planned, fabricated phenomenon requiring active creative deployment.

**[CLUSTER]** S — Not evidenced in any of the four characteristics. The M10c cluster's domain is moral-volitional, sacral-categorical, and constitutional — not imaginative or creative.

findings.session_b_note: The silence on creativity is itself informative. Contrition is a receptive rather than generative condition — the contrite person is oriented toward receiving (divine revival, nearness, salvation) rather than toward creating or originating. This is consistent with the Dependence/Creatureliness dimension: the creaturely posture of lowliness is structurally receptive, not assertive or creative. The absence of creative faculty engagement reflects the fundamental character of contrition as the condition of disclosed need before God.

findings.session_b_note: The marginal engagement with creativity (Job 16:4 as the primary evidence point) suggests that fellowship's primary constitutional operation is not creative but participatory and relational. Fellowship enables persons to *enter* existing relationships, not primarily to *originate* new ones (though the proclamation mode in 1Jo 1:3 does show a generative dimension). The characteristic is more about joining what is already there than creating what is not yet there — with the exception of the fellowship-through-proclamation mode.

findings.session_b_note: The creative engagement pattern — where evidenced — reveals that love's depth produces a surplus that demands expression beyond ordinary speech. The love-song, the poem, the kiss, the anointing (Luk 7:38) are all creative acts that exceed propositional communication. This suggests love has an expressive excess: it overflows the available ordinary forms and generates new ones. However, the pattern of non-engagement is unclear — the data does not indicate love impairing creativity, nor does it name love as the explicit source of creative capacity. The data supports: love is one of the inner-being states most associated with creative expression; whether this constitutes enabling the creative faculty or simply being a frequent companion of it is not determinable from the current evidence.

findings.finding_value: T3 reveals two structurally distinctive findings about compassion's faculty engagement. First, creativity is entirely silent (three S ratings) — the most informative absence in the tier: compassion responds, it does not originate or create. It is the most responsive of the faculties-engaging characteristics. Second, affect and moral action are structurally unified in compassion — not sequentially related but simultaneous. Affect is the mechanism of movement (splanchnizō is both the felt inner event and the cause of the action), not a precursor or accompaniment. This is unique among the characteristics reviewed: in most other registries, affect and volition are distinguishable stages; in compassion, the felt movement is already the morally motivated action beginning. A third distinctive finding: compassion converts moral knowledge into motivated action — it is the motivational ground of conscientiousness, not a product of it. The conscience faculty engagement reveals compassion as conscience-healing: it addresses the pitiable condition that conscience perceives as a moral claim, resolving the tension between moral knowledge and moral incapacity. The three relational modes (building/sustaining — chesed; restoring/repairing — splanchnizō; extending across difference — Good Samaritan) are a new finding not in the instruction typology.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-003: T3 produces four structurally significant findings about grace's faculty engagement. First, grace is agency-constituting rather than agency-replacing: 1Cor 15:10 holds in explicit paradox — "I worked …
findings.finding_value: T3 produces four structurally significant findings about grace's faculty engagement. First, grace is agency-constituting rather than agency-replacing: 1Cor 15:10 holds in explicit paradox — "I worked harder than any of them, though it was not I but the grace of God that is with me." Agency is not displaced but constituted by grace. This relationship holds in paradox that the T3.6 prompt options (enable/deepen/bypass/impair) cannot accommodate — a prompt design limitation noted for catalogue revision. Second, grace produces moral clarity (T3.8 — sharpens moral evaluation rather than bypassing it): the person who recognises grace has made a precise moral evaluation (they know they received what they did not deserve). Third, grace and conscience are mutually necessary: grace is the condition within which conscience can operate fully without destroying the person; conscience without grace produces condemnation; grace without conscience produces presumption (T3.9). Fourth, grace is the primary relational faculty developer in the registry's evidence — it reaches every relational register (vertical access, horizontal forgiving, speech-grace) and enables each one. Creativity (T3.5) is the one genuinely silent faculty — not an impairment but a non-engagement: grace receives and constitutes, it does not create.

findings.session_b_note: The absence of creative/imaginative faculty engagement is itself analytically informative. Kindness is constitutively oriented toward the actual existing other — its chesed character is loyalty and steadfast commitment to a real relational partner in a real relational context. It does not require imagination to conjure a recipient or creativity to originate a new relational reality. This distinguishes kindness from characteristics like hope (which envisions what does not yet exist) or creativity (which brings the new into being). The non-engagement with creativity reveals that kindness is a conserving and sustaining characteristic rather than an originating one — it holds and maintains the relational bond rather than creating it.

findings.session_b_note: Silence on the creative faculty for peace is consistent with the registry's character: peace is not primarily described as a creative or generative condition but as a receptive, restful, and relational one. The data's silence on creativity suggests that the creative dimension of peace is not theologically foregrounded in the biblical vocabulary — the emphasis throughout is on reception, orientation, and the condition of the whole person rather than on creative output. This is worth noting as a gap for Session D if creativity's relationship to peace is to be explored.

findings.finding_value:
No engagement with creativity evidenced across any sub-group.

[Cluster-level addition — Phase 9 cross-sub-group review] The creative faculty (imagination and origination) is absent from all four sub-groups' verse evidence. The sole marginal reference is Pro 18:11 ("in his imagination" — be.mash.kit-to, describing the mental construct of wealth as security), which is cognitive-constructive rather than creative in the full sense. The wealth domain does not engage the creative faculty across any register of its vocabulary or any of its 197 relevant verses. This silence is noted as a structural feature.

findings.finding_value: The pattern reveals that disordered fear captures the imagination for negative projection, while ordered fear does not distinctively engage the creative faculty. Fear is not a creative-enabling characteristic but a creative-channelling one: in its disordered forms it channels imagination toward threat-scenarios. This is consistent with the science extract's Borkovec worry-model (verbal-linguistic, future-oriented, repetitive cognitive engagement).

The pattern reveals that anger, especially in its possessing form, does not destroy the creative faculty but redirects it destructively. This is consistent with the observation that Haman's planning (Est 3:6–15) is elaborate and systematic — the creative capacity remains functional but has been commandeered by rage. The characteristic's engagement with creativity is one of instrumentalisation, not enhancement.

Grief generates a specific and distinctive creative form — lament — which is a creative expression of inner suffering rather than inner joy. The Lamentations and prophetic lament tradition shows grief as one of the most generative sources of Hebrew literary creativity. Grief does not bypass or impair the creative faculty but redirects it toward a specific register.
**[CHAR-1]** E — Exultation is a generative characteristic — it produces creative expression as a natural overflow. The triumphing cry becomes the song; the inner surge becomes the poem.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Joy is a generative characteristic: its inner pressure naturally seeks and produces creative forms — song, poetry, dance, communal festivity. The feast-commandments (Deu 16:11–15) are in part the institutional recognition that Joy requires a creative-communal form to sustain and express itself. The pattern suggests Joy and creativity are mutually reinforcing: Joy presses toward creative expression; creative expression sustains and deepens Joy.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Suffering-Joy generates prophetic-creative expression as a natural overflow — the exultation that transcends circumstances presses toward poetry and praise. This is consistent with the agalliao root's leaping-outward quality: what arises in the deepest inner being seeks the most expressive outer form.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Gladness generates a particular form of creativity — the doxological and declarative. The creative expression that Gladness produces is primarily the expression of recognised goodness: testimony, praise declaration, and the written wisdom that codifies evaluative learning (Proverbs, Ecclesiastes as creative-literary crystallisations of the evaluative-gladness faculty).

**[CHAR-4]** E — Delight is a creative-generative characteristic: Pro 8:30–31's Wisdom delighting in the children of man frames Delight as constitutive of the creative act — God and Wisdom delight in creating and in what they have created. Human creativity that arises from Delight in God's word and wisdom participates in this creative-delight pattern. The pattern reveals Delight as the inner source from which authentic creativity flows.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Pleasure is creativity-generating in its relational and beauty-appreciating register: when the inner person is genuinely pleased by what it perceives, creative expression follows naturally. Psa 45:1 is the clearest evidence — a heart overflowing with pleasing matter cannot but speak it. The pattern reveals Pleasure as one of the generative roots of creative expression in Scripture.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Wonder is creatively generative specifically because its object (God's incomprehensible acts) can never be fully expressed — the inexhaustibility of the wonder-object perpetually motivates new creative attempts. The Psalmic tradition's breadth and variety (61 verses across many different psalms all proclaiming God's wondrous works) is itself the evidence of this creative generativity: each poet's encounter with divine wonders produces a new creative expression.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster reveals M04 as the most creatively generative cluster in the programme's positive-affect domain. All seven characteristics produce creative expression; all seven are reinforced by and sustain creative expression. The cluster's historical testimony — the Psalms, the Songs of Ascent, the festival songs, the Magnificat, the lament-to-praise movements — is itself the evidence of this: the scriptural canon's most creative literary productions arise from the inner states this cluster names. Formation in the cluster's characteristics is simultaneously formation in creative-doxological capacity.

**[CHAR-2]** S — The 72-verse CHAR-2 corpus does not evidence engagement with the creative faculty. Silent.

**[CLUSTER]** S — All six characteristics are silent on the creative faculty. M07's shame-field does not engage imagination or the capacity to originate in any evidenced way across the entire corpus. This cluster-wide silence is analytically significant: the shame-field is oriented toward withdrawal, concealment, and moral assessment — not toward creative origination. Shame closes; it does not open. This is a genuine cluster-level characteristic and not merely a data gap. Its significance: M07 may represent one of the most creativity-suppressing fields in the programme, which would make its eschatological resolution (Char 1's shame permanently removed) a necessary precondition for the full exercise of the image-bearer's creative capacities.

---

**[CHAR-1]** S — The silence on creativity suggests CHAR-1 does not operate primarily through the imaginative/creative register. Its primary faculties are dispositional/volitional (T1.8), cognitive-perceptual (T3.1–3.2), and relational (T3.11). This pattern of non-engagement may be significant for cross-characteristic comparison: characteristics that do engage creativity as part of their inner-being expression would stand in contrast to CHAR-1's perceptual-volitional profile.
**[CHAR-2]** S — CHAR-2's silence on creativity confirms its primary register as volitional and relational-authority-transgressing rather than creative-imaginative.
**[CHAR-3]** S — CHAR-3's silence on creativity confirms its primary communicative/expressive register — it operates through speech and social display, not through imaginative origination.

**[CHAR-4]** S — CHAR-4's silence on creativity confirms its exclusively cognitive-self-assessment register. It does not engage imagination or creative origination but the mind's self-referential evaluation function.

**[CHAR-5]** S — CHAR-5's silence on creativity confirms its structural-power and dispositional register — it operates through received structural goods (power, wealth, position) rather than through imaginative origination.

**[CLUSTER]** S — The cluster-wide silence on the creative faculty confirms that M08 does not map onto creativity as a dimension. This is analytically informative: pride's evidence base is concentrated on the self in relation to God's authority, received goods, and social others — not on creative generation. The creative faculty's absence from M08 may indicate it belongs to a different cluster-domain.

**[CHAR-2]** S — The silence on creative faculty engagement reveals that submission's constitutional reach is constitutively relational-responsive (oriented toward authorities and commands) rather than originating-creative. The characteristic is structured by reception-and-yielding rather than origination-and-generation.
**[CHAR-3]** S — The silence confirms that contrition's constitutional focus is narrowly on the person's inner moral-relational state before God rather than on creative or generative capacities.
**[CHAR-4]** S — The silence confirms the characteristic operates in the quality-of-engagement-with-others register rather than the creative-generative register.
**[CHAR-5]** S — The silence confirms semnotēs operates in the character-ordering-social register rather than the creative-generative register.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The 1Ch28:21 pattern reveals that willing-heartedness is the *enabling condition for wholehearted creative skilled service* — it is not itself creative but enables creativity to be deployed fully. This is one of the most distinctive findings about CHAR-6: it enables other faculties (creativity, skill) to be fully expressed rather than partially deployed under reluctant compliance.

**[CHAR-1]** S — The silence on creative faculty engagement reveals that humility's constitutional reach is primarily interpersonal and relational (between person, God, and others) rather than creative or generative. The characteristic opens the person toward genuine relation and accurate self-knowledge; it does not evidence itself in the creative-imaginative register.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The near-universal silence on creative faculty engagement reveals that M09's constitutional reach is primarily interpersonal and relational rather than creative or generative. The cluster opens the person toward genuine relation and accurate self-knowledge; it does not primarily evidence itself in the creative-imaginative register. The single exception — Willing-heartedness (CHAR-6) enabling creative deployment via 1Ch28:21 — is consistent with CHAR-6's role as the cluster's agency-maximising characteristic: it enables the fullest expression of whatever capacities the person has, including creative ones. The cluster's relationship to creativity is one of enabling rather than constituting — M09 is not a creativity cluster but can free the creative faculty from reluctance-friction.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The limited evidence (Hos 13:2; Neh 6:13) suggests that wilful sinning does not primarily operate through the creative faculty — it is not constitutively a creative act. The creative dimension appears as a secondary effect (elaborated idolatry) rather than the primary mechanism. The characteristic's core is volitional (will choosing the wrong) with creativity as a vehicle for expressing and deepening the sinning pattern over time, not as its origin.

**[CHAR-10]** S — The silence on creativity is consistent with the mechanisms' non-creative character: enticement exploits what exists (desire), hypocrisy performs an existing identity pattern, apostasy departs from an existing commitment. None require or primarily engage creative origination. Noted.

**[CHAR-11]** S — The silence on creativity reflects the characteristic's focus on the person's condition before God (sin as structural state, debt, enslaving power) rather than on the person's creative productive capacity. The condition is primarily about what sin has done to the person's inner-being standing, not about what the person creates. Noted.

**[CHAR-12]** S — The silence on creativity is consistent with the enslaving-power characteristic's focus on captivity (not creation), structural imprisonment (Gal 3:22), and constitutional identity (1Jo 3:8/9). Noted.

**[CHAR-13]** E — The creative pattern reveals that the divine record is not only generated by obvious moral failures but also by the active cognitive-creative deployment of the person's planning and devising capacities toward ends contrary to God (Pro 24:9; Isa 30:1). The record captures what the mind devises and what the will plans, not only what the body does overtly. This confirms the record's comprehensive scope: it is sensitive to inner creative-cognitive movements as well as outer acts.

**[CHAR-14]** S — The silence on creativity is consistent with the characteristic's focus on the restoration of the sin-broken relationship rather than on creative origination. Forgiveness restores what sin damaged; it does not primarily operate through the creative faculty. Noted.
**[CHAR-15]** S — The silence on creativity is consistent with the characteristic's focus on inherited corporate moral identity rather than individual creative capacity. Noted.

**[CHAR-16]** S — The silence on the creative faculty is consistent with the characteristic's focus on constituted moral identity (who the person is) rather than creative production (what the person makes). The sinner-identity is received or formed, not created. Noted.

**[CHAR-17]** S — The silence is consistent with the characteristic's focus on the retrospective (backward-looking) conscience-recognition of past violation rather than the forward-looking creative faculty. Guilt-as-inner-state looks backward at what was done; creativity looks forward toward what might be made. Noted.

**[CHAR-18]** S — The silence is consistent with CHAR-18's backward-looking nature: the characteristic is the accumulated record of what has been done rather than the forward-looking creative generation of what might be. Noted.

**[CHAR-19]** S — The silence on the creative faculty is consistent with CHAR-19's constitutive volitional nature: the characteristic is defined by the will's act of crossing a given boundary rather than the creative generation of new boundaries or possibilities. Noted.

**[CHAR-2]** S — The silence on creative-faculty engagement is consistent with the characteristic's nature: unintentional sinning is not a creative act. It arises from the absence of knowledge rather than from the active exercise of any faculty. The silence is expected.

**[CHAR-20]** S — The silence is consistent with CHAR-20's constitutively relational-covenantal nature: the characteristic is about the disposition within an existing bond, not creative generation of new realities. Noted.

**[CHAR-21]** E — The creative pattern reveals a significant distinction from CHAR-20 (faithlessness) and CHAR-19 (transgression): CHAR-21 is the only M10 characteristic studied that explicitly evidences engagement of the creative-devising faculty. Pro 6:14's "perverted heart devises evil continually" names the creative capacity as captured by perversion. This confirms CHAR-21 as M10's characteristic of active inner distortion rather than passive failure — the perverted heart is not merely wrong but actively, creatively wrong.

**[CHAR-22]** E — The creative pattern confirms Psa 58:2's characterisation: injustice is not a passive failure but an active devising — the heart creatively plans wrong before the hands enact it. Psa 64:6's "diligent search" for injustice names the systematic, analytical effort the unjust person invests in finding opportunities. This active-creative wrongdoing dimension distinguishes CHAR-22 from accidental or negligent wrong: the unjust person is a creative agent of planned wrongdoing.
**[CHAR-3]** S — The silence on creative-faculty engagement is consistent with confession's retrospective naming structure. This prompt is closed.
**[CHAR-4]** S — The silence is consistent with conscience suppression's nature as a failure-mode characteristic. This prompt is closed.
**[CHAR-5]** S — The silence is consistent with the characteristic's nature as a volitional-dispositional phenomenon. This prompt is closed.
**[CHAR-6]** S — The silence is consistent with the characteristic's dispositional nature. This prompt is closed.

**[CHAR-7]** E — The creative-faculty pattern reveals that contagious sin captures and deploys the image's creative capacity for structural sinning: the same capacity to build worship structures that was designed for God-directed worship is redirected to construct sinning-transmission vehicles (high places, altars). This is consistent with CHAR-7's broader pattern of image-capacity inversion: authority, creativity, memory — all designed for God-oriented community formation — are captured by the sinning pattern and deployed in its service.

**[CHAR-8]** E — The creative pattern reveals that political revolt is not only destructive (breaking the prior relationship) but constructive: the revolting community creates new political structures as the positive assertion of independence (2Ki 8:20). This constructive dimension distinguishes political revolt from mere non-compliance: revolt builds alternative governance, not merely refuses existing governance.

**[CHAR-9]** E — The creative pattern reveals that sinful speech can deploy the image's creative-speech capacity — the capacity to name, define, and declare — in the direction of false naming, false definition, and false declaration. This is the inversion of the image's designed creative-speech function: the image-bearer is designed to speak truth (including truth about God); sinful speech uses the same creative-speech capacity to speak falsehood (about God and persons).

**[CHAR-1]** E — The creative engagement pattern reveals that wickedness-as-settled-person-identity does not destroy the inner-being faculties — it subverts and redirects them. This is analytically important: the wicked person remains a fully equipped image-bearer in terms of faculty-presence (they can plan, reason, speak, desire, imagine) — but every faculty is oriented away from its designed end toward wickedness. The creative faculty's subversion into harm-planning confirms that wickedness is not a reduction of the person's inner capacities but a reorientation of them.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The creative engagement pattern reveals that evil as constitutional inner nature is not a passive absence of good — it is an active generating condition. The evil treasury (Mat 12:35 — VCG-03) is not empty but full, and the person actively draws from it. This confirms the characteristic as a structural source of active evil production, not merely a deficiency. The creative pattern also reveals why the NT's remedial commands focus on filling and renewal rather than merely emptying: Jam 1:21 (vc=14368 — VCG-05) calls for receiving the implanted word — the creative faculty needs a new treasury to draw from, not merely the old one removed.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The creative pattern reveals the characteristic as particularly threatening in the social sphere because the creative faculty is deployed to mask and perpetuate it. Pro 26:25 (vc=1694 — VCG-02) shows that the person with seven abominations in their heart can generate gracious and convincing social performance — the creative faculty is the tool of concealment. This explains the emphasis on divine perception penetrating social performance: Luk 16:15 (vc=21 — VCG-02): "God knows your hearts" — the divine faculty sees through the creative social construct to the abominable inner condition beneath.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The creative pattern reveals that idolatrous abomination co-opts human creative capacity as the vehicle through which false devotion is embodied. The idol is not a discovery but a creation — it is made (Eze 7:20 — VCG-05; crafted from materials). This means the characteristic redirects the image-bearing creativity that should produce images of God's glory toward the production of rival god-images. The pattern confirms that idolatrous abomination is not a passive deficiency but an active creative project — the inner attachment to idols expresses itself through the creative construction of the objects of devotion.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The creative pattern reveals that iniquity as active scheming specifically requires and deploys the creative faculty — the characteristic is not merely passive or reactive but generatively productive. The birth metaphor (Psa 7:14 — VCG-02; Job 15:35 — VCG-02) positions the characteristic as the output of a creative inner process. This makes iniquity-as-scheming distinctively different from moral failure through weakness or impulse: it involves sustained, creative, premeditated inner activity. The creative pattern reveals the characteristic as an anti-creation: the image-bearing creative capacity redirected from good generation to harm generation.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The creative pattern reveals a distinction within the characteristic's three registers. VCG-02/03's false-attribution and false-charge modes engage the creative faculty through verbal construction of misrepresentations (Rom 3:8 — VCG-02; Joh 18:30 — VCG-03). VCG-01's direct blasphemy mode bypasses elaborate creative construction — the defiant cursing (Rev 16:9/11/21 — VCG-01) is direct, unelaborate hostile speech. The creative engagement pattern thus reveals that false accusation and defamation (VCG-02/03) require creative verbal fabrication, while direct hardened-will blasphemy (VCG-01) is more raw and immediate.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's creative pattern confirms Char 5's T3.5.3 finding at cluster scope: M10b inner evil is an anti-creation — the image-bearing creative capacity redirected from good generation to harm generation. The six creative modes (Char 1: devising evil plans; Char 2: constituting an evil inner nature; Char 3: hidden corrupt motivations behind smooth performance; Char 4: crafting idol-objects; Char 5: scheming evil schemes; Char 6: fabricating false charges) together constitute a comprehensive anti-creative profile — the six faces of the image-bearer's creative capacity corrupted.

**[CHAR-1]** S — The silence on creativity reveals that the characteristic belongs to the domain of normative regulation rather than imaginative origination. The defilement-state is managed through prescribed, structured responses — there is no latitude for creative improvisation in its handling. This reveals the characteristic as a condition embedded in law and covenant structure, not in the open domain of the creative faculty.

**[CHAR-2]** S — The silence on creativity reveals that the characteristic operates primarily in the moral-volitional-desiderative domain rather than the imaginative. Its impact is on the inner faculties of willing, desiring, conscience-forming, and moral evaluation — not on the constructive or imaginative capacities.

**[CHAR-3]** S — The silence on creativity reveals the characteristic as operating in the domain of moral-covenantal conduct and its consequences for sacred environments rather than in the generative-imaginative domain. The characteristic's inner-being engagement is with the will's fidelity or betrayal, not with the imaginative or creative capacity.

**[CHAR-4]** S — The silence confirms the characteristic as operating in the domain of will, faculty-suppression, and bodily domination rather than in the generative-imaginative domain. The characteristic suppresses existing faculties rather than corrupting the creative capacity.

**[CLUSTER]** S — The uniform silence across all four characteristics reveals that the M10c defilement domain operates in a domain that does not intersect the creative faculty. This is analytically significant: defilement impairs and distorts the person's relationship to their own inner life, but not through the creative-imaginative dimension. The cluster's concern is with conditions and their management (Char 1), the suppression of moral faculties (Chars 2, 3), and the suppression of bodily-spiritual integrity (Chars 3, 4) — all of which are distinct from the creative imagination. This contrasts the M10c cluster with clusters that engage the creative-imaginative faculty (such as wisdom or prophecy clusters) and confirms M10c as a moral-constitutional domain.

findings.session_b_note:
Yes — volition is the **primary faculty** engaged by forgiveness at the human exercise level. The evidence is extensive:

**Forgiveness as commanded volitional act:**
- Luk 17:3-4 — "you must forgive him." The command structure addresses the will directly and unambiguously.
- Mat 18:35 — "from your heart" — the heart-locus names the volitional centre. Forgiveness is commanded as achievable — commands address the faculty that can comply.
- Mar 11:25 — "whenever you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against anyone." The ongoing volitional obligation: every prayer context is an occasion to choose forgiveness.

**Forgiveness as volitional release:**
- OBS-064-026: "The inner-being act in both cases [forgiveness and discipleship-leaving] is a volitional release — choosing to no longer hold a legitimate claim."
- The debt-cancellation language of Mat 18 frames the act as a decision to absorb the cost rather than extract payment — a volitional choice with real cost.

**The will's four modes in relation to forgiveness** (Q032 answer):
- **Imposed** — God declares forgiveness without the person seeking it (Luk 7:47-48)
- **Invited** — access-postures name the conditions through which the will orients to receive
- **Enabled** — received forgiveness transforms the volitional orientation (love produced)
- **Required** — human forgiveness is commanded; the will is required to act

findings.session_b_note:
Yes — the volitional faculty is engaged at two distinct points in compassion's constitutional movement, and in opposite directions depending on context.

**Volition as the suppressor of compassion (judicial contexts):** The chus vocabulary — "your eye shall not pity" (Deut 19:13; Ezek 7:4) — addresses the will directly. The compassion-impulse arises from perception; the will can then override it in contexts where judicial requirements demand non-pity. This is volition engaged against compassion: the capacity to choose suppresses the natural arising impulse. The fact that judicial prohibitions must be stated — "shall not pity" — reveals that the volitional suppression of compassion is not automatic; it requires a deliberate inner act.

**Volition as the executor of compassion (action contexts):** In the Synoptic pattern, the splanchnizō-movement produces volitional engagement in the service of compassion: "stretched out his hand" (Mark 1:41), "touched their eyes" (Matt 20:34). The will acts on the compassion-movement — choosing to cross boundaries, extend help, or initiate action. The volitional faculty here translates the affective stirring into directed action.

**The divine inner deliberation (Hos 11:8):** The divine heart recoiling and compassion warming in Hos 11:8 is presented as a volitional contest — compassion competing with judgment for the outcome of the divine will. Compassion wins; judgment is overridden. This is the most complex volitional engagement in the data: not suppression of compassion by will, and not simple execution of compassion through will, but a genuine deliberative resolution in which compassion determines the volitional outcome.

findings.session_b_note:
Yes — volition is engaged in a distinctive and analytically important way. The vocabulary contains a specifically volitional form: H1792 da.kha in the Hithpael ("to allow oneself to be crushed") — a reflexive-permissive form noted in OBS-030-007 and OBS-030-008. This verbal form implies a volitional dimension: the possibility of permitting or refusing the crushing rather than merely receiving it passively.

The evidence also shows volition engaged at the point of resistance: Jer 44:10 — "they have not humbled themselves" — implies that humbling is a volitional act that has been refused. The contrite posture is not purely automatic — it requires a volitional orientation of non-resistance (allowing oneself to be brought low).

Additionally, Psa 51:17 — the broken and contrite heart offered as sacrifice — implies a volitional bringing of the inner state before God: the person brings their broken heart as an offering. This is a voluntary act even from a broken condition.

Yes — volition is engaged in a distinctive and analytically important way. The vocabulary contains a specifically volitional form: H1792 da.kha in the Hithpael ("to allow oneself to be crushed") — a reflexive-permissive form noted in OBS-030-007 and OBS-030-008. This verbal form implies a volitional dimension: the possibility of permitting or refusing the crushing rather than merely receiving it passively.

The evidence also shows volition engaged at the point of resistance: Jer 44:10 — "they have not humbled themselves" — implies that humbling is a volitional act that has been refused. The contrite posture is not purely automatic — it requires a volitional orientation of non-resistance (allowing oneself to be brought low).

Additionally, Psa 51:17 — the broken and contrite heart offered as sacrifice — implies a volitional bringing of the inner state before God: the person brings their broken heart as an offering. This is a voluntary act even from a broken condition.

findings.session_b_note:
Yes. Volition is centrally engaged in fellowship's operation.

**Choice of fellowship object:** Psa 119:63 — *I am a companion of all who fear you* — the psalmist's companionship is an explicit volitional choice: he has *chosen* those who fear God and keep God's precepts as his companions. The volitional act of choosing the fellowship object is the foundational act of righteous fellowship.

**Choice of wrong fellowship:** Mat 23:30 — the Pharisees' hypothetical claim involves volitional counterfactual reasoning about what they *would have* chosen. Moral complicity through fellowship is traced to volitional alignment.

**Refusal of incompatible fellowship:** 2Cor 6:14 — the command *do not be unequally yoked* is addressed to the volitional capacity: the person must choose not to enter incompatible fellowship. The command presupposes that the person has the volitional capacity to refuse.

**Idolatrous joining as volitional misdirection:** Hos 4:17 — *Ephraim is joined to idols* — finding 062-GROUN-001 and the group description identify this as volitional inner joining. The will is turned toward the wrong object.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-067-003: T3 reveals that goodness is the most comprehensively faculty-engaging characteristic in the programme's current analytical record. Every faculty except creativity (T3.5 — silence confirmed) shows subs…
findings.finding_value: T3 reveals that goodness is the most comprehensively faculty-engaging characteristic in the programme's current analytical record. Every faculty except creativity (T3.5 — silence confirmed) shows substantive engagement: perception (tasting and seeing goodness), cognition (moral evaluation and ranking), memory (covenantal knowing and moral reckoning), affect (stable rooted gladness vs fragile surface gladness), volition (reconstituted toward the good), agency (active expression required and enabled), moral evaluation (goodness as the normative anchor of the evaluative faculty), conscience (goodness calibrates the conscience's standard), conscientiousness (integration of all faculties into sustained moral expression), and relational capacity (dual-directional overflow). The tier as a whole reveals that goodness is not a specialist characteristic — it is an integrating one. The person who possesses genuine goodness has every faculty engaged and aligned. This comprehensive faculty-engagement is what distinguishes genuine goodness from its surface forms: surface goodness (the Haman problem) engages affect without engaging conscience or volitional alignment; genuine goodness integrates all.

findings.finding_value: T3 shows mercy activating the full faculty system (perception, cognition, memory, affect, volition, agency, moral evaluation, conscience, conscientiousness, relational capacity) and T4 shows mercy operating across three relational directions (God→human, human→God, human→human). Reading together: the faculty activations in T3 are the inner capacities that each T4 relational direction requires. God→human mercy (T4.1) engages mercy's receptive faculty complex — conscience, moral evaluation, affect, memory (asymmetric structure). Human→God mercy (T4.2 — mercy-seeking) engages volition, agency, affect, conscience, and perception (face-toward-God). Human→human mercy (T4.3) engages moral evaluation, agency, volition, and relational capacity. The three relational directions of T4 are served by the specific faculty subsets activated in T3.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-030-003: Reading T3 as a whole reveals that contrition engages virtually every inner faculty — with one exception (creativity, T3.5 — data silent). The pattern across the engaged faculties is consistent: contr…
findings.finding_value: Reading T3 as a whole reveals that contrition engages virtually every inner faculty — with one exception (creativity, T3.5 — data silent). The pattern across the engaged faculties is consistent: contrition deepens and opens rather than impairs or bypasses. It deepens perception (opens to divine address), deepens cognition (enables accurate self-knowledge), deepens affect (makes grief and longing both fuller), redirects volition (from self-assertion to God-direction), converts agency (from self-directed to God-seeking), deepens moral evaluation (requires and enables accurate self-assessment), deepens conscience (allows conscience's verdict to reach the spirit/heart), deepens conscientiousness (grounds it in inner reality rather than performance), and enables relational capacity (specifically for divine nearness). The single thread running through all faculty engagements is: contrition removes self-protective barriers — it is the inner-being event in which every protective reflex is dissolved, leaving the person fully exposed and open. This is why it enables rather than impairs every faculty: openness is the condition in which all faculties function most truthfully.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-030-019: The faculty tier (T3) establishes that contrition opens every engaged faculty toward God (perception deepened for divine address, volition redirected toward God, agency converted to God-seeking, relat…
findings.finding_value: The faculty tier (T3) establishes that contrition opens every engaged faculty toward God (perception deepened for divine address, volition redirected toward God, agency converted to God-seeking, relational capacity enabled for divine nearness); the relational tier (T4) shows that the primary relational direction is indeed toward God. T3 and T4 are aligned: the faculty effects all point in the same direction that T4's relational analysis names as the primary direction. The faculties do not pull in multiple directions — they converge on the vertical relational axis. This convergence is analytically significant: it means contrition is constitutively God-directed at the faculty level, not merely structurally positioned toward God.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-030-020: The faculty tier (T3) shows that contrition deepens every faculty without impairing any; the formative tier (T5) shows that this deepening accumulates into settled character over time. T3's snapshot (…
findings.finding_value: The faculty tier (T3) shows that contrition deepens every faculty without impairing any; the formative tier (T5) shows that this deepening accumulates into settled character over time. T3's snapshot (what contrition does to the faculties in the moment) and T5's longitudinal account (what repeated contrition produces in the person over time) together yield a complete picture: the opening of perception, cognition, affect, volition, agency, conscience, conscientiousness, and relational capacity that contrition produces in the moment (T3) becomes, through repetition, the settled character of the person who habitually trembles at God's word (T5 — Isa 66:2). The character of lowliness is the long-term form of the faculty-opening that contrition produces in the short term.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-030-021: The faculty tier (T3) establishes that contrition deepens the perceptive capacity for divine address and opens the conscience to receive its verdict; the structural relationships tier (T6) shows that …
findings.finding_value: The faculty tier (T3) establishes that contrition deepens the perceptive capacity for divine address and opens the conscience to receive its verdict; the structural relationships tier (T6) shows that contrition consistently co-occurs with fear (R061 — trembling at God's word) and is causally related to it (Isa 66:2). The faculty engagement (T3) explains the co-occurrence (T6): contrition opens the person to divine address (T3.1) and this openness to divine word is what fear of God (trembling at God's word) also names — they are the same inner orientation named from different perspectives. T3's faculty account of contrition's perceptive opening and T6's co-occurrence data for fear (R061) are mutually explanatory.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-062-003: Reading T3 as a whole reveals that every faculty engagement with fellowship runs in both directions — right fellowship deepens and enables; wrong fellowship degrades and constrains. Perception, cognit…
findings.finding_value: Reading T3 as a whole reveals that every faculty engagement with fellowship runs in both directions — right fellowship deepens and enables; wrong fellowship degrades and constrains. Perception, cognition, moral evaluation, conscience, conscientiousness, and relational capacity are all deepened by rightly directed fellowship and progressively impaired by wrongly directed fellowship. The single exception is creativity (T3.5 — data silent). The pattern is systematic: fellowship is not merely a relational characteristic but a faculty-shaping characteristic — it progressively shapes every inner faculty in conformity with its object. This makes the choice of fellowship objects one of the most consequential inner-being decisions a person makes: the consequences extend through every faculty across time.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-062-009: T1 establishes that fellowship is object-determined and progressively constitutional; T3 shows that fellowship shapes every inner faculty in conformity with its object. These are two descriptions of t…
findings.finding_value: T1 establishes that fellowship is object-determined and progressively constitutional; T3 shows that fellowship shapes every inner faculty in conformity with its object. These are two descriptions of the same reality: "object determines character" (T1) is the principle; "every faculty shaped by fellowship direction" (T3) is the mechanism. The five-mode structure (T1) explains why T3 finds diverse faculty effects: existential mode primarily engages affect and relational capacity; companionship mode primarily engages volition, moral evaluation, and conscientiousness; suffering mode primarily engages affect and agency; ontological mode primarily engages relational capacity at its deepest level.

The soul-level (T2.2 — Ecc 9:4) corresponds to T3.4 affect — the existential fellowship produces hope as an affective state at the soul level. Perception, volition, moral evaluation, conscientiousness, and relational capacity are all deepened when directed toward the right fellowship object (God and God-fearers). T3's bilateral finding (right fellowship deepens; wrong fellowship degrades) explains T4's structural negative (misdirected fellowship is more dangerous than absence — Hos 4:17, Mat 23:30): when every faculty is progressively shaped by the fellowship object, misdirected fellowship progressively degrades every faculty, not just the relational capacity.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-062-020: T3's snapshot (what fellowship does to faculties in the moment) and T5's longitudinal account (what habitual fellowship produces over time) together reveal that faculty deepening (T3) is the process o…
findings.finding_value: T3's snapshot (what fellowship does to faculties in the moment) and T5's longitudinal account (what habitual fellowship produces over time) together reveal that faculty deepening (T3) is the process of which constitutional character formation (T5) is the endpoint. The right-direction faculty deepening (T3 — perception, cognition, conscience, moral evaluation each deepened by right fellowship) accumulates over time into the fixed character of Psa 119:63's declared God-fearer companion, which is on its way to Jer 13:23's constitutional formation. T3 → T5 is the moment-to-character arc.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-062-021: T3's moral evaluation and conscience faculty engagements explain the co-occurrence pattern with desire (R43) in T6. Desire (R43) directs fellowship; conscience assesses the moral quality of the fellow…
findings.finding_value: T3's moral evaluation and conscience faculty engagements explain the co-occurrence pattern with desire (R43) in T6. Desire (R43) directs fellowship; conscience assesses the moral quality of the fellowship object; moral evaluation confirms or challenges the direction. The three characteristics (desire, fellowship, conscience) operate in sequence: desire directs → conscience evaluates → fellowship forms. The T6 co-occurrence signal between R43 and R062 is the shared-verse evidence of this sequential relationship that T3's faculty analysis illuminates.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-062-022: T7's literary forms explain why T3 finds different faculty engagements in different evidential contexts. The wisdom poetry setting (Psa 119:63, Jer 13:23, Ecc 9:4) engages primarily the volitional, co…
findings.finding_value: T7's literary forms explain why T3 finds different faculty engagements in different evidential contexts. The wisdom poetry setting (Psa 119:63, Jer 13:23, Ecc 9:4) engages primarily the volitional, conscientiousness, and moral evaluation faculties. The apostolic epistolary setting (Phili 3:10, 2Cor 1:7, 2Pe 1:4, 1Jo 1:3) engages primarily the relational capacity, affect, and agency faculties. The prophetic setting (Hos 4:17, Isa 53:5, Jer 13:23) engages primarily the moral evaluation and conscience faculties (diagnostic-corrective function). Literary form determines which faculty register the fellowship vocabulary is deployed in.
