findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-003: T3 reveals two structurally distinctive findings about compassion's faculty engagement. First, creativity is entirely silent (three S ratings) — the most informative absence in the tier: compassion re…
findings.finding_value: T3 reveals two structurally distinctive findings about compassion's faculty engagement. First, creativity is entirely silent (three S ratings) — the most informative absence in the tier: compassion responds, it does not originate or create. It is the most responsive of the faculties-engaging characteristics. Second, affect and moral action are structurally unified in compassion — not sequentially related but simultaneous. Affect is the mechanism of movement (splanchnizō is both the felt inner event and the cause of the action), not a precursor or accompaniment. This is unique among the characteristics reviewed: in most other registries, affect and volition are distinguishable stages; in compassion, the felt movement is already the morally motivated action beginning. A third distinctive finding: compassion converts moral knowledge into motivated action — it is the motivational ground of conscientiousness, not a product of it. The conscience faculty engagement reveals compassion as conscience-healing: it addresses the pitiable condition that conscience perceives as a moral claim, resolving the tension between moral knowledge and moral incapacity. The three relational modes (building/sustaining — chesed; restoring/repairing — splanchnizō; extending across difference — Good Samaritan) are a new finding not in the instruction typology.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-009: T1's four kinds explain T3's most distinctive finding: that affect and moral action are structurally unified rather than sequential. In T1 terms, compassion-as-inner-event (splanchnizō) and compassion…
findings.finding_value: T1's four kinds explain T3's most distinctive finding: that affect and moral action are structurally unified rather than sequential. In T1 terms, compassion-as-inner-event (splanchnizō) and compassion-as-externalised-act are not two separate kinds but a continuous movement — the felt-movement is the beginning of the act. T3 confirms this: affect is the mechanism of movement, not its precursor. T1's finding that compassion converts moral knowledge into motivated action (the unique position as motivational ground of conscientiousness) maps onto T3.10's finding of the same: the definitional claim (T1) that compassion is constitutively outward-facing explains T3's finding that it is the driving faculty between moral knowledge and moral action.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-014: T2's four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) maps directly onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The somatic-arousal s…
findings.finding_value: T2's four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) maps directly onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The somatic-arousal stage (T2.6 — gut stirring, splanchnizō) corresponds to T3.1's perceptive-trigger stage (sight activates the somatic response) and T3.4's affect stage (the stirring is the affective movement). The soul-engagement stage (T2.2 — chesed as soul-character) corresponds to T3.8 moral evaluation (the soul assesses the need) and T3.9 conscience (the conscience activates the response). The volitional-engagement stage (T2.3 — heart-locus as deliberative site) corresponds to T3.6 volition (the will directs the action). The outward-action stage corresponds to T3.7 agency. T2 and T3 describe the same movement sequence from two perspectives: T2 maps the constitutional levels; T3 maps the faculties active at each level.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-020: T3's affect-moral-action unity (affect is the mechanism, not the precursor) and T5's formation finding (compassion is simultaneously character target and motivational ground) are structurally connecte…
findings.finding_value: T3's affect-moral-action unity (affect is the mechanism, not the precursor) and T5's formation finding (compassion is simultaneously character target and motivational ground) are structurally connected. T5 names compassion as the motivational ground that makes the sanctification arc survivable through failure and return — but T3 has already established that affect is the mechanism of this motivational ground: the character formation that T5 describes is accomplished through the affective mechanism that T3 identifies. The person who is formed into compassionate character (T5) is the person whose affective faculty has been trained to respond immediately and morally to perceived suffering (T3). T3's finding that affect and moral action are unified is T5's mechanism of formation: the person becoming compassionate is the person in whom the affective-moral unity is deepening and stabilising.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-003: T3 produces four structurally significant findings about grace's faculty engagement. First, grace is agency-constituting rather than agency-replacing: 1Cor 15:10 holds in explicit paradox — "I worked …
findings.finding_value: T3 produces four structurally significant findings about grace's faculty engagement. First, grace is agency-constituting rather than agency-replacing: 1Cor 15:10 holds in explicit paradox — "I worked harder than any of them, though it was not I but the grace of God that is with me." Agency is not displaced but constituted by grace. This relationship holds in paradox that the T3.6 prompt options (enable/deepen/bypass/impair) cannot accommodate — a prompt design limitation noted for catalogue revision. Second, grace produces moral clarity (T3.8 — sharpens moral evaluation rather than bypassing it): the person who recognises grace has made a precise moral evaluation (they know they received what they did not deserve). Third, grace and conscience are mutually necessary: grace is the condition within which conscience can operate fully without destroying the person; conscience without grace produces condemnation; grace without conscience produces presumption (T3.9). Fourth, grace is the primary relational faculty developer in the registry's evidence — it reaches every relational register (vertical access, horizontal forgiving, speech-grace) and enables each one. Creativity (T3.5) is the one genuinely silent faculty — not an impairment but a non-engagement: grace receives and constitutes, it does not create.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-009: T1's immediate response pattern (fear → mourning → prostration as the creaturely recognition response) is the affective-volitional expression of T3's faculty engagement at the moment grace arrives. T3…
findings.finding_value: T1's immediate response pattern (fear → mourning → prostration as the creaturely recognition response) is the affective-volitional expression of T3's faculty engagement at the moment grace arrives. T3.4 (affect is the first named faculty engaged by grace) and T3.6 (the agency-constituting paradox of 1Cor 15:10) together explain why T1.5 finds the creaturely recognition response before positive states settle: grace first produces the affective recognition (fear, mourning) before constituting the agency through which the person responds (prostration as the body enacting the inner posture that grace has produced). T1's finding that grace requires creaturely recognition to complete its operation (T1.7) is T3.1's finding at the faculty level: grace requires and enables perception simultaneously.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-014: T2's constitutional movement (spirit reception → soul standing → capacity → character expression) maps onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The spirit-reception stage (T2.1) corresponds to T3.1 (per…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional movement (spirit reception → soul standing → capacity → character expression) maps onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The spirit-reception stage (T2.1) corresponds to T3.1 (perception — grace enabling the inner sight and hearing that receives it). The soul-standing stage (T2.2) corresponds to T3.9 (conscience — grace as the condition within which conscience can operate without destruction) and T3.8 (moral evaluation — the standing produces the clarity of moral self-assessment). The capacity-gifting stage (T2.1 — spirit level) corresponds to T3.7 (agency — capacity given constitutes agency for the task). The character-expression stage (T2.7 — outward through body-soul) corresponds to T3.10 (conscientiousness — the integrated moral-action expression of received grace-character). T2 maps the constitutional space; T3 maps the faculties active at each spatial level; the two tiers describe the same movement from orthogonal perspectives.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-019: T3's agency-constituting finding (grace constitutes rather than replaces agency — 1Cor 15:10) and T4's human-to-God direction (supplication as the human posture of appeal — requiring genuine human age…
findings.finding_value: T3's agency-constituting finding (grace constitutes rather than replaces agency — 1Cor 15:10) and T4's human-to-God direction (supplication as the human posture of appeal — requiring genuine human agency in the act of plea) are structurally aligned. The constituted agency (T3.7) is precisely the agency that supplication requires: the creature must genuinely appeal, not merely receive passively. T3's finding that grace and conscience are mutually necessary (T3.9) corresponds to T4's relational-access finding: grace transforms the threshold of human-to-God approach (prosagōgē — SD035) from impassable to open, which is the relational expression of T3.9's constitutional finding that grace creates the condition within which conscience can operate fully without destruction. T3 names the inner-being event; T4 names the relational consequence of the same event.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-020: T3's faculty findings are the synchronic expression of T5's diachronic formation arc. The creaturely recognition response (T5.2 — fear → mourning → prostration as the consistent transitional state in …
findings.finding_value: T3's faculty findings are the synchronic expression of T5's diachronic formation arc. The creaturely recognition response (T5.2 — fear → mourning → prostration as the consistent transitional state in all grace-sequences) is the affective-faculty event (T3.4) at the moment of grace-arrival, which then constitutes the volitional-faculty alignment (T3.6 — the agency-constituting paradox) that enables the conscientious expression (T3.10). T5's formation arc (sustained work producing character-quality) is the longitudinal development of T3.9's finding (conscience operating fully within grace) into T3.10's finding (conscientiousness as the integrated moral character that grace constitutes over time). The person who has been formed by grace through the T5 formation arc is the person in whom T3's faculty engagements have been progressively deepened and integrated.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-022: T3's faculty findings are grounded in and confirmed by T7's primary anchor evidence. The perceptive-faculty finding (T3.1 — grace requires and enables perception) is grounded in the eye-formula of che…
findings.finding_value: T3's faculty findings are grounded in and confirmed by T7's primary anchor evidence. The perceptive-faculty finding (T3.1 — grace requires and enables perception) is grounded in the eye-formula of chen (SD041), Zec 12:10's grace-produced vision, and SD012's hearing-receptivity pattern. T7's argument structure for Zec 12:10 (grace outpoured → "when they look on me, on him whom they have pierced") confirms T3.1 precisely: the grace-event produces and requires the inner sight that recognises what grace has cost. T3.6's agency-constituting paradox (1Cor 15:10) is T7.3's most significant framework-divergence point: at the moment of constitutional incapacity, all human science frameworks assume the person has some prior agency; the biblical account holds the paradox of grace-constituted agency that is genuinely human while grace-originated. This is the methodological divergence T7.3 identifies and T3.6 establishes as the operative finding.

findings.session_b_note: The evidence shows both enabling and bypass, in different covenantal modes. Enabling: the Sinai covenant engages and calls for volition — the bilateral covenant structure requires human volitional response. Covenant gives the person something to commit to, a concrete object for volitional commitment. The moral weight of covenant (oath/curse structure — OBS-034-007) makes the volitional act serious and binding. Bypass (in a specific sense): the new covenant does not wait for the person's volitional transformation but produces it — God writes the law on the heart (Jer 31:33) and administers through the Spirit (2 Cor 3:6). This is not bypassing volition in the sense of overriding it, but operating at a constitutional depth that transforms the volitional faculty from within rather than calling for its exercise from without. The new covenant produces willingness rather than demanding it — "I will be their God and they shall be my people" is a relational promise, not a conditional demand. Gal 4:24 (OBS-034-071): the Sinai covenant produces children for bondage — constrained volition; the new covenant produces free children — liberated volition. The new covenant thus enables and liberates volition at a deeper constitutional level than the old.

findings.session_b_note: Peace both requires and enables volition: (1) Requires volition: the pursuit of peace (Psa 34:14), the choice to be at peace with others (Rom 12:18 — G1514), the volitional orientation of the mind toward God (Isa 26:3) — all are deliberate acts of will; (2) Enables volition: the quieted person is in a better position to choose rightly — H2790B group 408-001 (holding silence under emotional provocation) shows peace-as-restraint enabling volition over impulse; H2814 group 409-004 (prophetic inner resolve, refusing silence for God's purposes) shows the person of peace being more decisively volitional, not less; (3) False peace bypasses true volition: Deu 29:19 — the self-deceived person's volitional claim ("I shall be safe") is not a genuine act of will directed toward peace but a bypass of the real volitional cost of covenant faithfulness. Peace-bearing volition is the will rightly informed and directed; false peace is the will disengaged from reality.

findings.finding_value: T3's faculty findings and T5's developmental findings illuminate each other. Memory (T3.3) connects to T5's sequence finding: the Lam 3 pathway (peaceless → remember → hope → wait) uses memory as the specific faculty through which the peaceless person recovers peace. Volition (T3.6) connects to T5's mechanism: the deliberate re-direction of the mind (Isa 26:3) is both a volitional act (T3.6) and the cognitive-orientation mechanism (T5.3) by which peace is received. Conscience (T3.9) connects to T5's transformation: the confession that exercises conscience (T3.9) is simultaneously the mechanism (T5.3) by which the suppressed-conscience peacelessness is resolved. Each faculty engagement is also a developmental mechanism.

findings.finding_value: T3's volitional finding (peace is chosen and refused, T3.6) connects to T6's causal sequences (trust → peace, T6.2) — trust is the volitional act that enables the causal chain; the refusal of peace (Isa 30:15) is the volitional act that interrupts it. T3's conscience-gateway finding (T3.9) connects to T6's peace-is-produced-by findings (T6.3.2 — confession produces peace) — conscience exercise is the specific faculty engagement that makes the Psa 32 causal sequence possible. T3's moral evaluation finding (T3.8 — authentic peace enables right judgment) connects to T6's shared anchor Isa 59:8 (the way of peace they do not know) — the morally disordered person cannot find the peace-way because moral disorder corrupts the evaluative faculty.

findings.session_b_note: The characteristic deepens volition in its human expression (Jobs 1:21, Isa 50:6) — the act of self-giving under loss or suffering represents a deepened volitional capacity, not a constrained one. The Servant's giving of himself (Isa 50:6) is freely chosen. For divine volition: Hos 11:8 shows divine volition under constraint from within — the compassion constrains the judicial will, producing the restraint of giving-over. This is not impairment of divine volition but its full expression through the integration of affective-volitional movement. In the receiving direction: the imperative to give glory (Jer 13:16) presupposes full volitional capacity in the human — the command would be meaningless if volition were bypassed. The characteristic neither bypasses nor impairs human volition; it calls it forth and elevates it.

Enables a specific volitional direction — away from the despised object — while closing off the volitional response of compliance and obedience. Contempt de-obligates the will from the claims of what has been despised.
Organises the will toward separation (righteous form) or toward the destruction of what is good (inverted form). The volitional impact follows the direction of the abhorrence.
Enables destructive agency without restraint. The characteristic removes the volitional brakes that fear of God and mercy would have applied.

Drives urgency and active resistance. The adversary relationship demands volitional response.
Organises the will toward purposive destruction of the other, sustained across time ("never-ending").

Volition is engaged across all seven sub-groups, making it the most universally engaged inner faculty in M05. The cluster's characteristics are not merely felt or perceived but consistently require volitional engagement — they must be chosen, maintained, practiced, and directed. The one significant variation is M05-B (compassion), where the primary stirring is pre-volitional (the visceral trigger precedes deliberation), though volition is engaged in the judicial-withholding register. The cluster as a whole requires the will — these characteristics cannot be merely passive. This is one of M05's most important faculty findings: love, compassion, mercy, goodness, gentleness, comfort, and fellowship are all volitional commitments, not only experiential states.

**[CLUSTER]** E. Righteousness enables and empowers volition by clarifying what the right choice is and providing the inner resources (faith, hope, love of righteousness) to make it. Justification (C) creates the freedom in which volition can be exercised toward God rather than away from him. Wickedness impairs volition progressively: the hardened heart is less and less capable of repentance (Rom 2:5) — the volitional capacity atrophies under sustained wickedness.
All three: volitionally received (the person who asks — Jas 1:5), maintained (the wise person who accumulates and guards), refused (the person who rejects wisdom's call — Pro 1:24-33).

findings.finding_value: Transforms from inside: Phili 2:13 is unique in the programme's data — grace does not merely constrain or direct volition from outside but works inside the will. The grace-characteristic does not bypass the will (as compulsion would) but reconstitutes it. The person who "became obedient from the heart" (Rom 6:17) has a will that has been transformed by grace, not overridden. Grace expands volitional capacity by aligning it with what is genuinely good.

findings.finding_value: M01-A **enables and deepens** volition by aligning it with right action. Fear of God does not suppress the will but governs it toward wisdom, ethics, and covenant faithfulness. Pro 14:16 ("the wise person's reverential caution causes him to turn from evil — the inner quality is a wary, fear-informed prudence that **restrains reckless action**"). This is volition enabled and governed, not suppressed.

M01-B's acute fear and M01-C's terror **bypass** or **override** volition in many instances: 1Sa 17:24 (flight "without deliberation" — the will bypassed); Gen 35:5 (terror paralyzing the will — bypassed). But in some B instances, fear governs without bypassing: Mat 14:5 (Herod's social fear "restrained his will from executing John" — fear governing the will without bypassing it).

M01-B's acute fear and M01-C's terror **bypass** or **override** volition in many instances: 1Sa 17:24 (flight "without deliberation" — the will bypassed); Gen 35:5 (terror paralyzing the will — bypassed). But in some B instances, fear governs without bypassing: Mat 14:5 (Herod's social fear "restrained his will from executing John" — fear governing the will without bypassing it).

M01-D dismay **impairs and dissolves** volition: Eze 7:27 (hands paralyzed — volitional capacity physically disabled); Job 32:15 (friends speechless — the will to speak dissolved). Dismay is the sub-group most destructive of the volitional faculty.
M01-G timidity **impairs** volition by channelling it toward passive self-preservation. The will is not absent but misdirected — toward burying, hiding, and shrinking rather than action.

The pattern: M01-A enables/deepens volition (governance toward right action); M01-B and C bypass or override volition (urgency overwhelming deliberation); M01-D dissolves volition (hands paralyzed, speech gone); M01-G impairs volition (misdirection toward passivity). Ordered fear enriches volitional life; disordered fear degrades it.

Possessing rage bypasses deliberative volition: Dan 3:13 (M02-B-VCG-03) — "a sudden, imperious inner fire that bypasses deliberation and demands instant compliance." The will is overridden by the rage — the person acts without deliberate choice. Est 7:7 (M02-B-VCG-03) shows the king's wrath "driving him physically from the banquet" — the will is moved from the outside of itself by the anger's force.

Righteous anger enables and energises volition toward its proper target. Nehemiah's anger (Neh 5:6) enables decisive confrontation of exploitation — the anger provides the volitional energy that confronts what would otherwise be left unchallenged. Luk 15:28 (M02-B-VCG-02) shows the elder son's anger "paralysing his will — he refuses to enter" — the anger can also immobilise the will when it is resentment-driven.

Nehemiah's anger (Neh 5:6) enables decisive confrontation of exploitation — the anger provides the volitional energy that confronts what would otherwise be left unchallenged. Luk 15:28 (M02-B-VCG-02) shows the elder son's anger "paralysing his will — he refuses to enter" — the anger can also immobilise the will when it is resentment-driven.

Four patterns: (1) grief bypassing the will (overwhelming grief where the will is disabled — Zion's hands fall helpless under distress, Jer 4:31 — BOUNDARY); (2) grief failing to govern the will (Herod, the rich young man — M03-C-VCG-01); (3) grief reshaping the will through repentance (godly grief, M03-C-VCG-02); (4) grief activating the will toward God in prayer (M03-D-VCG-01, D-VCG-03). The characteristic's relationship with volition is therefore not simple: grief can strengthen or weaken the will depending on whether it is godly or worldly, acute or chronic, received or resisted.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Exultation both requires and strengthens volition. The commands require the will to engage; Hab 3:18 shows the will overriding adverse circumstances to choose exultation. The sustained orientation of Psa 89:16 ("all the day") shows a will that has been trained to maintain exultation as a standing posture.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Joy enables and strengthens volition by providing the inner motivation for action: 2Cor 8:2 (abundance of joy in poverty overflowing into generosity — Joy produces volitional giving); Neh 8:10 ("the joy of the Lord is your strength") — Joy enables the will's perseverance; Act 5:41 (apostles "rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer" — joy enabling volitional endurance under persecution). Joy does not bypass volition but works through it, providing the inner incentive for difficult volitional acts.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Suffering-Joy both requires and strengthens volition: the commands require the will to engage; the Spirit's enabling empowers the will to sustain what it cannot produce alone (Job's failed volitional attempt at ba.lag vs. the Spirit-enabled agalliao). Act 5:41 (apostles rejoicing → continuing to teach) shows Suffering-Joy enabling sustained volitional ministry despite ongoing opposition.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Gladness enables volition by providing the cognitive-evaluative framework within which good choices are made: the person who accurately evaluates what is genuinely good (M04-L-VCG-02) has the inner clarity needed for right volitional choices. Gladness does not bypass volition but informs it. The Proverbs evaluative corpus is essentially a guide to informed volition — knowing what is good (evaluative Gladness) enables choosing what is good (volition).

**[CHAR-4]** E — Delight is the primary shaper of volition in M04: (1) **Enables** — Psa 40:8 (Delight to do God's will enables willing obedience); Gen 34:19 (Delight driving immediate action — will energised by desire); (2) **Deepens** — God's sovereign cha.phets cannot be diverted or overridden (Psa 115:3; Isa 46:10) — perfect Delight produces perfect volitional consistency; the will shaped by Delight in God's law becomes a will that naturally chooses what it loves (Psa 1:2; 40:8); (3) **Distorts** — misdirected Delight drives the will toward wrong objects (Isa 65:12; 2Th 2:12 — the will shaped by pleasure in unrighteousness); desire without knowledge (Pro 19:2) shows Delight as a volitional driver that can produce disaster when unguided by wisdom.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Genuine Pleasure in wisdom and right worship enables volition by providing clear grounds for choosing what is genuinely good: Pro 16:24's gracious-word Pleasure enables the will to prefer gentle speech; the wisdom-comparative Pleasure enables the will to choose integrity over material abundance. Distorted Pleasure (Pro 7:18's a.las; Pro 9:17's stolen bread) bypasses and corrupts volition by making wrong choices feel pleasant.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Wonder-at-God enables volition by motivating action: Psa 119:129 ("your testimonies are wonderful; therefore my soul keeps them") — Wonder in God's word motivating the volitional act of keeping the testimonies; the wonderfulness of God's commands is what motivates obedience. Wonder-failure (Neh 9:17) leads to volitional rebellion — the absence of wonder removes the motivational ground for obedience.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's relationship to volition follows a consistent pattern: (1) **Enables and energises**: Delight (Char 4) is the primary volitional energiser — the will directed by Delight toward God's law enables natural, willing obedience; Psa 40:8's "I delight to do your will" is the fullest volitional integration in the cluster; (2) **Sustains and strengthens**: Joy (Char 2) — Neh 8:10 ("the joy of the Lord is your strength") — Joy sustains volitional perseverance; Suffering-Joy (Char 7) — Act 5:41 (apostles rejoicing → continuing to teach) shows Suffering-Joy enabling continued mission-agency; (3) **Provides motivational ground**: Wonder (Char 6) — Psa 119:129 ("your testimonies are wonderful; therefore my soul keeps them") — Wonder motivates obedience without requiring it to be merely duty; (4) **The most explicitly insistent commands** are in Suffering-Joy (Char 7) — the commands are most insistent precisely because the natural volitional response to suffering is grief rather than joy; the will must be most actively engaged precisely where the characteristic most requires Spirit-enabling.

**[CHAR-1]** E — In its acute received form, shame **impairs** volition by collapsing the person's inner resources for self-determination — the shamed person cannot act confidently, cannot lift the face, withdraws from social agency. In its corrective form, shame **enables** volition by clearing out false confidence and creating the space for genuine reorientation: 2Ch 30:15 — the shame-activated priests immediately consecrate themselves. In the voluntary-bearing mode, a strong will **overcomes** shame's impairing effect — Heb 12:2, Isa 50:7. The three possibilities (impaired by shame, enabled by corrective shame, overcoming shame through will) constitute the full volitional-shame relationship in the evidence.

**[CHAR-2]** E — CHAR-2 primarily impairs volition: the humiliated cannot return to public life (2Sa 10:5), cannot respond (Mat 22:12), retreat rather than advance. The enforced character of CHAR-2 is the primary volitional engagement — the person's will is not operative in the humiliation; it is done to them. The absence of the proper inner disposition of regard (entrepō evidence) shows that the failure of will to recognise proper standing enables CHAR-2 to become necessary.

---

**[CHAR-3]** E — VCG-01 active-dishonour is deeply volitional — it requires the willful act of refused-acknowledgment. "Willful inner refusal to acknowledge worth" (Pass A on Joh 8:49, vc=35000). The absent-regard of Luk 18:2/4 is a sustained volitional disposition. VCG-02 structural dishonour is less volitionally constituted — it arrives as assignment rather than choice.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — VCG-03 is most volitionally engaged: "rulers dearly love shame" (Hos 4:18) — the will has chosen dishonour as its object. Phili 3:19's "minds set on earthly things" — the will has oriented the evaluative faculty toward an earthly standard. Functioning CHAR-4 (VCG-01) requires the will's cooperation to renounce shameful ways (2Cor 4:2 — "we have renounced"). The volitional dimension is significant across all three VCGs.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — Volition is engaged in CHAR-5 through the contempt-er's willful act of dismissal (exoutheneō is consistently presented as a volitional disposition in its VCG-01 register — Luk 18:9: "trusted in themselves that they were righteous" and "treated others with contempt"). For the recipient, the will is engaged in the response: whether they retaliate (1Pe 3:9's temptation) or bless (1Pe 3:9's call). The decision to throw off the cloak (Mar 10:50) is a decisive volitional act of shame-identity abandonment.

---

**[CHAR-6]** E — Volition is CHAR-6's constituting faculty: the maintenance of innocence (Psa 73:13 — "I have kept my heart clean") is a volitional practice. The incapacity for innocence (Hos 8:5) is precisely a failure at the volitional level — the will's capacity for moral purity is so damaged by sustained idolatry that innocence-oriented choices are no longer possible. CHAR-6 is constituted by the will's sustained orientation toward moral cleanness and free-from-deliberate-wrongdoing choices.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — Volition is the decisive faculty across the entire cluster. Every M07 characteristic is ultimately determined at the level of the will: whether shame is received, resisted, borne, extended, maintained, or refused depends on the will's orientation. In Char 1: the will determines whether shame functions as wound, corrective, or borne-for-God's-sake — the voluntary-bearing of M07-A-VCG-03 (Isa 50:6-7; Heb 12:2) is the highest form of volitional agency in the shame-field. In Char 2: the will's failure to recognise proper standing enables CHAR-2 to become necessary. In Char 3: the will's refusal to acknowledge worth constitutes CHAR-3. In Char 4: the will's choice of standard (God or earthly things) determines whether the conscience functions or inverts. In Char 5: the will's disposition toward self-righteousness generates contempt; the will's orientation toward blessing rather than retaliation is the commanded response (1Pe 3:9). In Char 6: the will's sustained orientation toward moral cleanness constitutes innocence; its choice of idolatry destroys innocence-capacity (Hos 8:5). Cluster-level confirmation: the shame-field is primarily a volitional field — the will is the decisive faculty in determining where each characteristic lands.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — CHAR-1 does not impair will-capacity but misdirects it — amplifying the will's self-directed agency while systematically bypassing the constraints (divine authority, creaturely limits) under which the will properly operates. Dan 11:36 (vc=34235, M08-A1-VCG-02): "the king shall do as he wills" — CHAR-1 produces a will that acts without external constraint, a maximised volitional capacity unchecked by reverence or submission. Num 15:30 (vc=65731, M08-A4-VCG-05): acting "with a high hand... equivalent to reviling the Lord directly" — the will overrides divine command, removing the normative constraint under which it should operate. The interaction with other characteristics: CHAR-1's volitional amplification feeds into CHAR-2 (presumptuous defiance) and CHAR-3 (boasting) — the will energised by self-elevation generates both the defiant act and the verbal self-proclamation.

**[CHAR-2]** E — CHAR-2 amplifies and misdirects volition: it intensifies the will's self-directing capacity (the boiling energy of zid) while bypassing the constraints (divine authority, appointed human authority) under which the will properly operates. Deu 1:43 (vc=34123, M08-B-VCG-01): "you acted presumptuously and went up" — the will executes its own agenda despite divine prohibition. The will's capacity is not impaired; its constraints are removed. This produces a will of maximum self-assertive energy in minimum legitimate constraint.

**[CHAR-3]** E — CHAR-3's VCG-01 form is relatively unexamined volitionally — the self-directed boasting acts without the volitional self-discipline that VCG-02 names. VCG-02's examined discourse shows CHAR-3's impulse subjected to volitional discipline: Paul voluntarily restrains, redirects, and bounds his boasting (2Cor 10:13; Gal 6:14; 2Cor 12:9). VCG-03's God-directed boasting is a fully redirected volitional expression of the glorying-impulse. The volitional engagement is primarily in the disciplines applied to CHAR-3 rather than in the characteristic itself.

**[CHAR-4]** E — CHAR-4 misdirects volition through the inflated self-assessment that generates false confidence about one's own rights and freedoms. 1Cor 4:18 (vc=33938, M08-D-VCG-01): the puffed-up persons act on the presumption that Paul will not challenge them — their inflated cognitive picture generates a volitional posture of unchallenged freedom. 1Ti 6:4 (vc=33925, M08-D-VCG-02): "unhealthy craving for controversy" — the conceited person's will is directed toward intellectual combat as a form of self-validation. Volition is not impaired in capacity but misdirected through the inflated self-picture.

**[CHAR-5]** E — CHAR-5 amplifies volition in the direction of self-securing and self-assertive action: Eze 16:30 (vc=57959): shal.le.tet as "brazen, unrestrained" self-will — the structural power position enables the will to operate without the relational constraints that vulnerability would impose. Hab 2:9 (vc=34169): wilful accumulation of unjust gain to secure elevated position. CHAR-5 does not impair will-capacity but misdirects it toward the self-securing and self-exalting ends that structural power makes possible.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster comparison reveals a consistent pattern: M08 characteristics amplify or misdirect the volitional faculty rather than impairing it. CHAR-2 amplifies the will's self-authorising energy. CHAR-3's VCG-02 uniquely shows the volitional faculty disciplined — the examined-boasting discourse is the will's deliberate discipline of the boasting-impulse. CHAR-4 misdirects the will toward controversy-craving. CHAR-5 amplifies the will's reach through structural power. The cluster-synthesis: M08 is not a will-impairing cluster — it is a will-amplifying and will-misdirecting cluster. The volitional capacity is operating at full or even enhanced strength in all five characteristics; what is distorted is its direction (toward the self rather than toward God and others).

**[CHAR-2]** E — Submission *rightly orders and deepens* volition. The characteristic requires the will's own active engagement — "humble yourselves," "obey," "yield" — all address the will's capacity. The submission that produces pure-heart love (1Pe1:22) and sustained conscience-grounded character (Phili2:12) shows the will operating at its deepest and most self-directed level — not suppressed but oriented under legitimate authority. Rom6:16/17 reveals the most significant volitional insight: the will's habitual yielding determines whose servant one is — meaning the will is what is most at stake in submission. Genuine submission requires the will to be most fully engaged, not bypassed.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Contrition *rightly orders* the will by stripping the self-asserting, self-protective volitional orientation that prevents genuine openness to God. The crushed spirit (Psa34:18) is one whose will no longer asserts itself in proud self-sufficiency; the characteristic enables the will to be genuinely receptive rather than defensively closed. The reviving that follows (Isa57:15) produces a renewed volitional capacity that flows from the cleared ground of the contrite spirit.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Meekness/gentleness *rightly orders and expresses* volition. Metriopatheō enables the will to act proportionately rather than reactively — the measured quality requires the will to calibrate its response rather than defaulting to whatever impulse arises. Okneō (Act9:38) reveals the will's most freely-expressed quality: the will that does not generate inner friction or resistance when called to respond. Both aspects of the characteristic express the will at its most freely and proportionately functioning.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Semnotēs *orders and directs* volition toward settled, non-self-asserting expression. The characteristic provides the inner character-ground from which volitional choices about manner and comportment flow appropriately — the person of semnotēs makes choices about how they inhabit their roles from a settled inner quality rather than from anxious self-assertion. The characteristic enables volition to function from a grounded inner position rather than from insecure self-promotion.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Willing-heartedness *expresses and enables* the will at its most liberated. The freely-moved will (Exo35:5/22) is the will functioning at maximum voluntary freedom — not constrained, not compelled, but springing forward from genuine inner motivation. The characteristic enables volition to operate in its purest form: genuinely self-determined rather than externally-determined. Psa51:12 confirms the inverse: without the willing spirit (after moral failure), the will cannot exercise this free movement and requires divine restoration.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Humility both *requires* volition and *rightly orders* it. The imperative form throughout ("humble yourselves") presupposes and addresses the volitional capacity. The Phili2:8 paradigm reveals that the volitional act of self-humbling is the highest exercise of free self-determination — choosing, from a position of full capability and freedom, to take the downward path. This suggests that humility does not impair volition but *expresses* it in its highest form: the will most fully itself when it freely releases the claim to standing rather than defending it. Conversely, pride (the structural opposite) represents the will enclosed in self-assertion — technically free but functionally self-limiting in its capacities for genuine relation and perception.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All six enable and rightly order volition; none suppress or bypass it. The enabling patterns differ by characteristic. Humility (CHAR-1) expresses volition in its highest form — Phili2:8 (the Son freely choosing the downward path) is the paradigmatic instance of genuine volitional freedom expressed through self-humbling. Submission (CHAR-2) rightly orients the will — Rom6:17 (obedient from the heart) shows the will operating at its most self-directed level under legitimate authority rather than being suppressed by it. Contrition (CHAR-3) rightly orders the will by stripping the self-asserting, self-protective volitional orientation that prevents genuine openness to God. Meekness and Gentleness (CHAR-4) enables proportionate and frictionless volitional expression — metriopatheō calibrates the will's force; okneō removes hesitation-friction from its response. Dignity (CHAR-5) provides the inner character-ground from which volitional choices flow appropriately. Willing-heartedness (CHAR-6) expresses the will at its most liberated — the freely-moving will functioning at maximum voluntary freedom without compulsion or reluctance. Cluster-level: M09 redirects and liberates the will from self-enclosure rather than suppressing it — the will most fully itself when freely released toward God and others.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — Wilful sinning *expresses* volition (the will is actively choosing) while *deepening constraint on future volition* over time. The escalation evidence (Hos 4:7 — "the more they sinned"; Hos 13:2 — "they sin more and more") shows a progressive narrowing of the will's range: each act of sinning makes subsequent sinning more likely and more compulsive. Neh 13:26 — "foreign women made even him to sin" — implies that sustained exposure progressively undermines the will's capacity to resist. The will that wilfully sins remains technically free (the corpus maintains moral accountability throughout) but its effective range is progressively constrained by habituation.

**[CHAR-10]** E — Different patterns. (1) *Enticement impairs volition*: Jam 1:14 — the enticement mechanism draws the will through desire before the will has made a deliberate choice; the desire pre-empts deliberate volition. 2Pe 2:18 — "those who are barely escaping" — the barely-escaping person's will is weakened, making the desire-exploitation more effective; enticement targets and exploits volitional weakness. (2) *Hypocrisy misdirects volition*: Gal 2:13 — the will makes a choice (to act alongside) but the choice is driven by social pressure rather than authentic identity. (3) *Apostasy exercises volition*: Act 21:21 — the departure is a volitional act; the will chooses to stand away from the covenantal commitment.

**[CHAR-11]** E — The condition *enslaves and progressively captures* volition. Rom 7:14 — "sold under sin" — the will is in a slave-ownership relationship; its capacity for autonomous choosing has been compromised by the sale. Rom 6:20 — "when you were slaves of sin, you were free in regard to righteousness" — the enslaved will has no freedom toward righteousness; the will's freedom is preserved in one direction (sinning) while closed in the other (righteousness). The condition's enslavement is thus a directional impairment: the will can continue to choose within the sinful domain but cannot freely choose toward God.

**[CHAR-12]** E — Sin's enslaving power *captures and progressively binds* volition. Joh 8:34 — the will of the practice-sinner is progressively captured through the accumulating practices; each practice-act deepens the will's directional captivity toward sin. The will is not eliminated (the person continues to choose and act) but its free direction toward God is foreclosed: Rom 6:1/2 — "continue in sin... live in it" — the enslaved will continues choosing within the sin-domain but cannot exit the domain through its own freedom.

**[CHAR-13]** E — The record *accumulates through volitional persistence* and *is addressed through volitional turning*. The will's sustained choices in one direction deepen the record (Lev 26:18-28 — sevenfold escalation; VCG-04 — kings who did not depart). The will's decisive turn enables the record's erasure (Eze 18:21; 33:14/16). The record thus tracks the will's directional history precisely: VCG-04's "he walked in" and "he did not depart" language is the volitional vocabulary of record accumulation.

**[CHAR-14]** E — Forgiveness received *liberates* volition. Col 2:13 — "dead in your trespasses... made alive" — the death-in-trespasses suppresses volitional freedom (the dead cannot will effectively); the forgiveness that makes alive restores the volitional capacity. Act 2:38 — "you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit" — the Spirit's indwelling following forgiveness is the source of renewed volitional capacity; the Spirit enables the will's ongoing God-directed freedom that sin had foreclosed.

**[CHAR-15]** E — The generational pattern *captures and progressively deepens* volitional commitment to sinning: Psa 78:17 — "sinned still more" — the volitional momentum is in the direction of increasing sin; the "still more" indicates the will becoming progressively more committed to the inherited direction rather than less. However, 1Ki 8:47 confirms the will retains the capacity to turn (the heart can be turned; repentance is possible), meaning the generational pattern does not eliminate volition but skews its default direction.

**[CHAR-16]** E — The sinner-identity *constrains and narrows* volition. Luk 6:32/33/34 — the sinners' volitional range extends only to reciprocal relationships; they love those who love them, do good to those who do good, lend to those who will repay. The sinner-identity confines the will to a self-interest radius: the will can operate within that radius (genuine love, real goodness — Luk 6:33 notes sinners genuinely "do the same") but cannot extend beyond it without a deeper transformation. The volitional capacity is not eliminated but limited in its reach.

**[CHAR-17]** E — The guilt-state *redirects volition* toward remedial action when conscience operates correctly. Lev 6:4 — "realized his guilt and will restore" — the guilt-state produces a volitional impulse toward restitution; Num 5:7 — "he shall confess... and shall make full restitution" — the guilt-recognition is the volitional turning-point. However, the unaddressed guilt-state can *paralyse volition*: Gen 4:13 — "my punishment is greater than I can bear" — Cain's experience implies a volitional paralysis under overwhelming punitive guilt; 2Ch 33:23 — "incurred guilt more and more" — the will persisting in guilt-generating choices despite accumulation shows volition captured by the wrong direction.

**[CHAR-18]** E — The iniquity *captures and constrains* volition progressively. Pro 5:22 — "the iniquities of the wicked ensnare him, and he is held fast in the cords of his sin" — the accumulated iniquity becomes the cords that bind the will; voluntary choices have produced an involuntary bondage. Eze 18:30 — "lest iniquity be your ruin" — the warning presupposes the will can still turn; before the bondage becomes total, the will retains the capacity to repent. The progression is: free volitional choice of iniquity → accumulation → progressive bondage of will → ruin. The iniquity does not eliminate will immediately but ensnares it progressively.

**[CHAR-19]** E — Transgression *progressively enslaves* the will that committed it. Psa 19:13 — "let them not have dominion over me!" — transgression seeks dominion over the will; Pro 29:6 — "ensnared in his transgression" — the will is trapped by what it chose; Pro 12:13 — "ensnared by the transgression of his lips" — the spoken transgression returns to ensnare the speaker's will. The progression is: free volitional act (the first crossing) → repeated crossings → accumulated ensnaring → dominion over the will. The will that chose transgression is progressively constrained by what it chose until it requires divine liberation.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Unintentional sinning operates through *uninformed volition* — the will acts without the moral information that would enable it to choose rightly. This is not impairment of the will but operation of the will within an information deficit. The remedy sequence (confession → offering → forgiveness) restores the will's alignment: Num 22:34 (Balaam's will, now informed, offers to reverse) shows the will in its corrected mode post-disclosure. The characteristic does not impair volition; it reveals the will's dependence on adequate moral information to operate rightly.

**[CHAR-20]** E — Faithlessness *progressively captures* the will. Pro 11:6 — "the treacherous are taken captive by their lust" — the faithless will is eventually captured by the very desire that drove it to betray; 2Ch 28:22 — the will that chose faithlessness progressively loses its freedom to turn toward God (each distress-event produced more faithlessness, not less). The will begins as the agent of betrayal (the choice to break faith) and ends as the captive of the betrayal's consequences (lust-captivity). The remedy (Lev 26:40 — "if they confess") requires the will's active engagement in the confession-act.

**[CHAR-21]** E — Perversion *captures and enslaves* the volitional faculty progressively. The initial active-will choice of perversity (Pro 2:14 — delight in perverseness) produces the enslavement of 2Pe 2:19 — "slaves of corruption"; whatever overcomes the person enslaves them. The will that freely chose perversity is progressively incapacitated by what it chose. The remedy (Eph 4:22-24 — "put off... put on") is a volitional act requiring renewal of the spirit of the mind (Eph 4:23 — "renewed in the spirit of your minds").

**[CHAR-22]** E — Sustained injustice *progressively captures* the will. The initial volitional choice to commit injustice (Eze 3:20 — "turns and commits") develops toward the fixed-character dishonesty of Luk 16:10 — consistent across small and large — where the will's choices are no longer deliberated afresh but flow from the constituted unjust character. The will that could have withheld (Eze 18:8 — "withholds his hand") becomes the will that consistently enacts wrong at every scale. The remedy calls the will back to volitional choice: Job 34:32 — "I will do it no more."

**[CHAR-3]** E — Genuine confession *aligns and deepens* volition: the act of naming sin as sin before God commits the will to a moral position — by confessing "I have sinned," the will agrees with the conscience's verdict and moves toward alignment with God's moral standard. 2Sa 24:10 — "please take away the iniquity of your servant" — the confessing will is oriented toward restoration and away from the sinning direction. Hollow confession (Deu 1:41) shows that verbal confession without volitional alignment does not enable the will — the will remains on its own course.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Conscience suppression *both enables and impairs* volition. It *enables* the will to choose sin without the moral resistance that an active conscience would create — Ecc 8:12 (sinning a hundred times is possible partly because no inner check is operating). It simultaneously *impairs* the will's capacity for right moral choice: a will habituated to sinning without conscience (Tit 3:11 — "warped") progressively loses the inner equipment it needs to choose well.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Refusal to repent *misdirects* volition while keeping it fully operative. The will remains fully functioning — it is making choices, clinging to the sinful course, resisting correction (Neh 9:29 — "would not obey" is an act of will). But the direction of volitional operation is away from God and away from the available turn. Over time, sustained refusal *constrains* volition: Heb 10:26 — "there no longer remains a sacrifice for sins" — the persistent-refusal will progressively forecloses the options available to it (the sacrifice is closed off). The will is not impaired in its operational capacity but progressively constrained in its available options through sustained refusal.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Habitual defection *misdirects and progressively constrains* volition. The will remains operative — the habitual sinner keeps sinning, keeps refusing to listen, keeps directing allegiance elsewhere — but its directional freedom is progressively constrained by the habit it has formed. Exo 9:34's hardening cycle shows this: each iteration of sinning-and-hardening makes the will's sinning direction more natural and the alternative less accessible. The self-reinforcing structure (Hos 8:11 — altars for sinning producing more sinning) shows how habitual defection builds an environment in which the will's sinning direction is the path of least resistance.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Contagious sin *misdirects* the leader's volition (toward causing others to sin) and *shapes* the community's volition (toward the sinning direction). For the leader, the will is fully operative and causatively engaged — there is no impairment, only a wrong direction. For the community, the will is gradually shaped toward the sinning direction through sustained exposure to the leader's transmitted sinning (1Ki 22:52 — three generations; 2Ki 21:11 — Manasseh's sustained idolatry shaping Judah). The community's volitional freedom is not removed but its default orientation is progressively shaped toward the sinning course.

**[CHAR-8]** E — Political revolt *expresses* volition at full capacity: the revolt is a decisive exercise of the revolting community's collective will. The corpus shows no impairment — the volitional capacity is fully engaged in the breaking and the constructive establishment of alternative authority. 2Ki 3:7 — Jehoram's immediate political-military response to Moab's revolt shows the governing authority also exercising full volition in the response. Volition is fully operative on both sides of the revolting relationship.

**[CHAR-9]** E — Sinful speech *misdirects and progressively binds* the will. 1Ti 6:4's craving — the will's appetite for controversy — feeds on the sinful speech it produces: slander generates more craving, and the craving generates more slander. VCG-03's beast-blasphemy shows the endpoint: the will entirely bound to the sinful speech orientation as its constitutive expression (Rev 17:3 — "full of blasphemous names"). The will is not impaired in its operational capacity but is progressively bound to the sinful speech pattern.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The characteristic progressively impairs the full range of volitional freedom. Volition is initially engaged (Pro 4:14 — the choice to enter the path) but the sustained operation of the characteristic restricts the scope of volitional capacity: Pro 5:22 ("ensnared, held fast in the cords of his sin") — wickedness generates its own volitional constraints; Isa 26:10 ("he does not learn righteousness") — the volitional capacity to receive righteous instruction is impaired by the settled characteristic. The evidence presents volition as both the primary faculty by which the characteristic is adopted and the primary faculty the characteristic eventually constrains. This is the trajectory: volitional entry → sustained volitional refusal to turn → progressive volitional bondage.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The characteristic constrains volitional freedom while keeping the will active. The will is present (the person suppresses truth, chooses darkness, obeys unrighteousness — all volitional acts), but the constitutional condition narrows the range within which the will operates freely. Mat 7:18 (vc=14440 — VCG-02): "a diseased tree cannot bear good fruit" — the word "cannot" indicates a constitutional constraint on volitional possibility. The will is not eliminated but is structurally constrained by the constitutional evil condition: it can choose among evil options but cannot choose good fruit from an evil tree without the tree's nature being changed. This is distinct from CHAR-1's volitional orientation: CHAR-2 describes a constitutional constraint on what the will can produce; CHAR-1 describes the direction the will has chosen.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The characteristic progressively constrains volitional freedom. In its settled state, the fool's will is so oriented toward evil that departure is experienced as repugnant (Pro 13:19 — VCG-05) — the will's range of choice has narrowed to within the abominable. Eze 14:6 (vc=65984 — VCG-04) reveals that the will is currently "facing" abominations — the volitional direction requires the commanding divine call to reverse. The characteristic does not eliminate volition (the commands to repent and turn presuppose volitional capacity) but it constrains and misdirects the will toward abominable orientations and away from departure.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The characteristic progressively constrains volitional freedom. Initially, the characteristic enters through a volitional choice (Isa 66:3 — VCG-04: "chosen their own ways"). Sustained attachment then constrains the will: Eze 20:8 (vc=65911 — VCG-05) shows a community "not willing" to cast away the idols — the will has become bound by the attachment. Deu 7:26 (vc=65927 — VCG-02): bringing the abominable thing into the house "makes you devoted to destruction like it" — the act of proximity re-orients the will toward the abominable object. The will is not eliminated but progressively aligned with the idol's pull, narrowing the person's volitional freedom to depart.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The characteristic progressively constrains volitional freedom. Initially the characteristic is entered through volitional choice (Job 36:21 — VCG-04). As it deepens, the will becomes bound by the characteristic: Psa 119:133 (vc=38227 — VCG-04): iniquity seeking "dominion over me" — the will's governing function is at risk of being displaced by iniquity's control. Job 36:10 (vc=38215 — VCG-04): God must open their ears to enable return — the will cannot independently reverse the trajectory without divine intervention at an advanced stage. The characteristic does not eliminate volition (the commands to return and put far away are addressed to the will) but progressively constrains its range of free movement toward departure.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The characteristic progressively constrains and hardens the volitional faculty. Rev 16:9/11/21 (VCG-01): across three escalating divine judgments, the will maintains and deepens its defiant posture — each judgment compounds the hardening. The volitional refusal to repent becomes more absolute rather than weakening. This progressive constraint shows the characteristic as self-reinforcing in its volitional dimension: each act of defiant speech entrenches the will more deeply in the direction it has chosen. The will is not eliminated (the choice to speak remains deliberate) but its range of genuine choice toward repentance progressively narrows.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster reveals a consistent pattern across all six: M10b characteristics are entered through volitional choice but progressively constrain the will's freedom to depart. Char 5 (Psa 119:133 — iniquity seeking dominion over the will), Char 4 (Eze 20:8 — "not willing" as the settled volitional state after sustained idolatrous attachment), Char 6 (Rev 16:9/11/21 — the will becoming more fixed under escalating judgment pressure). The cluster's volitional trajectory: initial free volitional choice → progressive volitional constraint → eventual will-hardening that makes departure require divine intervention (Job 36:10 — divine ear-opening). This is the cluster's most important cross-characteristic finding: all six M10b characteristics follow the same volitional trajectory from free entry to constrained exit.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The characteristic structures the volitional faculty rather than enabling or impairing it directly. It creates a framework of volitional obligation: the will must choose at each contact point (touch or refrain), at each remedy point (cleanse or refuse). The characteristic bypasses the will in the unconscious-defilement cases (Lev 5:2-3, M10c-A-VCG-01) — defilement arrives without volitional participation — but this does not eliminate the will's obligation to respond once awareness arrives. The characteristic thus reveals volition as operative at the perimeter of the condition (avoidance and remedy), not at its core (acquisition in most cases).

**[CHAR-2]** E — The characteristic impairs volition in a specific way: it produces bondage of the will (Rom 6:19 — "slaves to impurity") while maintaining the appearance of volitional activity (Eph 4:19 — "given themselves up" — the person appears to choose). The will remains active but is redirected and constrained: it can choose to pursue impurity ("greedy to practice every kind of impurity," Eph 4:19) but cannot freely choose away from it without the intervention of the gospel's liberating power (Rom 6:19 — "so now present your members as slaves to righteousness" — the new possibility must be named as a call, implying it requires external enabling). The characteristic thus produces a pseudo-freedom that is actually bondage.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The characteristic engages volition in two contradictory directions. On one hand it is generated by volitional acts (deliberate idolatry, deliberate sexual betrayal, deliberate desecration) — the will is functional and active, choosing the defilement. On the other hand, Eze 20:30 (VCG-02) — "will you defile yourselves after the manner of your fathers?" — reveals a generational volitional pattern that has become an inherited temptation, suggesting that the will's range of motion may be constrained by generational idolatrous patterns. The characteristic does not eliminate volitional capacity but embeds it in a context of inherited temptation and communal pressure toward repeated defection.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The characteristic overrides volition rather than simply impairing it. The person's will is not gradually weakened (as in Characteristic 2's conscience-suppression trajectory) but suddenly and completely overridden by an external will: Luk 8:29 — "driven by the demon." This is the most extreme form of volitional impairment in the M10c cluster: the will exists but is effectively imprisoned by the spirit's domination.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The four characteristics produce a gradient of volitional impact that reveals the cluster's range of will-engagement. Characteristic 1 structures and obligates the will without impairing it: the will operates under a framework of volitional obligations (avoidance, remedy-seeking) without being itself corrupted. Characteristic 2 impairs the will through self-generated bondage: the will's own prior choices (desire-following, habituation) produce a condition of pseudo-freedom that is actually slavery (Rom 6:19 — "slaves to impurity" while "greedily" pursuing more — Eph 4:19). Characteristic 3 neither impairs nor destroys the will — the community retains full volitional capacity but exercises it through sustained deliberate defection (Eze 22:3 — "a city that makes idols to defile herself" — fully purposeful). Characteristic 4 overrides the will from outside (Luk 8:29 — "driven by the demon") — the most acute form of volitional impairment in the cluster, not through internal corruption but through external domination.

questions.question_text: Across the verses, what does the pattern of engagement and non-engagement with volition indicate about the characteristic's nature?

findings.session_b_note:
The volitional engagement pattern reveals that forgiveness operates at two distinct volitional levels simultaneously:

1. **Divine volitional initiative:** God's decision to forgive is the originating volitional act — sovereign, free, grounded in his own character (Psa 86:5 — "to all who call upon you"). The divine will is the ultimate source of the possibility of forgiveness.

2. **Human volitional response:** The human will is engaged both as receiver (the access-postures: repentance, faith, confession are volitional orientations) and as giver (the commanded horizontal extension). The human will is not passive in the forgiveness economy — it is enrolled at both ends.

The characteristic does not **bypass** the will — it requires it, engages it, transforms it (through received forgiveness generating love-orientation), and commands it. This is one of the most fully volitionally-engaged characteristics in the programme.

findings.session_b_note:
The pattern reveals that compassion occupies a unique position relative to the volitional faculty: it is pre-volitional in origin (the somatic stirring precedes the choice) but volitionally engageable in both directions (toward action or toward suppression). This makes it unlike characteristics that are purely volitional (choice-dependent from the outset) and unlike characteristics that are purely affective (purely felt, not enacted).

Compassion is the inner-being reality that the will must reckon with — it is the natural arising that judgment must deliberately override, and it is the affective ground that courage-in-action enacts. The will does not initiate compassion but it determines what compassion produces: either restrained (judicial suppression) or released (boundary-crossing action). This positions compassion as the characteristic that most directly tests the moral quality of the will — whether the will serves the natural outward movement toward the suffering other or serves other moral demands that require its suppression.

findings.session_b_note: The pattern reveals that contrition is neither purely passive (something that simply happens to the inner being without the will's involvement) nor purely active (something the will generates from its own resources). It occupies a middle position: the will's consent to receive and not resist the crushing that comes from moral self-recognition or divine encounter. This middle position — volitional receptivity — is constitutive of genuine contrition and distinguishes it from both mere suffering (purely passive) and willed performance of penitence (purely active without inner reality).

findings.session_b_note: The pattern reveals that fellowship operates at the intersection of freedom and formation: volitional choice is the entry-point for most fellowship modes, but sustained fellowship progressively shapes the constitutional character that makes future volitional choices. This is consistent with finding 062-CHAR-001 (fellowship produces character conformity to the fellowship object) and the moral-alignment emphasis of the righteous-companionship groups. Volition is the hinge-point of fellowship: what the person chooses to be joined to determines what they become.

findings.session_b_note: The volitional engagement reveals that goodness is not merely a character quality but an active principle that must be chosen and willed. Goodness does not produce compliance or passive absorption — it produces resolve ("every resolve for good," 2Th 1:11) and active choosing ("do what seems good," 884-008). The person who possesses goodness chooses it actively — Col 3:12 frames this as "put on therefore" — a deliberate volitional act enabled by prior transformation. This reveals that goodness has a volitional depth that distinguishes it from passive character states: it is both a quality possessed and a quality actively willed. The reconstitution of volition by goodness means that the good person is not merely compliant but genuinely desirous of the good — the will itself has been reoriented rather than overridden. (OBS-067-OBS-039, OBS-067-OBS-040, SBF-067-Q040)

findings.session_b_note: The volitional engagement pattern reveals that love and will are not rivals but partners in the data's inner-being architecture. Love is not opposed to will (as if love were pure feeling that will must constrain) — love provides the motivational ground that the will exercises from. This is the pattern of Joh 14:15: love of Christ produces the will's obedience, not as external compulsion but as the natural expression of the inner love. Enemy-love (Mat 5:44) pushes this furthest: love extends the will's reach beyond what it could achieve through discipline alone. The pattern also reveals that disordered love progressively constrains the will — the person addicted to a wrong love-object finds their volitional freedom increasingly reduced. Love's quality determines the will's freedom: righteous love expands volitional range; disordered love narrows it toward its object.

findings.finding_value: T3 reveals two structurally distinctive findings about compassion's faculty engagement. First, creativity is entirely silent (three S ratings) — the most informative absence in the tier: compassion responds, it does not originate or create. It is the most responsive of the faculties-engaging characteristics. Second, affect and moral action are structurally unified in compassion — not sequentially related but simultaneous. Affect is the mechanism of movement (splanchnizō is both the felt inner event and the cause of the action), not a precursor or accompaniment. This is unique among the characteristics reviewed: in most other registries, affect and volition are distinguishable stages; in compassion, the felt movement is already the morally motivated action beginning. A third distinctive finding: compassion converts moral knowledge into motivated action — it is the motivational ground of conscientiousness, not a product of it. The conscience faculty engagement reveals compassion as conscience-healing: it addresses the pitiable condition that conscience perceives as a moral claim, resolving the tension between moral knowledge and moral incapacity. The three relational modes (building/sustaining — chesed; restoring/repairing — splanchnizō; extending across difference — Good Samaritan) are a new finding not in the instruction typology.

findings.finding_value: T1's four kinds explain T3's most distinctive finding: that affect and moral action are structurally unified rather than sequential. In T1 terms, compassion-as-inner-event (splanchnizō) and compassion-as-externalised-act are not two separate kinds but a continuous movement — the felt-movement is the beginning of the act. T3 confirms this: affect is the mechanism of movement, not its precursor. T1's finding that compassion converts moral knowledge into motivated action (the unique position as motivational ground of conscientiousness) maps onto T3.10's finding of the same: the definitional claim (T1) that compassion is constitutively outward-facing explains T3's finding that it is the driving faculty between moral knowledge and moral action.
