findings.finding_value: T2's four-stage constitutional movement sequence (somatic arousal → soul engagement → volitional engagement → outward action) maps directly onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The somatic-arousal stage (T2.6 — gut stirring, splanchnizō) corresponds to T3.1's perceptive-trigger stage (sight activates the somatic response) and T3.4's affect stage (the stirring is the affective movement). The soul-engagement stage (T2.2 — chesed as soul-character) corresponds to T3.8 moral evaluation (the soul assesses the need) and T3.9 conscience (the conscience activates the response). The volitional-engagement stage (T2.3 — heart-locus as deliberative site) corresponds to T3.6 volition (the will directs the action). The outward-action stage corresponds to T3.7 agency. T2 and T3 describe the same movement sequence from two perspectives: T2 maps the constitutional levels; T3 maps the faculties active at each level.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-020: T3's affect-moral-action unity (affect is the mechanism, not the precursor) and T5's formation finding (compassion is simultaneously character target and motivational ground) are structurally connecte…
findings.finding_value: T3's affect-moral-action unity (affect is the mechanism, not the precursor) and T5's formation finding (compassion is simultaneously character target and motivational ground) are structurally connected. T5 names compassion as the motivational ground that makes the sanctification arc survivable through failure and return — but T3 has already established that affect is the mechanism of this motivational ground: the character formation that T5 describes is accomplished through the affective mechanism that T3 identifies. The person who is formed into compassionate character (T5) is the person whose affective faculty has been trained to respond immediately and morally to perceived suffering (T3). T3's finding that affect and moral action are unified is T5's mechanism of formation: the person becoming compassionate is the person in whom the affective-moral unity is deepening and stabilising.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-003: T3 produces four structurally significant findings about grace's faculty engagement. First, grace is agency-constituting rather than agency-replacing: 1Cor 15:10 holds in explicit paradox — "I worked …
findings.finding_value: T3 produces four structurally significant findings about grace's faculty engagement. First, grace is agency-constituting rather than agency-replacing: 1Cor 15:10 holds in explicit paradox — "I worked harder than any of them, though it was not I but the grace of God that is with me." Agency is not displaced but constituted by grace. This relationship holds in paradox that the T3.6 prompt options (enable/deepen/bypass/impair) cannot accommodate — a prompt design limitation noted for catalogue revision. Second, grace produces moral clarity (T3.8 — sharpens moral evaluation rather than bypassing it): the person who recognises grace has made a precise moral evaluation (they know they received what they did not deserve). Third, grace and conscience are mutually necessary: grace is the condition within which conscience can operate fully without destroying the person; conscience without grace produces condemnation; grace without conscience produces presumption (T3.9). Fourth, grace is the primary relational faculty developer in the registry's evidence — it reaches every relational register (vertical access, horizontal forgiving, speech-grace) and enables each one. Creativity (T3.5) is the one genuinely silent faculty — not an impairment but a non-engagement: grace receives and constitutes, it does not create.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-009: T1's immediate response pattern (fear → mourning → prostration as the creaturely recognition response) is the affective-volitional expression of T3's faculty engagement at the moment grace arrives. T3…
findings.finding_value: T1's immediate response pattern (fear → mourning → prostration as the creaturely recognition response) is the affective-volitional expression of T3's faculty engagement at the moment grace arrives. T3.4 (affect is the first named faculty engaged by grace) and T3.6 (the agency-constituting paradox of 1Cor 15:10) together explain why T1.5 finds the creaturely recognition response before positive states settle: grace first produces the affective recognition (fear, mourning) before constituting the agency through which the person responds (prostration as the body enacting the inner posture that grace has produced). T1's finding that grace requires creaturely recognition to complete its operation (T1.7) is T3.1's finding at the faculty level: grace requires and enables perception simultaneously.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-014: T2's constitutional movement (spirit reception → soul standing → capacity → character expression) maps onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The spirit-reception stage (T2.1) corresponds to T3.1 (per…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional movement (spirit reception → soul standing → capacity → character expression) maps onto T3's faculty engagement sequence. The spirit-reception stage (T2.1) corresponds to T3.1 (perception — grace enabling the inner sight and hearing that receives it). The soul-standing stage (T2.2) corresponds to T3.9 (conscience — grace as the condition within which conscience can operate without destruction) and T3.8 (moral evaluation — the standing produces the clarity of moral self-assessment). The capacity-gifting stage (T2.1 — spirit level) corresponds to T3.7 (agency — capacity given constitutes agency for the task). The character-expression stage (T2.7 — outward through body-soul) corresponds to T3.10 (conscientiousness — the integrated moral-action expression of received grace-character). T2 maps the constitutional space; T3 maps the faculties active at each spatial level; the two tiers describe the same movement from orthogonal perspectives.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-019: T3's agency-constituting finding (grace constitutes rather than replaces agency — 1Cor 15:10) and T4's human-to-God direction (supplication as the human posture of appeal — requiring genuine human age…
findings.finding_value: T3's agency-constituting finding (grace constitutes rather than replaces agency — 1Cor 15:10) and T4's human-to-God direction (supplication as the human posture of appeal — requiring genuine human agency in the act of plea) are structurally aligned. The constituted agency (T3.7) is precisely the agency that supplication requires: the creature must genuinely appeal, not merely receive passively. T3's finding that grace and conscience are mutually necessary (T3.9) corresponds to T4's relational-access finding: grace transforms the threshold of human-to-God approach (prosagōgē — SD035) from impassable to open, which is the relational expression of T3.9's constitutional finding that grace creates the condition within which conscience can operate fully without destruction. T3 names the inner-being event; T4 names the relational consequence of the same event.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-020: T3's faculty findings are the synchronic expression of T5's diachronic formation arc. The creaturely recognition response (T5.2 — fear → mourning → prostration as the consistent transitional state in …
findings.finding_value: T3's faculty findings are the synchronic expression of T5's diachronic formation arc. The creaturely recognition response (T5.2 — fear → mourning → prostration as the consistent transitional state in all grace-sequences) is the affective-faculty event (T3.4) at the moment of grace-arrival, which then constitutes the volitional-faculty alignment (T3.6 — the agency-constituting paradox) that enables the conscientious expression (T3.10). T5's formation arc (sustained work producing character-quality) is the longitudinal development of T3.9's finding (conscience operating fully within grace) into T3.10's finding (conscientiousness as the integrated moral character that grace constitutes over time). The person who has been formed by grace through the T5 formation arc is the person in whom T3's faculty engagements have been progressively deepened and integrated.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-022: T3's faculty findings are grounded in and confirmed by T7's primary anchor evidence. The perceptive-faculty finding (T3.1 — grace requires and enables perception) is grounded in the eye-formula of che…
findings.finding_value: T3's faculty findings are grounded in and confirmed by T7's primary anchor evidence. The perceptive-faculty finding (T3.1 — grace requires and enables perception) is grounded in the eye-formula of chen (SD041), Zec 12:10's grace-produced vision, and SD012's hearing-receptivity pattern. T7's argument structure for Zec 12:10 (grace outpoured → "when they look on me, on him whom they have pierced") confirms T3.1 precisely: the grace-event produces and requires the inner sight that recognises what grace has cost. T3.6's agency-constituting paradox (1Cor 15:10) is T7.3's most significant framework-divergence point: at the moment of constitutional incapacity, all human science frameworks assume the person has some prior agency; the biblical account holds the paradox of grace-constituted agency that is genuinely human while grace-originated. This is the methodological divergence T7.3 identifies and T3.6 establishes as the operative finding.

findings.session_b_note: The pattern reveals a developmental trajectory in covenant's engagement with volition. The old covenant calls for volition as its primary human requirement; the new covenant transforms volition as its primary human gift. Both engagements are profound, but they operate in opposite directions: the old covenant requires the person to bring their will to the covenant; the new covenant brings a transformed will to the person. This pattern reveals that covenant is the structuring reality within which the theological question of human will and divine grace is most sharply focused in Scripture. Covenant is the framework that makes the will-and-grace question visible — and the covenant trajectory from old to new is the narrative resolution of that question: not the abolition of human volition but its liberation through the Spirit's transforming work.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-034-003: T3 as a whole reveals that covenant comprehensively engages the inner faculties but with a specific structural bias: the faculties it most deeply and richly engages are those oriented toward the Other…
findings.finding_value: T3 as a whole reveals that covenant comprehensively engages the inner faculties but with a specific structural bias: the faculties it most deeply and richly engages are those oriented toward the Other (relational capacity, memory, cognition as knowing-God, moral evaluation, conscientiousness) rather than those oriented inward (creativity, which is notably absent). This faculty-engagement pattern is coherent with covenant's relational-disposition primary classification — covenant is constitutively Other-oriented and therefore engages the Other-oriented faculties most richly. The deepest T3 finding is the developmental one: the old covenant calls for volition from outside (demands obedience); the new covenant transforms volition from inside (liberates and enables faithfulness through Spirit). This volitional trajectory is confirmed across T3.6 (volition) and T3.7 (agency) and is the faculty-level expression of the same transformation that T2 identified at the constitutional-movement level and T5 identifies at the mechanism level. All three tiers point to the same inner-being reality from different analytical vantage points.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-020: T3 identifies the new covenant's faculty-level effect as the transformation of volition (from called-for to liberated — Q&A-085) and the production of covenantal knowing (Q&A-073). T5 identifies the d…
findings.finding_value: T3 identifies the new covenant's faculty-level effect as the transformation of volition (from called-for to liberated — Q&A-085) and the production of covenantal knowing (Q&A-073). T5 identifies the developmental sequence through which this transformation occurs (failure → inscription → belonging → knowing — Q&A-128) and the mechanism change (letter to Spirit — Q&A-131). The T3 × T5 synthesis: the faculty transformations identified in T3 (volition liberated, cognition/knowing produced) are the outcome of the developmental sequence and mechanism identified in T5. The sequence "inscription → belonging → knowing" (T5) describes how the specific faculty transformations of T3 are produced. The mechanism shift from letter to Spirit (T5) is the developmental mechanism that produces the volitional liberation (T3.6) and cognitive knowing (T3.2) that the new covenant delivers. T5 is the developmental story; T3 is the faculty-level outcome of that story.

findings.session_b_note: The volitional pattern reveals that peace is not a deterministic state but a characteristic that engages the will at every point — in its reception (choosing to orient toward God), its pursuit (actively seeking peace with others), its refusal (the structural human refusal documented in the prophets), and its false claim (bypassing the real volitional cost). This has significant anthropological implications: the human person is not a passive recipient of peace but an active participant in whether and how peace is received, held, and expressed. The refusal pattern (Isa 30:15) is the most theologically significant volitional evidence — God's offer of peace is genuine, the refusal is genuine, and the consequence is the person's responsibility.

findings.session_b_note: The pattern reveals that inner-being giving requires and expresses genuine volition — it cannot be coerced or mechanically produced. The imperative form (give glory), the contemplated act (how can I give you up?), and the active self-offerings (I gave my back; blessed be the name of the Lord) are all volitional structures. This distinguishes the characteristic sharply from passive reception — even the human who receives divine giving must volitionally receive it (Q&A-031 showed that reception requires inner conditions). The pattern further reveals that faithfulness-as-giving is an exercise of the full volitional capacity in alignment with inner-being commitment — volition in service of prior covenantal orientation.

findings.finding_value:
The volitional faculty is the hinge of the wealth domain. The direction in which the will engages with wealth — toward accumulation (M46-A, M46-B impairment) or toward release and contentment (M46-D) — determines the inner-being outcome. M46-C's wisdom tradition consistently calls the will to ordered exercise (diligent work, deliberate stopping of the wealth-drive). The volitional pattern in M46 confirms that the wealth domain is fundamentally a domain of volitional testing.

[Cluster-level addition — Phase 9 cross-sub-group review] The volitional faculty is the consistent hinge of the wealth domain across all four sub-groups — but its directional deployment varies entirely. M46-A: the will is disengaged from seeking God by satiation (sha.a.nan, Amo 6:1) or actively deployed against God (Deu 32:15 — Jeshurun "kicked"). M46-B: the will is deployed in volitional refusal toward the poor (lo a.vah — "was unwilling," 2Sa 12:4). M46-C: the will is commanded toward sustained diligence (Pro 13:4) and wisdom-shaped restraint of the wealth-seeking drive (Pro 23:4). M46-D: the will exercises its highest deployment in deliberate, costly, irreversible voluntary release (Gen 14:23; Luk 19:8; 2Cor 8:9 — Christ's voluntary becoming-poor). The wealth domain does not bypass the volitional faculty but consistently reveals and tests the directional deployment of the whole acting person's will. The will's direction in the wealth domain is the most reliable structural indicator of which sub-group's pattern the person inhabits.

findings.finding_value: The pattern reveals that fear is fundamentally a volitional characteristic: its defining effect in every sub-group is on what the person chooses or fails to choose. This is the cluster's most structurally significant finding for the inner-faculties tier. Fear is not merely felt — it determines action. The ordered form (M01-A) makes the will's choices wise and ethical; the disordered forms (M01-B-D, F, G) suppress, bypass, misdirect, or dissolve those choices. The characteristic cannot be understood apart from its volitional impact.

The characteristic consistently engages and drives the will, but the quality of volitional engagement varies dramatically: righteous anger energises the will toward just action; resentful anger paralyses the will (Luk 15:28); possessing rage bypasses deliberation and drives involuntary action. The will is the primary faculty through which anger issues outward — but the anger can drive the will, energise it, or bypass it depending on its form and grounding.

The volition-grief relationship is one of the cluster's most analytically significant findings. Grief does not automatically determine the will. Worldly grief (grief over loss of wealth or status) tends to fail to govern the will productively; godly grief (grief over sin and relational rupture) tends to reshape the will toward repentance and moral reformation. The decisive factor appears to be the object of the grief and the spiritual orientation of the person receiving it — not the intensity of the grief itself.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Exultation is not purely spontaneous but involves the will as a significant constituent — particularly in adverse circumstances and in cultivated sustained orientation. The volitional dimension distinguishes exultation from passive emotional states and makes it susceptible to formation and practice.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Joy and volition have a constitutive relationship in both directions: the will can cultivate and direct Joy (commanded joy); Joy in turn enables and motivates the will (joy produces strength, generosity, endurance). This bidirectional relationship is what makes Joy a formation characteristic — it is both a goal of volitional formation and a resource for further volitional formation.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Suffering-Joy is the characteristic most explicitly requiring volitional engagement in M04: the commands are the most insistent (Jas 1:2's "count it ALL joy"; Mat 5:12's doubled command "rejoice AND be glad"). This volitional insistence confirms that the natural response to suffering is not joy and the will must be actively engaged by command. The Spirit enables what the will is commanded to do.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Gladness and volition are related in the pattern of cognition-informs-choice: Gladness's cognitive face (accurate evaluation of the good) is the prerequisite for good volitional choices. The pattern reveals Gladness as the inner faculty that prepares the will — it is not the same as the will but it precedes and enables its right operation.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Delight is the most volitionally-constituted characteristic in M04, distinctly more so than Gladness (primarily cognitive), Suffering-Joy (primarily Spirit-produced), or Joy (primarily affective). The cha.phets/che.phets vocabulary's pervasive use for both divine sovereign will and human desire confirms that Delight and volition are structurally intertwined: Delight is what the will is when fully engaged with its proper or improper object. The pattern reveals that the deepest volitional structure of a person is their Delight — what they are directed toward with their deepest pleasure.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Unlike Delight (where volition is constitutive) and Joy (where volition is involved through command), Pleasure engages volition instrumentally: right Pleasure supports right willing; wrong Pleasure corrupts and bypasses right willing. Pleasure is primarily receptive rather than volitional — but the quality of what is received as pleasant directly shapes and can corrupt volitional direction.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Psa 119:129's "wonderful… therefore my soul keeps them" is the most analytically significant volition-Wonder connection: Wonder in the testimonies motivates obedience. Wonder provides the motivational ground for volition: the person who is genuinely arrested by the wonderfulness of God's commands has a deep motivational reason to keep them beyond mere duty.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster reveals a volition-positive ensemble: all seven characteristics either require or enable or sustain volitional engagement. Delight (Char 4) is the primary volitional characteristic; Joy (Char 2) is the primary volitional-sustainer; Suffering-Joy (Char 7) makes the most demanding volitional requirement. The cluster's positive inner states are not passive experiences that happen to the person but inner-being realities that involve and develop the will. The formation implication: cultivating the cluster's characteristics is simultaneously cultivating the volitional capacity of the person.

**[CHAR-1]** E — That the will is the decisive faculty in CHAR-1's operation: whether shame functions as wound, corrective, or borne-for-God's-sake depends ultimately on the orientation of the will toward or away from a greater referent. Shame without will engagement is merely paralysis. Shame with the will engaged toward God becomes either the gateway to restoration (M07-C) or the mark of faithful endurance (M07-A-VCG-03).

**[CHAR-2]** E — CHAR-2 primarily impairs volition: the humiliated cannot return to public life (2Sa 10:5), cannot respond (Mat 22:12), retreat rather than advance. The enforced character of CHAR-2 is the primary volitional engagement — the person's will is not operative in the humiliation; it is done to them. The absence of the proper inner disposition of regard (entrepō evidence) shows that the failure of will to recognise proper standing enables CHAR-2 to become necessary.

---

**[CHAR-3]** E — VCG-01 active-dishonour is deeply volitional — it requires the willful act of refused-acknowledgment. "Willful inner refusal to acknowledge worth" (Pass A on Joh 8:49, vc=35000). The absent-regard of Luk 18:2/4 is a sustained volitional disposition. VCG-02 structural dishonour is less volitionally constituted — it arrives as assignment rather than choice.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — VCG-03 is most volitionally engaged: "rulers dearly love shame" (Hos 4:18) — the will has chosen dishonour as its object. Phili 3:19's "minds set on earthly things" — the will has oriented the evaluative faculty toward an earthly standard. Functioning CHAR-4 (VCG-01) requires the will's cooperation to renounce shameful ways (2Cor 4:2 — "we have renounced"). The volitional dimension is significant across all three VCGs.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — Volition is engaged in CHAR-5 through the contempt-er's willful act of dismissal (exoutheneō is consistently presented as a volitional disposition in its VCG-01 register — Luk 18:9: "trusted in themselves that they were righteous" and "treated others with contempt"). For the recipient, the will is engaged in the response: whether they retaliate (1Pe 3:9's temptation) or bless (1Pe 3:9's call). The decision to throw off the cloak (Mar 10:50) is a decisive volitional act of shame-identity abandonment.

---

**[CHAR-6]** E — Volition is CHAR-6's constituting faculty: the maintenance of innocence (Psa 73:13 — "I have kept my heart clean") is a volitional practice. The incapacity for innocence (Hos 8:5) is precisely a failure at the volitional level — the will's capacity for moral purity is so damaged by sustained idolatry that innocence-oriented choices are no longer possible. CHAR-6 is constituted by the will's sustained orientation toward moral cleanness and free-from-deliberate-wrongdoing choices.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — Volition is the decisive faculty across the entire cluster. Every M07 characteristic is ultimately determined at the level of the will: whether shame is received, resisted, borne, extended, maintained, or refused depends on the will's orientation. In Char 1: the will determines whether shame functions as wound, corrective, or borne-for-God's-sake — the voluntary-bearing of M07-A-VCG-03 (Isa 50:6-7; Heb 12:2) is the highest form of volitional agency in the shame-field. In Char 2: the will's failure to recognise proper standing enables CHAR-2 to become necessary. In Char 3: the will's refusal to acknowledge worth constitutes CHAR-3. In Char 4: the will's choice of standard (God or earthly things) determines whether the conscience functions or inverts. In Char 5: the will's disposition toward self-righteousness generates contempt; the will's orientation toward blessing rather than retaliation is the commanded response (1Pe 3:9). In Char 6: the will's sustained orientation toward moral cleanness constitutes innocence; its choice of idolatry destroys innocence-capacity (Hos 8:5). Cluster-level confirmation: the shame-field is primarily a volitional field — the will is the decisive faculty in determining where each characteristic lands.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — The pattern reveals that CHAR-1 is constitutively volitional at its core: it is not merely a mood or a cognitive error but a settled orientation of the will toward its own sovereignty. Psa 75:6–7 (vc=34301, vc=34230, M08-A4-VCG-05) states the theological frame: "not from the east or from the west... comes lifting up, but it is God who executes judgment, putting down one and lifting up another" — legitimate exaltation is God's volitional prerogative; CHAR-1 is the creature's will usurping that prerogative. Isa 14:13 (vc=34233, M08-A4-VCG-05) at its most extreme names CHAR-1 as a volitional declaration against God's own position. CHAR-1 is, at its constitutional core, the will claiming sovereignty over elevation — refusing to receive standing as gift from God and asserting it as the will's own possession.

**[CHAR-2]** E — CHAR-2 reveals that the volitional faculty's proper operation requires external constraint (divine command, appointed authority) to function rightly; when CHAR-2 removes those constraints, the unconstrained will becomes the instrument of transgression. Psa 19:13 (vc=34095, M08-B-VCG-02): "let not the presumptuous sins have dominion over me" — the presumptuous sins are characterized as internal forces seeking to "gain dominion" over the will, showing that even from within, unconstrained volitional impulses can enslave the will rather than liberate it.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The pattern reveals that CHAR-3 is uniquely susceptible to volitional discipline and redirection — unlike CHAR-1 (dispositional) and CHAR-2 (transgressive-act), the boasting-impulse can be voluntarily examined, bounded, and redirected (VCG-02 and VCG-03 are the evidenced results). This volitional redirectability is what makes the Pauline examined boasting discourse possible: the same impulse that generates VCG-01 condemned boasting can be volitionally disciplined into VCG-02 and VCG-03.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The pattern reveals that CHAR-4's cognitive distortion generates downstream volitional misdirection: the person who believes themselves above their actual measure will act accordingly — claiming freedoms they do not have (1Cor 4:18), craving controversy that validates their self-assessment (1Ti 6:4). CHAR-4 is volitionally consequential without being volitionally primary.

**[CHAR-5]** E — CHAR-5's volitional pattern reveals that structural power enables the will to operate without the natural constraints that vulnerability imposes on human agency. The person with structural power (shal.le.tet — Eze 16:30) can act "unrestrained" because the power position removes the relational and physical constraints that would otherwise limit the will. CHAR-5 is therefore the form of pride most directly enabled by external structural conditions — it amplifies the will's reach proportionally to the structural power available.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The volitional pattern across the cluster reveals that M08's characteristics are not passive states but active orientations — the person bearing them is volitionally engaged in their maintenance and expression. This has an important implication: M08 characteristics are not merely affective or cognitive disorders that happen to the person, but disorders in which the person's active will participates. CHAR-3's VCG-02 uniquely shows the volitional capacity for examining and redirecting the characteristic's expression — confirming that the will is available for corrective discipline, which is the ground for the Pauline examined-boasting discourse's formation-significance.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The volitional pattern reveals that submission is the characteristic most directly constituted by the will. Without volitional engagement, what remains is mere compliance (the M09-C/D distinction is precisely this: M09-C carries the genuine will-submission face; M09-D carries the relational-pattern expression). The volitional character of submission makes it the characteristic in which the will's orientation is most transparently at issue — whose servant the person is, and at what depth they genuinely yield, is determined by the will's habitual orientation (Rom6:16/17). The will is not merely the instrument of submission; it is the constitutional site where submission is determined.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The volitional pattern reveals that contrition operates on the will by dissolving its proud self-assertion — the will is not suppressed but reoriented from defensive self-protection to open receptivity. This makes contrition the characteristic that clears the ground for renewed volitional orientation — the revived spirit and heart (Isa57:15) imply a renewed volitional capacity that follows from the characteristic's resolution through God's presence.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The volitional pattern reveals that meekness and gentleness are expressions of *free, non-reactive willing*. The will that is meek/gentle is one that has freedom from two kinds of compulsion: (a) the compulsion to react with severity (metriopatheō restrains this) and (b) the compulsion to hesitate with self-protective reluctance (okneō absence restrains this). The characteristic is the will in its most liberated form — free from reactive extremes in both directions.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The volitional pattern reveals that semnotēs is maintained through sustained volitional commitment but is not constitutively an act of will — it is a character quality that persists and from which volitional choices flow. The distinction is that volition is secondary (maintains and expresses the characteristic) while the characterological quality is primary (the upstream source from which volitional expression flows).

**[CHAR-6]** E — The volitional pattern reveals that willing-heartedness is the *positive pole of the volitional faculty* — the will in its most freely-expressed, most genuinely-self-determined form. It is not the will suppressed (coerced compliance) nor the will in neutral (neither willing nor unwilling) but the will actively and gladly moving toward good. This makes the characteristic the expression of volitional health and freedom rather than of volitional constraint.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The volitional pattern reveals that humility is fundamentally a *choice-structured* characteristic: it cannot be imposed on the will from outside without ceasing to be genuine humility and becoming mere experienced lowliness (the M09-B condition register). The distinction between M09-A (willed self-lowering) and M09-B (imposed lowliness) maps directly onto the distinction between volitionally-engaged and volitionally-bypassed humility. The Col2:23 critique of imposed asceticism confirms this: external constraint cannot produce genuine inner transformation. Genuine humility is constitutively volitional — it requires the person's own choice — which is precisely what makes the Phili2:8 paradigm so striking: the divine Son freely *choosing* the downward path.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The volitional engagement pattern reveals that M09 is fundamentally a cluster of choice-structured characteristics — they cannot be imposed from outside the will without ceasing to be genuine. The Humility (CHAR-1) volume-split (Observation #16) most clearly confirms this: M09-A (willed self-lowering) is genuine humility; M09-B (imposed lowliness) is the same faculty under external pressure rather than volitional self-application. Col2:23 confirms the principle: external constraint cannot produce genuine inner transformation. The most striking confirmation is Phili2:8 — the divine Son freely choosing the downward path — which demonstrates that volitional choice of the lower place is the highest expression of freedom, not its negation. Cluster-level: the volitional pattern confirms that M09 characteristics require the person's own volitional engagement; they are expressions of freedom rightly directed, not suppressions of freedom for the sake of compliance.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — The pattern reveals that wilful sinning is a *volitional act with volitional consequences*: the will that sins remains the responsible agent (Eze 18:20 — "the soul who sins alone shall die") but exercises its agency in a direction that progressively constrains future agency. The characteristic is constituted by the will's exercise, but its sustained exercise progressively reshapes the will's default orientation. This is the deepest finding of the T3.6 cluster: sinning is wilful, but sustained wilful sinning is self-undermining of the very volition that produces it.

**[CHAR-10]** E — The volitional pattern reveals that the three mechanisms stand in a spectrum relative to explicit volition. Apostasy is most volitionally explicit (a deliberate departure — Act 21:21). Hypocrisy is volitionally present but socially pressured (the choice is made under group conformity pressure — Gal 2:13). Enticement is least explicitly volitional — operating through the desire-faculty that pre-empts deliberate choice (Jam 1:14). This spectrum reveals why enticement is the most insidious mechanism: it captures the will through a route that bypasses its deliberate-decision mode.

**[CHAR-11]** E — The volitional pattern reveals that sin as universal condition creates a constitutive *volitional captivity with preserved volitional identity*. The person under the condition still wills, chooses, and acts (the condition does not abolish the will) but the will's effective freedom toward God has been compromised by the enslavement: Rom 7:17/20 — "it is no longer I who do it" — the "I" remains (identity preserved) but effective agency is overridden (the enslavement operates through the person's members). This subtlety is unique to CHAR-11: the condition does not destroy the will but captures its directional freedom, producing the characteristic divided-person experience of willing the good while the condition produces the evil.

**[CHAR-12]** E — The volitional pattern reveals that sin's enslaving power produces *directional captivity without volitional elimination*: the enslaved will continues to function as a will (choosing, acting) but its free range of motion has been restricted to the sin-domain. Joh 8:34's "slave to sin" names the restriction precisely: a slave still wills and acts but within the bounds of the master's domain. The liberation (1Jo 3:9 — "cannot keep on sinning") creates a counter-directional impossibility: the born-of-God person's will is constitutionally directed away from sustained sinning, just as the enslaved will is constitutionally directed within it.

**[CHAR-13]** E — The volitional pattern reveals that the divine record is the precise moral archive of the will's history: each volitional choice either adds to or (through repentance) moves toward erasure of the record. VCG-04's 46 verses of kings who "walked in" and "did not depart from" the sins of Jeroboam are the clearest evidence: the record is constituted by sustained volitional direction. The will's "turning away" (Eze 18:21) is the key to addressing the record: not a cognitive acknowledgement alone but a volitional redirection that enables divine erasure.

**[CHAR-14]** E — The volitional pattern reveals the characteristic's paradoxical structure: the seeking requires volition (repent, go up, believe), yet the received forgiveness produces a restored volition (alive, Spirit-empowered) that was not fully available before seeking. The will must be exercised in seeking (with whatever partial freedom remains) before the forgiveness received restores the will's fuller freedom. This is the characteristic's volitional dynamic: partial will exercises toward God → forgiveness received → fuller will restored.

**[CHAR-15]** E — The volitional pattern reveals the generational pattern's dynamic: the inherited sinning condition creates a volitional default-direction toward sin (each generation's "still sinning" — Psa 78:17/32) while the potential for heart-turning remains (1Ki 8:47 — "if they turn their heart"). Generational sin is thus not volitional determinism but *volitional habituation*: the will's default is shaped by the inherited pattern, but the capacity for the decisive turn (repentance — 1Ki 8:47) is not eliminated. The will must actively turn against the inherited direction rather than merely choosing differently.

**[CHAR-16]** E — The volitional pattern reveals a distinctive feature of CHAR-16 absent from other M10 characteristics: Luk 6:32/33/34's portrait of the sinner as having *limited but real moral capacity*. Sinners are not presented as totally depraved (without any good volition) but as volitionally confined to reciprocal self-interest. This is the corpus's most nuanced inner-being finding: the sinner has genuine inner goodness within a restricted radius (loving those who love them is real love; Luk 6:33 — "sinners do the same" treats their good-doing as genuine). The sinner-identity limits the will's reach, not its reality.

**[CHAR-17]** E — The volitional pattern reveals that guilt-as-inner-state is a volitional hinge-point: when the conscience's guilt-recognition engages correctly, it redirects the will toward restitution and confession (Lev 6:4; Num 5:7); when it is suppressed or overwhelmed, the will either persists in guilt-accumulation (2Ch 33:23) or is paralysed by the punitive weight (Gen 4:13). The guilt-state itself does not determine the volitional response — the will's direction (toward remedy or away from it) is what determines whether guilt becomes productive or destructive.

**[CHAR-18]** E — The volitional pattern reveals CHAR-18's most significant inner-being dynamic: accumulated iniquity progressively constrains the will that generated it. The will begins as free agent (choosing iniquity — Eze 14:3), produces the accumulation, and is then bound by what it chose (Pro 5:22 — "held fast in the cords"). This self-generated volitional bondage makes the removal of iniquity require external divine action (Zec 3:4 — "I have taken your iniquity away"; Mic 7:19 — "he will tread our iniquities underfoot") rather than merely the will's renewed effort — the will is no longer fully free to extract itself.

**[CHAR-19]** E — The volitional pattern reveals CHAR-19's central inner-being dynamic: the will that freely chose to cross the boundary is progressively enslaved by the transgression it chose. Psa 19:13 — "great transgression" seeking dominion over the will; Pro 29:6 — ensnared. This self-generated volitional bondage distinguishes CHAR-19 from all other M10 characteristics: the will is both the agent that creates the characteristic (the deliberate crossing) and the primary victim of its sustained operation (the ensnaring). The remedy requires the will to turn (Eze 18:30) — but this turning itself requires divine assistance (Eze 18:31 — "make yourselves a new heart and new spirit").

**[CHAR-2]** E — The volitional pattern reveals that *the will alone is insufficient for moral integrity* — the will requires accurate moral information (knowledge of the commandments, awareness of the morally relevant facts) to operate in alignment with God's standards. Unintentional sinning exposes the gap between the will's capacity and the information the will needs to exercise that capacity rightly. This is a theologically important insight: moral failure does not require a wilfully defiant will; it can occur through an uninformed will operating normally within its creaturely limitations.

**[CHAR-20]** E — The volitional pattern reveals CHAR-20's most characteristic inner-being dynamic: the will that freely chose to betray is progressively enslaved by what it chose. 2Ch 28:22's Ahaz — distress producing more faithlessness — is the most extreme portrait of this dynamic: the will has become so constitutively set in the faithless direction that environmental pressure drives it further rather than correcting it. This volitional-hardening is distinct from CHAR-19's volitional-ensnaring (Pro 29:6 — ensnared in transgression) in that CHAR-20's hardening is specifically of the covenant-allegiance faculty rather than general will-bondage.

**[CHAR-21]** E — The volitional pattern reveals the same trajectory as CHAR-19 and CHAR-20: the will freely embraces perversity (Pro 2:14) and is progressively enslaved by it (2Pe 2:19). CHAR-21's distinctive contribution is the enslavement-mechanism precision: "whatever overcomes a person, to that he is enslaved" (2Pe 2:19) — the general principle that mastery produces slavery confirms that perversion's capture of the will is not unique to perversion but follows the universal mechanism of conquest-produces-slavery.

**[CHAR-22]** E — The volitional pattern reveals CHAR-22's distinctive trajectory: from volitional act (Eze 3:20 — commits injustice) through fixed character-scale (Luk 16:10 — dishonest in all) to shameless insensibility (Zep 3:5 — knows no shame). The will begins as the agent of injustice and progressively becomes the captive of the unjust character it has formed. The reversibility remains open until judgment (Eze 33:15 — the wicked can still stop doing injustice and live) but grows more constitutionally embedded with each sustained choice.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The volitional pattern is the key diagnostic of genuine vs hollow confession: the will must agree with and enact what the mouth says. 1Ch 21:17 shows this alignment at full depth — the will claims personal ownership, distinguishes itself from the innocent, and invites divine judgment on itself alone. This is confession as a full volitional act, not merely a verbal formula. The characteristic thus tests the will at its deepest level: will it own what it has done, or will it use the verbal form while directing the will elsewhere?

**[CHAR-4]** E — The volitional pattern reveals that conscience suppression *corrupts the will's operating environment*: without the conscience's moral input, the will operates without its designed check. The will remains operative (the person keeps making choices) but its choices are no longer guided by accurate moral information. The corrupted environment progressively reshapes the will's default orientations — the will that has chosen against conscience's witness repeatedly (or chosen to deny it) becomes a will whose default is conscience-absent operation (Tit 3:11 — "warped").

**[CHAR-5]** E — The volitional pattern reveals that refusal to repent is a *sustained volitional commitment to non-departure*: each moment of "did not depart from" is itself a volitional act (or sustained non-act) that constitutes the characteristic. The cumulative effect of these sustained volitional non-departures is: the will becomes increasingly bound to the sinful course (2Ki 3:3 — "clung to"), the volitional options progressively narrow (Heb 10:26), and the will's default orientation is shaped toward continued refusal. Refusal to repent is thus a self-propagating volitional condition: each act of volitional non-departure makes the next one more likely.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The volitional pattern reveals that habitual defection is the *dispositional form* of the will's sinning capacity: the will has moved from making discrete choices to sin (CHAR-1) through sustained refusal to turn (CHAR-5) into a formed dispositional default toward sin. At the CHAR-6 stage, the will no longer needs to make an active choice to sin — the habitual orientation produces sinning as its natural output. 1Jo 3:6 — "keeps on sinning" — the continuous present describes a volitional state, not a series of discrete decisions. The corrective requires not just a different choice but a reformation of the will's dispositional direction — which is what "abiding in him" (1Jo 3:6) provides.

**[CHAR-7]** E — The volitional pattern reveals that contagious sin respects the community's volitional reality while shaping it: the community members are not forced (their will is not overridden) but their will is gradually shaped through sustained authoritative sinning transmission. This is why the Hiphil causative is the perfect grammatical form: "caused to sin" names a real causal influence that respects the recipient's volitional reality while acknowledging the leader's role in shaping it. The community's sinning after contagious sin transmission is genuinely their own sinning (God holds them accountable — 1Ki 14:22) while also being causally connected to the leader's transmission.

**[CHAR-8]** E — The volitional pattern confirms that political revolt is a *full exercise of collective volitional agency* at the community-political level: the revolting community makes a decisive collective decision to break submission and act on it. The pa.sha root's deliberate-transgressive character confirms the volitional quality: the revolt is not accidental or coerced but a deliberate chosen act of the community's political will. This volitional character is what gives political revolt its moral weight — it is transgression because it is wilfully chosen, not merely circumstantially produced.

**[CHAR-9]** E — The volitional pattern reveals that sinful speech is *volitionally avoidable* (Jude 9 — Michael withholds it) but *volitionally self-binding* once practised (1Ti 6:4 — craving grows with use; VCG-03 — beast's will fully bound to its blasphemous character). The will is the decisive faculty: the same situation that Jude 9's Michael navigates with restraint is the situation where a lesser-willed creature might produce sinful speech. Restraint is possible — the will can withhold the word — but requires the inner condition of creaturely humility (deferring to God: "The Lord rebuke you" — Jude 9).

**[CHAR-1]** E — The volitional engagement pattern reveals a crucial diagnostic: because wickedness-as-settled-person-identity is primarily a volitional phenomenon (entered, sustained, and potentially reversed by the will), it is the will that must be addressed in any transformation of the characteristic. The Ezekiel corpus's consistent call for the wicked to "turn from his way" (Eze 18:21-27; 33:11-19) confirms this: the therapeutic address is volitional ("turn," "forsake" — Isa 55:7). This also explains why the characteristic cannot be overcome by external reform alone — Isa 26:10 demonstrates that even a favourable environment does not produce change in the wicked person without the volitional turn. The characteristic is, at its root, a volitional commitment.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The volitional pattern reveals the most analytically significant distinction between CHAR-2 and CHAR-1. CHAR-1 (wickedness as settled person-identity) is primarily volitional — the will has chosen a direction and settled into it. CHAR-2 (evil as constitutional inner nature) is primarily constitutional — the will operates within a structural constraint that the tree-nature metaphor (Mat 7:17-18 — VCG-02) names precisely: the nature constrains the will's productive range. The will can still choose how to express the constitutional evil (choice of specific evil acts), but it cannot produce good fruit from the constitutional condition without a transformation of the condition itself. The volitional engagement reveals the characteristic as deeper than willful choice — it is the condition that shapes what the will can choose to produce.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The volitional pattern reveals an important distinction from CHAR-1 (wickedness as settled person-identity): in CHAR-1, the volitional-directional dimension is primary. In CHAR-3, volition is the faculty through which the abominable inner conditions are expressed and maintained (Eze 14:6 — the will facing the abominations; Pro 13:19 — the will bonded to evil), but the primary dimension is the relational-moral verdict rather than the volitional direction per se. The volitional engagement shows that abomination is not merely incidental or passive — it requires sustained volitional commitment to the abominable inner conditions. The call to repent (Eze 14:6) shows that volitional reversal is both possible and required.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The volitional pattern reveals that idolatrous abomination is fundamentally a will-phenomenon: it begins with a volitional choice and ends with a bound will. This explains the Deuteronomic preventive strategy (VCG-02): address the will before the attachment forms (don't covet, don't learn, don't worship) because once the attachment is formed, the will is progressively constrained. The Ezekiel restoration trajectory (Eze 14:6 context: "repent and turn away from your abominations") also addresses the will — the therapeutic address is volitional. The volitional pattern confirms the characteristic's primary dimension (T1.8.1) and shows that volitional intervention is the primary address at both the preventive and therapeutic stages.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The volitional pattern reveals that iniquity as scheming is both constituted by the will (it is chosen — Job 36:21 — VCG-04) and eventually dominates the will (Psa 119:133 — VCG-04: seeking dominion). This paradox — the will creates what then masters it — is a defining feature of the characteristic's inner-being mechanism. The trajectory of the will is: free choice of iniquity → progressive constraint of the will by iniquity's hold → potential dominion of iniquity over the will → required divine intervention to re-open the ear and enable return (Job 36:10 — VCG-04). The volitional pattern confirms the characteristic as a will-phenomenon that turns against the will's own freedom.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The volitional pattern reveals the characteristic as the most extreme form of will-hardening in the M10b cluster: VCG-01's blasphemy under divine judgment (Rev 16:9/11/21 — VCG-01) shows a will that persists in defiance through maximum external pressure. The will's refusal to repent is not merely passive (failing to change) but active (generating defiant speech as its expression of continued refusal). This active-volitional defiance under judgment is the characteristic's most analytically distinctive feature: the will is not merely wrong but actively self-asserting against the divine in the moment of judgment. The volitional pattern reveals CHAR-6 as the characteristic of the maximally hardened will.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's volitional pattern reveals the theological paradox at the heart of M10b: inner evil is freely chosen (volitionally entered) but becomes self-enslaving (the will progressively constrained by what it chose). Char 5's "this you have chosen rather than affliction" (Job 36:21) paired with Char 5's "iniquity seeking dominion" (Psa 119:133) and Char 6's will-hardening under judgment (Rev 16:9/11/21) together articulate this paradox at cluster scope. The cluster reveals that the will's freedom is real at entry and progressively diminished over time — making the call to repentance urgent precisely because the window of free volitional response is finite and progressively narrowing.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The volitional engagement at the perimeter reveals the characteristic as morally significant without being primarily moral in its origin. The condition itself arrives through bodily mechanism, not primarily through sin of the will. But the will's response to the condition — whether it seeks remedy, maintains the duty not to transmit, exercises avoidance discipline, and pursues discernment — is where moral accountability resides within the characteristic's domain. Num 19:20 makes this structural contrast explicit: the defiled state is not the moral fault; willful refusal of remedy is.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The volitional pattern reveals the characteristic's most paradoxical feature: it binds the will while leaving the appearance of freedom intact. The person in moral-inner defilement-slavery (Rom 6:19) does not experience themselves as enslaved in the way a physically bound person does — they actively pursue their defilement (Eph 4:19: "greedily"). This reveals the characteristic as one that co-opts the will rather than simply overriding it: the will is not removed but is redirected, making the bondage feel like free activity. This is the mechanism that makes the characteristic so resistant to self-correction without external intervention.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The volitional pattern reveals the characteristic as one of repeated, deliberate corporate choice — the community is not innocently corrupted but repeatedly chooses the defilement despite divine warning (Eze 20:7: "do not defile yourselves with the idols of Egypt"; 20:18: "do not defile yourselves with their idols" — commands that are given precisely because the will could choose otherwise and repeatedly does not). The characteristic is thus a record of sustained volitional defection, not an overwhelming external force. The corporate will is the primary site of accountability.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The volitional pattern reveals the characteristic as the most acute form of will-subjugation in the cluster — not gradual erosion of conscience (Characteristic 2) or misdirection of corporate will (Characteristic 3) but sudden total override of individual will by an external spiritual agent. This addresses a dimension of human volitional vulnerability distinct from the moral-inner dimension: the human will can be externally overridden, not merely internally corrupted.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's volitional pattern reveals four distinct types of human volitional experience within the defilement domain: (1) structured obligation (Char 1 — the will operates within defilement's prescribed management system, bearing obligations but not being corrupted); (2) self-generated bondage (Char 2 — the will's own prior choices produce a condition that then constrains the will itself — the most paradoxical form); (3) sustained deliberate defection (Char 3 — the will is fully functional and fully choosing wrongly, repeatedly, corporately — the most clearly volitional form); (4) external override (Char 4 — the will is present but cannot express itself — the most extreme form). This taxonomy reveals that the M10c cluster does not have a single account of how defilement relates to the will. The four modes span from the will as morally neutral but obligated (Char 1) through self-corrupting (Char 2) and deliberately defecting (Char 3) to completely subjugated (Char 4). The cluster thus addresses the full range of human volitional vulnerability.

questions.question_text: In this verse, does the characteristic engage the agency faculty — the capacity to act, initiate, and make happen — and if so, how? Record none if it does not.

findings.session_b_note:
Yes — the motivational dimension of forgiveness is one of its most analytically significant features:

**Motivation generated by received forgiveness:**
- Luk 7:47 — forgiveness received → love produced → relational acts of devotion (the woman's anointing, weeping). The received forgiveness is the motivational origin of the subsequent relational acts. OBS-064-029 establishes this as a causal chain.
- The structural logic of Mat 18:35 — having received enormous forgiveness motivates (or should motivate) extending forgiveness to others. The parable's moral argument is a motivational argument: your received forgiveness should be the inner ground of your forgiving others.

**Motivation as precondition of the forgiving act:**
- Visceral compassion (splagchnizomai, Mat 18:27) — the gut-level compassion is the named motivational impulse from which the master's act of forgiving flows. Motivation (compassion) precedes and generates the volitional act.

**Fear of God as motivating sustained orientation:**
- Psa 130:4 — the knowledge of forgiveness available with God produces reverential fear, which is itself a sustained motivational orientation toward God (waiting, hoping — Psa 130:5-7).

findings.session_b_note:
Yes — agency is one of the most directly and consistently evidenced faculty-engagements in the compassion data. The registry description states: "Compassion always faces outward toward the one suffering and produces action." The production of action is definitional to compassion in this programme.

**Splanchnizō as action-generating:** Every splanchnizō event in the Gospels produces action: healing (Mark 1:41; Matt 20:34), feeding (Matt 15:32; Mark 8:2), raising the dead (Luke 7:14-15 — following v.13's compassion), teaching (Mark 6:34), crossing social boundaries (Luke 10:33-35 — the Samaritan's full investment in the stranger's recovery). The compassion-movement is never terminal — it always arrives at agency.

**Eleēmosunē as institutionalised agency:** G1654 (almsgiving) is the normalised social form of compassion-agency: the concrete act of giving through which the inner disposition becomes external action. The semantic development from pity to almsgiving (Pass 1, term 20) traces how compassion's agency becomes institutionalised in the community's social practice.

**The parable of the prodigal (Luke 15:20):** The father is splanchnizō, then runs, falls on the son's neck, kisses him — a cascade of agency. The compassion-movement produces an urgent, immediate, uninhibited expression of agency. Nothing intervenes between the gut-stirring and the running. This is compassion at its most agentive: the inner movement is immediately and fully expressed in action without hesitation or restraint.

findings.session_b_note:
Agency is engaged but in a notably reduced or redirected form. Contrition as a condition of lowliness is structurally opposed to assertive agency — the contrite person does not act from a position of self-initiated power. However, the data shows some agency-engagement:

- The act of bringing the broken heart as sacrifice (Psa 51:17) is an agentic move — bringing, offering, presenting. Even the broken person acts.
- The petition of Psa 51:8 ("let me hear") is a speech-act directed toward God — an agentic appeal even from the broken position.
- The Hithpael "allowing oneself to be crushed" is, paradoxically, an agentic act of non-resistance.

*Partial: agency is engaged in a paradoxical form — the agency of the one who acts from weakness and brokennness by bringing themselves before God. Full assertive agency is absent.*

findings.session_b_note:
Yes. Agency is present in multiple modes.

**Human agency in fellowship-extension:** 1Jo 1:3 — the one who has seen and heard *proclaims* — an active initiating act that extends fellowship. The agent takes what they have received and creates new fellowship.

**Human agency in fellowship-refusal:** 2Cor 6:14 — the person who obeys the command *do not be unequally yoked* exercises active refusal-agency. Fellowship can be actively declined as well as actively entered.

**Human agency in choosing companions:** Psa 119:63 — *I am a companion of all who fear you* — the psalmist's active positioning of himself among the fear-of-God community is an agentive act.

**Divine agency:** God grants promises (2Pe 1:4), God joins the sticks (Eze 37:19), God serves as witness (Mal 2:14). The divine agency in fellowship is more direct and effective than human agency — it does not depend on conditions being met in the same way.

**Finding 062-GRAMM-001** establishes that fellowship shows mixed grammatical subjects: divine and human agency both operate, sometimes simultaneously.

findings.session_b_note: Agency is engaged and required. Mic 6:8 requires active human doing — "to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly." The goodness defined here is not a state but a practice — it requires the person to initiate and sustain action. The "garment" language of Col 3:12 ("put on therefore... kindness") frames goodness as an active choice to take up — an agentive act. Pro 16:32 ("he who rules his spirit than he who takes a city") names self-governance as an agency act with positive moral value. 2Th 1:11's "every resolve for good" is a person's own resolve — the agentive capacity is intact and engaged. Goodness does not bypass agency; it requires it and enables it. (OBS-067-OBS-027, OBS-067-OBS-040, SBF-067-Q040)

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-067-003: T3 reveals that goodness is the most comprehensively faculty-engaging characteristic in the programme's current analytical record. Every faculty except creativity (T3.5 — silence confirmed) shows subs…
findings.finding_value: T3 reveals that goodness is the most comprehensively faculty-engaging characteristic in the programme's current analytical record. Every faculty except creativity (T3.5 — silence confirmed) shows substantive engagement: perception (tasting and seeing goodness), cognition (moral evaluation and ranking), memory (covenantal knowing and moral reckoning), affect (stable rooted gladness vs fragile surface gladness), volition (reconstituted toward the good), agency (active expression required and enabled), moral evaluation (goodness as the normative anchor of the evaluative faculty), conscience (goodness calibrates the conscience's standard), conscientiousness (integration of all faculties into sustained moral expression), and relational capacity (dual-directional overflow). The tier as a whole reveals that goodness is not a specialist characteristic — it is an integrating one. The person who possesses genuine goodness has every faculty engaged and aligned. This comprehensive faculty-engagement is what distinguishes genuine goodness from its surface forms: surface goodness (the Haman problem) engages affect without engaging conscience or volitional alignment; genuine goodness integrates all.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-103-003: Love engages all eleven inner faculties, but five show the richest engagement: (1) Identity and self-understanding — love is the primary faculty through which the person knows who they are: being-love…
findings.finding_value: Love engages all eleven inner faculties, but five show the richest engagement: (1) Identity and self-understanding — love is the primary faculty through which the person knows who they are: being-loved (agapētos) constitutes identity from the outside; what-one-loves constitutes identity from the inside. The person is doubly defined by love. (2) Relational capacity — love is the faculty's active content: it builds (Joh 13:34), sustains (Lam 3:22), and restores (Luk 15:20) relational capacity. (3) Memory — love's sustaining faculty: love without memory cannot maintain itself through absence (Jer 31:20 — 'I do remember him still'). (4) Moral sensitivity — love calibrates what the inner person registers as morally significant; the love-of-God requirement generates the hate-evil requirement (Psa 97:10). (5) Attention — love determines what the person perceives as worth attending to (Phili 4:8 — think on what is lovely). The weaker engagements: creativity (indirect, evidenced through Song-form) and conscience (inferred, not directly named). Overall: love is the faculty-most-engaged characteristic in the programme, operating through perception, reason, memory, imagination, desire, emotion, moral sensitivity, conscience (indirectly), identity, and relational capacity simultaneously.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-030-003: Reading T3 as a whole reveals that contrition engages virtually every inner faculty — with one exception (creativity, T3.5 — data silent). The pattern across the engaged faculties is consistent: contr…
findings.finding_value: Reading T3 as a whole reveals that contrition engages virtually every inner faculty — with one exception (creativity, T3.5 — data silent). The pattern across the engaged faculties is consistent: contrition deepens and opens rather than impairs or bypasses. It deepens perception (opens to divine address), deepens cognition (enables accurate self-knowledge), deepens affect (makes grief and longing both fuller), redirects volition (from self-assertion to God-direction), converts agency (from self-directed to God-seeking), deepens moral evaluation (requires and enables accurate self-assessment), deepens conscience (allows conscience's verdict to reach the spirit/heart), deepens conscientiousness (grounds it in inner reality rather than performance), and enables relational capacity (specifically for divine nearness). The single thread running through all faculty engagements is: contrition removes self-protective barriers — it is the inner-being event in which every protective reflex is dissolved, leaving the person fully exposed and open. This is why it enables rather than impairs every faculty: openness is the condition in which all faculties function most truthfully.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-030-019: The faculty tier (T3) establishes that contrition opens every engaged faculty toward God (perception deepened for divine address, volition redirected toward God, agency converted to God-seeking, relat…
findings.finding_value: The faculty tier (T3) establishes that contrition opens every engaged faculty toward God (perception deepened for divine address, volition redirected toward God, agency converted to God-seeking, relational capacity enabled for divine nearness); the relational tier (T4) shows that the primary relational direction is indeed toward God. T3 and T4 are aligned: the faculty effects all point in the same direction that T4's relational analysis names as the primary direction. The faculties do not pull in multiple directions — they converge on the vertical relational axis. This convergence is analytically significant: it means contrition is constitutively God-directed at the faculty level, not merely structurally positioned toward God.

findings.finding_value: Reading T3 as a whole reveals that every faculty engagement with fellowship runs in both directions — right fellowship deepens and enables; wrong fellowship degrades and constrains. Perception, cognition, moral evaluation, conscience, conscientiousness, and relational capacity are all deepened by rightly directed fellowship and progressively impaired by wrongly directed fellowship. The single exception is creativity (T3.5 — data silent). The pattern is systematic: fellowship is not merely a relational characteristic but a faculty-shaping characteristic — it progressively shapes every inner faculty in conformity with its object. This makes the choice of fellowship objects one of the most consequential inner-being decisions a person makes: the consequences extend through every faculty across time.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-064-003: T3 reveals forgiveness as uniquely faculty-comprehensive — it engages more named faculties with greater specificity than any other characteristic reviewed in this revision series. Memory is explicitly…
findings.finding_value: T3 reveals forgiveness as uniquely faculty-comprehensive — it engages more named faculties with greater specificity than any other characteristic reviewed in this revision series. Memory is explicitly named (Jer 31:34 — divine memory as the content of forgiveness) and distinctively: forgiveness transforms memory in both directions — God's memory of sin is set aside permanently; the human forgiver releases the active use of memory against the offender. Affect is bidirectionally engaged: as prerequisite (somatic compassion, Mat 18:27) and as product (love, Luk 7:47; reverence, Psa 130:4). Conscience is addressed and purified by forgiveness (Heb 9:14). Volition is constitutive (the heart-level release is chosen). Cognition is enabled (Jer 31:34 — forgiveness → knowing God). The single silence is creativity (T3.5). T3's synthesis: forgiveness is the most faculty-comprehensive characteristic in the current review set — it reaches every major faculty with specific evidenced content, most strikingly in the memory domain.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-019: T3's faculty engagements all point in the same relational directions that T4 identifies as primary. Conscience (T3.9) is engaged in both the seeking-forgiveness direction (human-to-God: confession as …
findings.finding_value: T3's faculty engagements all point in the same relational directions that T4 identifies as primary. Conscience (T3.9) is engaged in both the seeking-forgiveness direction (human-to-God: confession as conscience's public verdict) and the giving direction (human horizontal: the conscience that recognises the offence to be released). Memory (T3.3) is engaged in the God-to-human direction (divine "remember no more" — Jer 31:34) and the human-giving direction (releasing the memory's active use against the offender). Volition (T3.6) drives the giving direction (heart-level release is chosen). The vertical-horizontal interdependence (T4 structural claim) is the relational expression of T3's conscience-and-volition faculty account: the person whose conscience has accurately received the magnitude of divine forgiveness has the volitional capacity to extend horizontal forgiveness.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-003: T3 reveals two structurally distinctive findings about compassion's faculty engagement. First, creativity is entirely silent (three S ratings) — the most informative absence in the tier: compassion re…
findings.finding_value: T3 reveals two structurally distinctive findings about compassion's faculty engagement. First, creativity is entirely silent (three S ratings) — the most informative absence in the tier: compassion responds, it does not originate or create. It is the most responsive of the faculties-engaging characteristics. Second, affect and moral action are structurally unified in compassion — not sequentially related but simultaneous. Affect is the mechanism of movement (splanchnizō is both the felt inner event and the cause of the action), not a precursor or accompaniment. This is unique among the characteristics reviewed: in most other registries, affect and volition are distinguishable stages; in compassion, the felt movement is already the morally motivated action beginning. A third distinctive finding: compassion converts moral knowledge into motivated action — it is the motivational ground of conscientiousness, not a product of it. The conscience faculty engagement reveals compassion as conscience-healing: it addresses the pitiable condition that conscience perceives as a moral claim, resolving the tension between moral knowledge and moral incapacity. The three relational modes (building/sustaining — chesed; restoring/repairing — splanchnizō; extending across difference — Good Samaritan) are a new finding not in the instruction typology.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-003: T3 produces four structurally significant findings about grace's faculty engagement. First, grace is agency-constituting rather than agency-replacing: 1Cor 15:10 holds in explicit paradox — "I worked …
findings.finding_value: T3 produces four structurally significant findings about grace's faculty engagement. First, grace is agency-constituting rather than agency-replacing: 1Cor 15:10 holds in explicit paradox — "I worked harder than any of them, though it was not I but the grace of God that is with me." Agency is not displaced but constituted by grace. This relationship holds in paradox that the T3.6 prompt options (enable/deepen/bypass/impair) cannot accommodate — a prompt design limitation noted for catalogue revision. Second, grace produces moral clarity (T3.8 — sharpens moral evaluation rather than bypassing it): the person who recognises grace has made a precise moral evaluation (they know they received what they did not deserve). Third, grace and conscience are mutually necessary: grace is the condition within which conscience can operate fully without destroying the person; conscience without grace produces condemnation; grace without conscience produces presumption (T3.9). Fourth, grace is the primary relational faculty developer in the registry's evidence — it reaches every relational register (vertical access, horizontal forgiving, speech-grace) and enables each one. Creativity (T3.5) is the one genuinely silent faculty — not an impairment but a non-engagement: grace receives and constitutes, it does not create.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-019: T3's agency-constituting finding (grace constitutes rather than replaces agency — 1Cor 15:10) and T4's human-to-God direction (supplication as the human posture of appeal — requiring genuine human age…
findings.finding_value: T3's agency-constituting finding (grace constitutes rather than replaces agency — 1Cor 15:10) and T4's human-to-God direction (supplication as the human posture of appeal — requiring genuine human agency in the act of plea) are structurally aligned. The constituted agency (T3.7) is precisely the agency that supplication requires: the creature must genuinely appeal, not merely receive passively. T3's finding that grace and conscience are mutually necessary (T3.9) corresponds to T4's relational-access finding: grace transforms the threshold of human-to-God approach (prosagōgē — SD035) from impassable to open, which is the relational expression of T3.9's constitutional finding that grace creates the condition within which conscience can operate fully without destruction. T3 names the inner-being event; T4 names the relational consequence of the same event.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-021: T3's faculty findings explain several patterns in T6's co-occurrence landscape. The seeking co-occurrence dominance (R140 — 40 verses) is partly explained by T3.6's agency-constituting finding: seekin…
findings.finding_value: T3's faculty findings explain several patterns in T6's co-occurrence landscape. The seeking co-occurrence dominance (R140 — 40 verses) is partly explained by T3.6's agency-constituting finding: seeking requires the constituted agency that grace provides for its own reception (SD026 — grace giving the capacity for supplication). The power cluster co-occurrences (strength R187 — 15 verses, might R198 — 10 verses) confirm T3.7's agency-constituting finding at the cross-registry level: grace producing agency is registered as co-occurring with power/strength across the corpus. T3.8's moral clarity finding explains the guilt co-occurrence (R073 — 10 verses): the moral clarity grace produces is most visible at the point of moral failure, and the co-occurrence reflects this — grace and guilt appear together because grace produces the moral clarity that accurately names the guilt it addresses.

findings.session_b_note: Yes — agency is engaged on both sides of the covenant relationship, asymmetrically. (1) Divine agency: God is consistently the primary covenant-agent — he initiates (karat berit — OBS-034-046), he swears (OBS-034-052), he remembers and acts on covenant (OBS-034-038), he writes on the heart (OBS-034-040), he administers through the Spirit (OBS-034-061). Divine agency in covenant is unconditional and foundational — God's covenant-agency is the basis on which the covenant exists at all. (2) Human agency: covenant-entry is a human agency act — the person joins, commits, makes the oath (Neh 10:29 — OBS-034-035). The bilateral Sinai covenant calls for sustained human agency in obedience-keeping. Prohibited covenant (3304-003 — OBS-034-048) names the exercise of human agency in the wrong direction. (3) The new covenant shifts the agency dynamic: God acts within the person to produce the conditions of response — the human is more receiver than initiator in the new covenant's primary mode. Human agency remains but is now derivative of and enabled by prior divine agency within.

Divine agency in covenant is unconditional and foundational — God's covenant-agency is the basis on which the covenant exists at all. (2) Human agency: covenant-entry is a human agency act — the person joins, commits, makes the oath (Neh 10:29 — OBS-034-035). The bilateral Sinai covenant calls for sustained human agency in obedience-keeping. Prohibited covenant (3304-003 — OBS-034-048) names the exercise of human agency in the wrong direction. (3) The new covenant shifts the agency dynamic: God acts within the person to produce the conditions of response — the human is more receiver than initiator in the new covenant's primary mode. Human agency remains but is now derivative of and enabled by prior divine agency within.
