findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-099-003: T3 reveals that kindness engages a remarkably wide range of inner faculties — nine of eleven are evidenced with at least partial engagement. The two genuine absences (imagination and creativity) are s…
findings.finding_value: T3 reveals that kindness engages a remarkably wide range of inner faculties — nine of eleven are evidenced with at least partial engagement. The two genuine absences (imagination and creativity) are structurally coherent: kindness is relational and loyally directed, not generative. The most significant faculty engagements are: (a) volition — kindness is chosen, not merely felt; the "put on" and "love kindness" language makes this constitutive; (b) agency — chrēsteuomai names love actively exercising kindness — kindness is enacted, not passive; (c) relational capacity — kindness constitutes relationships in their quality, not merely accompanies them; (d) conscientiousness — the chasid represents the full integration of moral awareness, will, and action in consistent reliable pattern; (e) taste as the primary perceptive mode — "tasted that the Lord is good" establishes that kindness is encountered experientially before it is understood conceptually. The pattern across all engaged faculties: kindness integrates the whole inner person — it does not operate as a single-faculty characteristic but as a whole-person orientation. T3's most significant intra-tier finding: kindness is a multi-faculty characteristic whose breadth of engagement reflects its status as a constitutive relational orientation rather than a single affective or volitional act.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-009: T1's finding that kindness is primarily a disposition (not merely an act) is confirmed and deepened by T3's faculty analysis. The disposition identified in T1 requires the full engagement of multiple …
findings.finding_value: T1's finding that kindness is primarily a disposition (not merely an act) is confirmed and deepened by T3's faculty analysis. The disposition identified in T1 requires the full engagement of multiple faculties — volition (it is chosen), agency (it is enacted), conscientiousness (moral awareness + will + action integrated), and relational capacity (it constitutes relationship quality) — which together explain why it is dispositional rather than episodic: a characteristic that engages this many faculties simultaneously is, by its nature, a settled whole-person orientation rather than a single-faculty response. T1's three-mode finding (disposition / deliberate act / Spirit formation) is reflected in T3's faculty pattern: the dispositional mode engages conscientiousness and relational capacity; the deliberate act mode engages volition and agency; the Spirit-formation mode produces the integrated faculty engagement over time. The counterfeit (chrēstologia — T1.4.3 / Q&A-024) maps onto T3's faculty analysis as the pathology of the speech-mode: it engages the communicative faculty while bypassing genuine moral evaluation and conscientiousness — presence of outward form without inner faculty integration.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-014: T2's finding that kindness is located in the heart and moves outward through a constitutional trajectory (Spirit → heart → disposition → acts) connects structurally with T3's finding that kindness eng…
findings.finding_value: T2's finding that kindness is located in the heart and moves outward through a constitutional trajectory (Spirit → heart → disposition → acts) connects structurally with T3's finding that kindness engages the heart's integrating faculties — volition, agency, conscientiousness, moral evaluation, relational capacity, and conscience. The heart in T2 is not merely a location label but the integrating site where all these faculties converge (T2.3.2 — Q&A-045). The constitutional movement pattern in T2 (downward-outward from Spirit to acts) is powered by the multi-faculty engagement that T3 documents: the Spirit-formation produces the heart-level disposition, but the heart exercises volition (choosing to be kind), agency (enacting kindness), and conscientiousness (sustaining kindness reliably over time) to move the disposition into action. The T3 finding that kindness engages taste as the primary perceptive faculty (1Pet 2:3 — "tasted that the Lord is good") is the perceptive entry point for the T2 constitutional movement: the person first tastes divine kindness, then the Spirit forms it in the heart, then the heart's faculties exercise it outward. The two tiers together describe a complete inner-to-outer movement with both location (T2) and mechanism (T3) identified.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-019: T3's faculty analysis and T4's relational interface analysis are structurally interdependent in a specific way: the faculties that kindness most strongly engages (volition, agency, relational capacity…
findings.finding_value: T3's faculty analysis and T4's relational interface analysis are structurally interdependent in a specific way: the faculties that kindness most strongly engages (volition, agency, relational capacity, conscientiousness) are precisely the faculties required for the T4 relational circuit to operate. Relational capacity (T3.11) is what makes the T4 interfaces possible at all — the person must have the constitutional equipment for genuine connection before kindness can flow in any direction. Agency (T3.7) is what makes the T4 giving direction concrete — not passive benevolence but enacted care. Conscientiousness (T3.10) is what makes the T4 circuit sustainable across time — the chasid who reliably keeps covenant. The T4 communal interface (Moses's intercession; the chasidim assembly) requires an intercessory capacity (T3 — memory + relational capacity) that knows how to appeal on behalf of others. The two tiers together describe a portrait of the whole inner person oriented outward: T3 names the inner equipment and T4 names the relational directions in which that equipment is deployed.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-020: T3's faculty findings and T5's formation findings reveal a bidirectional relationship: the faculties that kindness engages are both the tools through which formation occurs and the products of formati…
findings.finding_value: T3's faculty findings and T5's formation findings reveal a bidirectional relationship: the faculties that kindness engages are both the tools through which formation occurs and the products of formation. Volition (T3) is exercised in the deliberate acts of kindness (Rut 3:10, 2Sa 10:2) that form the chasid's character — formation happens partly through the repeated exercise of volitional kindness. Conscientiousness (T3) is both engaged by kindness and deepened through its practice — "let not steadfast love forsake you" (Pro 3:3) implies that conscientiousness requires maintenance, and that maintenance in turn deepens conscientiousness. The T5 finding that suffering does not impair kindness formation (Lam 3:22, Job 6:4, Gen 44:29/32) maps onto the T3 faculty engagement in suffering contexts: conscience (T3.9 — the burden of Judah's surety-pledge), moral evaluation (T3.8 — Hos 6:6's priority ranking), and relational capacity (T3.11 — Moses's intercessory solidarity) are all engaged precisely in the suffering mode of kindness. The two tiers together: the inner faculties are both the instruments and the beneficiaries of kindness formation.

findings.finding_value: T3 maps inner faculty engagement; T4 maps relational directions. The synthesis: the relational capacity (T3.11) and the relational interfaces (T4) describe the same reality from different angles — the inner equipment (T3.11) and its external directions (T4). The conscience (T3.9 — gateway faculty for peace) connects directly to T4.2 (human to God): the human's movement toward God in confession (T4.2) is precisely the conscience-exercise that opens the peace-channel (T3.9). The volitional faculty (T3.6) connects to T4.3 (giving): genuine extension of peace requires authentic inner orientation (T4.3.2) — which is exactly the T3.6 finding that the giving of peace is a volitional act flowing from identity (Psa 120:7). findings.session_b_note: Yes — agency is the primary external form of this characteristic. Every instance of na.tan in the inner-being register is an act — something is given, transferred, offered. findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-060-003: T3 as a whole reveals that this characteristic engages virtually every inner faculty in the programme's 11-faculty model — the only consistent gap is creativity (T3.5, S across three prompts). The pat…
findings.finding_value: T3 as a whole reveals that this characteristic engages virtually every inner faculty in the programme's 11-faculty model — the only consistent gap is creativity (T3.5, S across three prompts). The pattern of engagement is not uniform: perception is engaged as precondition (God hears before giving); cognition is constituted (wisdom is given, not generated); memory is deepened (the narrative-temporal dimension of covenantal giving); affect is the source of giving (compassion, anger) and the target of transformation (mourning→gladness); volition is called forth and elevated (genuine giving cannot be coerced); agency is the bridge between disposition and act; moral evaluation both produces and is produced by the characteristic; conscience is engaged indirectly through Spirit-forming and prophetic warning; conscientiousness at the human apex is the full integration of all three (moral awareness, will, act). Relational capacity is intrinsic — every mode is two-party. What T3 reveals as a whole: faithfulness-as-giving is not a faculty-specific characteristic but a whole-person characteristic — it recruits and integrates all active faculties into a unified inner-being act. The creativity silence is the only dimension where the data cannot confirm engagement.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-002: The disposition-in-action definition (T1) requires the full inner faculty set to be operational (T3). The triadic architecture (source → act → object) maps directly onto faculty engagement: the source…
findings.finding_value: The disposition-in-action definition (T1) requires the full inner faculty set to be operational (T3). The triadic architecture (source → act → object) maps directly onto faculty engagement: the source requires affect (compassion/anger motivating), volition (choosing to give), and moral evaluation (assessing rightness); the act requires agency (initiating the transfer); the object requires relational capacity (attending to the other's condition). No individual faculty is the characteristic — but the characteristic integrates all of them in a coordinated whole. What this pair reveals: the definition of faithfulness-as-giving is not an abstract proposition but a faculty-integration event. The characteristic exists only when the full inner-being architecture — affective, volitional, agentive, relational — is engaged together. This is why the apex instance (Job 1:21, Isa 50:6) represents the highest form: all faculties operating in unified inner-being act.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-013: The faculty engagement pattern (T3) and the formation arc (T5) are directly linked: the faculties engaged by the characteristic are precisely the faculties that are formed through it. Cognition is bot…
findings.finding_value: The faculty engagement pattern (T3) and the formation arc (T5) are directly linked: the faculties engaged by the characteristic are precisely the faculties that are formed through it. Cognition is both constituted by endowing giving (T3.2 — wisdom deposited) and is the target of formation (T5.5 — Spirit given to instruct shapes over time). Memory is engaged by the covenantal mode (T3.3 — narrative-temporal dimension) and is the sustained environment of covenantal formation (T5.5 — the history of received giving shapes identity). Agency is both the bridge between disposition and act (T3.7) and is restored/enabled by eschatological giving (T3.7 Q&A-087 — depressed agency is renewed). Suffering reveals (T5.4 — tests the characteristic) and tests affect, volition, and conscientiousness (T3.4, T3.6, T3.10). What this pair reveals: the characteristic forms the person by engaging and developing the same faculties it requires for its own expression. Formation is circular in this characteristic: it needs faculties to be enacted, and its enactment develops those faculties further.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-014: The full-person faculty integration (T3 — all major faculties engaged) and the producing/produced-by structural position (T6) reveal that the characteristic's hub position is sustained by its faculty-…
findings.finding_value: The full-person faculty integration (T3 — all major faculties engaged) and the producing/produced-by structural position (T6) reveal that the characteristic's hub position is sustained by its faculty-integration property. It produces worship (R121, R176) because worship is the proper faculty response to received giving (T3 — perception of divine giving → affect of gratitude → volition of blessing → relational act of worship). It is produced by love (R103) and trust (R059) because love and trust are the inner-being sources from which the giving proceeds (T3 — affect motivates, volition commits, agency enacts). The causal sequences (T6.2) are faculty sequences in disguise: each sequential step is a faculty transition (suffering perceived → compassion moved → giving enacted). What this pair reveals: the structural network of this characteristic in the inner-being landscape is held together by faculty transitions. The characteristic is a hub because it is where multiple faculty-driven causal sequences converge and produce giving as their common expression.

**[A1 — God Righteousness]** Yes — God's righteousness is expressed through his acts: saving, delivering, vindicating, judging (A1-004; A1-002). The divine agency is expressed through righteousness — what God does expresses who he is. This establishes the model: righteous character expresses itself in righteous action.

**[A2 — Human Righteousness]** Yes — "execute justice and righteousness" (Eze 45:9, VSG 911-001); "do justice and righteousness and deliver from the hand of the oppressor" (Jer 22:3, VSG M26-A2-012). Agency is required: righteousness that does not express itself in just action is the concern of A2-003 (distortion and counterfeit). The person who is righteous acts righteously — the inner condition generates agency.

**[B — Moral Uprightness]** Yes — "he who walks righteously and speaks uprightly, who despises the gain of oppressions, who shakes his hands, lest they hold a bribe" (Isa 33:15, VSG 1212-002). Walking, speaking, shaking hands — all are acts of agency expressing the inner disposition of uprightness. Uprightness generates specific agentive expressions.

**[C — Justification]** Yes — "go, and from now on sin no more" (Joh 8:11, adjacent to C through E-connection). Justification (C) and the freedom from condemnation (E) that it produces result in a commission to agency: the freed and justified person is sent to act differently. The justified person is described as becoming an "heir" (Tit 3:7) — heirs act, they are not merely passive recipients.

**[D — Avenging Justice]** Yes — the cry for justice (944-001) is an agentive act: the person takes the situation to God rather than passively accepting it. The commissioned avenger (Rom 13:4: "an avenger who carries out God's wrath") is an agent of divine retributive justice. Agency is central to D.

**[E — Condemnation]** Yes — "condemn not, and you will not be condemned" (Luk 6:37, VSG 3201-001). The act of condemning is an agentive act. Self-condemnation (autokatakritos) is the conscience acting against the self — an inner agency directed inward.

**[F — Moral Reckoning]** Yes — the reckoning act produces agency: "count yourselves dead to sin... therefore do not let sin reign" (Rom 6:11–12). The reckoning (cognitive-volitional act) issues directly in commanded action. The reckoning faculty is the inner preparation for agency.

**[G — Structural Opposites]** Yes — "they band together against the life of the righteous and condemn the innocent to death" (Psa 94:21, VSG 1225-002). Wickedness expresses itself in agentive harm — it actively oppresses and destroys. Wickedness is not merely passive absence of righteousness; it generates its own destructive agency.

**[CLUSTER — T3.7]** E. Agency is engaged throughout the cluster. The consistent pattern is: inner condition (righteousness/wickedness) → agentive expression (righteous acts/harmful acts). Righteousness in M26 is not an interior state that remains interior — it issues in action. The cluster portrait is one of morally active persons: executing justice, speaking truth, delivering from oppression, entrusting vengeance, crying for justice, refraining from condemning. Righteousness is agentive.

findings.finding_value: The sha.men verb pattern (growing fat) involves a specific form of agency-reduction: Deu 32:15 ("Jeshurun grew fat and kicked") — the kicking is agency, but it is reactive agency directed at God, the one who provided the abundance. The fat-hearted person's agency is turned against God, not toward him. The at-ease person's (sha.a.nan) agency is specifically disengaged from appropriate action: "woe to those at ease in Zion" (Amo 6:1) — they are present but not acting as moral agents.

M46-B's hardness is not passivity but active agency deployed in morally wrong directions.

findings.finding_value: M01-A **enables** agency by generating ethical and covenant-faithful action: Exo 1:17 (the midwives' fear of God "functions as an inner moral allegiance that overrides the king's command — it is a reverent loyalty to God that controls the will even under coercive royal authority" — agency enabled against tyranny by fear of God); Jer 26:19 (Hezekiah "feared the Lord and entreated him, and disaster was averted — the inner reverence is shown to be an **active posture that turned toward God in prayer**, producing a concrete historical outcome"). Fear-of-God is an agency-enabling characteristic.

M01-B's relationship to agency is complex: acute fear can either enable agency (Gen 32:7: Jacob's fear immediately drives strategic action — splitting the camp, sending gifts ahead) or disable it (1Sa 17:24: all men of Israel flee without deliberation). The object and intensity of the fear determines whether it enables or disables agency.

M01-C and D primarily **impair or disable** agency: Gen 35:5 (terror paralyzing the will to pursue), Eze 7:27 (hands paralyzed — agency physically disabled), Jer 46:5 (terror causing Egypt's warriors to "abandon their posts and flee — inner resolve shattered by overwhelming dread").

M01-C and D primarily **impair or disable** agency: Gen 35:5 (terror paralyzing the will to pursue), Eze 7:27 (hands paralyzed — agency physically disabled), Jer 46:5 (terror causing Egypt's warriors to "abandon their posts and flee — inner resolve shattered by overwhelming dread").

M01-G timidity **suppresses** agency: Mat 25:25 (burying the talent instead of investing — the action not taken); Luk 19:21 (fear of the severe master producing inaction). Timidity is the failure of the agency-courage that would take faithful action.

The agency faculty is: **enabled** by M01-A (courage to act against tyranny, prayer in the face of disaster, ethical restraint as a form of moral agency); **conditionally engaged** by M01-B (enabling or disabling depending on the fear-object and intensity); **disabled** by M01-C, D (paralysis, hands immobilized, flight); and **suppressed** by M01-G (passive self-preservation rather than initiative). The pattern mirrors the volitional finding: ordered fear enables agency; disordered fear impairs or suppresses it.

Yes, extensively. The action-driving corpus (M02-B-VCG-02) is definitionally about anger issuing into agency: Moses smashing tablets (Exo 32:19), Asa imprisoning the prophet (2Ch 16:10), Samson striking thirty men (Judg 14:19). In each case anger is the inner engine driving the external act. Agency is not just associated with anger — it is what anger characteristically produces.

Yes, extensively. The action-driving corpus (M02-B-VCG-02) is definitionally about anger issuing into agency: Moses smashing tablets (Exo 32:19), Asa imprisoning the prophet (2Ch 16:10), Samson striking thirty men (Judg 14:19). In each case anger is the inner engine driving the external act. Agency is not just associated with anger — it is what anger characteristically produces.

The provocation corpus (M02-D-VCG-01) also engages agency: God's anger, once aroused, drives active decisions — giving Israel over to enemies (Judg 2:14), sending plague (Psa 106:29). The agency is divine, but the structure is the same: anger is the inner energy, agency is the outward expression.

Yes. Grief activates agency in the prayer-deliverance pattern (M03-D-VCG-01): distress drives the person to act — to cry out, to seek God, to make vows. Grief also activates agency in the mourning-and-action pattern: the morally motivated distress of servants leads directly to reporting injustice (Mat 18:31 — M03-C-VCG-02). Nehemiah's grief immediately drives him into sustained prayer and fasting (Neh 1:4 — M03-B-VCG-02).

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes. Exultation is expressed through agency — the shout of praise (Psa 32:11), the coming before God in singing (Psa 100:2), the approaching the altar (Psa 43:4). The person who exults acts: they come, they sing, they shout, they proclaim. The inner state moves the person into concrete action.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes. Joy consistently produces and motivates action: Act 8:39 (the eunuch "went on his way rejoicing" — joy motivating continued journey); 2Cor 8:2 (joy overflowing into generous giving — agency produced by joy); Isa 55:12 ("you shall go out in joy" — joy as the mode of redemptive departure); Act 5:41 (apostles rejoicing → continuing to teach in Jesus' name — joy motivating ongoing apostolic agency); Mat 13:44 ("in his joy he goes and sells all that he has" — joy as the inner motivator of radical action); Jer 31:13 (young women rejoice in the dance — joy producing movement and active festivity).

**[CHAR-7]** E — Yes. Act 5:41 (apostles rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer for Jesus' name → continuing to teach — Suffering-Joy producing continued agentive mission); Act 16:34 (the jailer coming to faith in crisis → communal agentive response of bringing Paul and Silas into the house, setting food before them, entire household rejoicing — agency around the crisis); Luk 10:21 (Jesus' Spirit-rejoicing is immediately followed by the declaration to the Father and instruction to the disciples — the rejoicing generates continued agentive proclamation).

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes. Neh 2:18 — the people's resolve to build ("let us rise up and build") was stirred by hearing of God's good hand — Gladness-recognition producing agency; 1Sa 11:9 — the men of Jabesh glad at the news of coming deliverance → implicit enabling of their sustained resolve; Lam 3:27 — "it is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth" — the gladness of formative discipline enables the agentive capacity of the mature person. The wisdom-evaluative corpus (M04-L-VCG-02, 03) produces agency through clarified moral vision: knowing what is genuinely good enables acting accordingly.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes, extensively: (1) **Sovereign divine agency** — M04-H-VCG-01: God's cha.phets/eudokeo produces immediate, unrestricted action (Psa 115:3; 135:6; Isa 55:11; 44:28 — Cyrus fulfilling God's purpose); divine Delight is the most agentively-direct characteristic in the entire programme — God's pleasure immediately produces action; (2) **Human urgent action** — Gen 34:19 (Shechem's delight → "did not delay to do the thing") — the most dramatic human agency-from-Delight example; (3) **Diplomatic agency** — the M04-H-VCG-03 "as it seems good to you" formula throughout the historical books frames Delight as the standard by which agency is authorised and directed; (4) **Obedience-agency** — Joh 8:29 (Jesus always doing what pleases the Father — continuous agentive faithfulness produced by Delight-in-the-Father); 1Jo 3:22 (doing what pleases God → receiving prayer answers — agency motivated by and productive of Delight).

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes, indirectly: (1) **Worship agency** — the ni.cho.ach corpus requires the worshiper to act (offer the sacrifice, wash the entrails, burn the fat) — agency in right worship produces the Pleasure-quality of the aroma; (2) **Psa 27:4's seeking** — "one thing have I asked… that will I seek" — the seeking act is agentive; (3) **Pro 15:26's gracious speech** — speaking pleasant words is an agentive act that extends Pleasure to others; (4) **Neh 9:17 negative** (in M04-I but adjacent) — Israel's failure to act in response to God's wonders shows agency failure as blocking the right Pleasure-response.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Yes: (1) **Proclamatory agency** — "declare his glory among the nations, his marvellous works" (1Ch 16:24; Psa 96:3) — active going-out to declare; (2) **Generational-transmission agency** — "we will not hide them from their children, but tell to the coming generation" (Psa 78:4) — active intergenerational teaching; (3) **Jos 3:5** — Israel's active consecration in anticipation of God's wonders; (4) **Mar 1:27** — the crowd's immediately acting to question among themselves following the wonder-seizure; (5) **2Ch 26:15** — Uzziah being "marvellously helped" enabling his productive agency (making machines, defending the city).

**[CLUSTER]** E — All seven engage agency and all seven produce or motivate action, but with distinctive agentive outputs: (1) **Most agentively-direct**: Delight (Char 4) — the most agentively-immediate characteristic in the cluster; Gen 34:19's "did not delay" and God's sovereign cha.phets both show Delight translating directly to action without intermediate steps; (2) **Most agentively-communal**: Joy (Char 2) — consistently produces communal festive action, giving (2Cor 8:2), proclamation, and sustained mission (Act 5:41); (3) **Most agentively-missional**: Wonder (Char 6) — the primary agentive output is proclamation to the nations (1Ch 16:24; Psa 96:3) and generational transmission (Psa 78:4); (4) **Most agentively-liberating**: Suffering-Joy (Char 7) — the characteristic that frees the will from circumstantial dependency: the person who rejoices amid suffering is not waiting for circumstances to improve before acting; (5) **Agency through worship-practice**: Pleasure (Char 5) — the carefully-offered sacrifice requires agentive ritual precision; the worship-Pleasure relationship is sustained through disciplined agentive practice.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes. Shame's primary relationship with agency is *impairing* — it withdraws the person's capacity to act, initiate, and present themselves. Ezr 9:6 — the inability to lift the face is the literal inability to present oneself before God to initiate worship or petition. Psa 127:5 — the man without sons "cannot speak with his enemies in the gate" — shame as the loss of public agency. Job 10:15 — "I cannot lift up my head" — shame as the inner paralysis of the agency to move forward. The backward-turning of the enemies under shame (Psa 35:4; 129:5) shows agency reversed — shame drives movement backward rather than forward.

**[CHAR-2]** E — CHAR-2 withdraws or collapses the recipient's agency: they cannot speak (Mat 22:12), cannot re-enter public space (2Sa 10:5), must retreat (Jer 48:39). In VCG-03, God is the agent; the proud person's agency is precisely what is overridden. CHAR-2 is the enforced withdrawal of agency from the person whose pride had inflated it beyond its proper scope.

---

**[CHAR-3]** E — The dishonorer exercises agency in the act of worth-denial (VCG-01). The dishonoured's agency may be affected when dishonour restricts their relational capacity (the poor man whose case cannot receive justice, Jam 2:6). The structural mode (VCG-02) restricts the recipient's agency in terms of what they can access or what roles they can occupy.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — CHAR-4's functioning enables the exercise of principled moral agency — the person who recognises and renounces the shameful can act with integrity. The inverted conscience (VCG-03) produces misdirected agency — the person acts, but in the direction of what is actually shameful. VCG-02's disordered desire overwhelms agency with appetite.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — Agency is impaired in the recipient by CHAR-5: Psa 14:6 — the plans of the poor are shamed (targeted for dismissal) — their capacity to act on their own plans and hopes is suppressed by the contempt. Paul's concern that contempt toward Timothy (1Cor 16:11) would "devalue his ministry and undermine his standing" shows agency-impairment as the downstream effect of sustained CHAR-5. Conversely, the act of throwing off the cloak (Mar 10:50) is the regaining of agency in response to a stronger worth-assignment from Jesus.

---

**[CHAR-6]** E — CHAR-6 enables agency: the person with clean hands and a blameless heart can approach God's altar (Psa 26:6) — the agency of worship is enabled by CHAR-6. The incapacity for innocence (Hos 8:5) impairs agency in the specific domain of approach to God — the people cannot exercise the agency of genuine covenant approach because innocence-capacity has been lost.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — The most consistent cluster-level finding on agency: the shame-characteristics impair agency (Chars 1, 2, 3, 5 all show shame withdrawing the capacity to act, speak, and present oneself); the counter-characteristics restore or protect agency (Char 6 enables the agency of approach to God; Char 4's functioning conscience enables principled moral agency). The cluster's agency-narrative: the shame-field takes agency from the person; the positive moral conditions (innocence, functioning conscience) return it. The christological dimension is critical: Jesus's voluntary acceptance of shame (Chars 1 and 5 in the passion narrative) demonstrates that agency can be maintained within the shame-condition — his "despising the shame" (Heb 12:2) is the highest form of volitional agency over against shame's impairing pull. The resurrection's reversal (Act 4:11 — the rejected cornerstone; 1Cor 15:43 — raised in glory) is the eschatological restoration of full agency from the shame-field's impairment.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes. CHAR-1 is an active, energising characteristic in the agency register. Psa 10:2 (vc=33963, M08-A4-VCG-03): "arrogance is the inner driving force behind the wicked person's hot pursuit of the poor — it is pride operating as agency, propelling oppressive action and entrapment of the vulnerable." Psa 36:11 (vc=33966, M08-A4-VCG-03): arrogance "personified as a foot that tramples and a hand that drives away — an aggressive inner force in the wicked." Psa 140:5 (vc=33954, M08-A4-VCG-02): "the proud person's inner disposition drives outward hostile action — they secretly lay traps and snares, showing that arrogance produces calculating aggression against others." Psa 31:18 (vc=33964, M08-A4-VCG-03): "pride here is the inner attitude that emboldens lying lips to speak insolently against the righteous — it is the motivating disposition behind contemptuous, oppressive speech." CHAR-1 drives specific, forceful, initiated action.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes, directly. CHAR-2 is constitutively agential — it is the will's assertion expressed through action. Deu 1:43 (vc=34123, M08-B-VCG-01): "you went up into the hill country" — a specific initiated action. Exo 21:14 (vc=34122): planning and executing murder — premeditated agency. Mar 10:42 (vc=55588, M08-B-VCG-03): rulers "lord it over" and "exercise authority over" others — the domineering agency of CHAR-2 in the social-power register. Mat 24:49 (vc=55613, M08-B-VCG-03): the wicked servant "beats fellow servants" — CHAR-2 as aggressive, self-authorised action against social others.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes. Boasting is inherently an agential act — the boaster initiates a public speech-act in the social field. 2Cor 10:13 (vc=33888, M08-C-VCG-02): Paul "constrains his boasting to the sphere God assigned" — boasting as an act with geographic/relational scope, requiring deliberate initiation. 2Cor 11:30 (vc=33873, M08-C-VCG-02): "I will boast of the things that show my weakness" — Paul initiates a specific boasting-act. The VCG-01 condemned form is agential too: Pro 27:1 (vc=33359): "do not boast about tomorrow" — the prohibition addresses an initiated speech-act.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes, through the actions the inflated self-picture generates. 1Cor 4:18 (vc=33938, M08-D-VCG-01): "some are arrogant, as though I were not coming to you" — the arrogant persons have taken actions (or adopted postures) on the basis of their presumed freedom from accountability. 1Ti 6:4 (vc=33925, M08-D-VCG-02): the conceited person engages in controversy and quarrels about words — an active, energised agency directed toward intellectual combat. 1Cor 5:2 (vc=33940, M08-D-VCG-01): the puffed-up community's failure to act on moral failure (failing to mourn and address it) is itself an agential failure enabled by CHAR-4.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes. Hab 2:9 (vc=34169, M08-E-VCG-02): "shame on him who builds his house by unjust gain, setting his nest on high to keep himself safe" — CHAR-5 generates a specific strategic agency: the deliberate accumulation of position through unjust means for self-securing purposes. Eze 16:30 (vc=57959, M08-E-VCG-02): "brazen, unrestrained harlotry" — specific acts of self-will from a position of structural power. The national proud-might corpus (Eze 30:6–32:12) implies collective national agency directed by CHAR-5: the Egyptian army exercising force from a posture of proud national confidence.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All five characteristics engage the agency faculty. The cluster reveals a consistent finding: every M08 characteristic is agentially expressed — pride consistently produces action in the world. CHAR-1: predatory pursuit of the poor (Psa 10:2, M08-A4-VCG-03), physical and social domination. CHAR-2: the specific transgressive act (going up to battle, speaking the unauthorised word, murder). CHAR-3: the deliberate boasting speech-act and social self-display. CHAR-4: the controversy-craving agency generating intellectual combat; the arrogant persons' presumptuous postures (1Cor 4:18, M08-D-VCG-01). CHAR-5: the strategic accumulation of position through unjust gain (Hab 2:9, M08-E-VCG-02), the imperious self-will actions. The cluster-synthesis: M08 is an active cluster — every characteristic generates outward action. The prideful person does not merely feel proud but acts on their pride.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Agency is engaged, but specifically directed toward yielding to rather than initiating from. Heb11:8 — Abraham "obeyed when he was called" — his agency is exercised in the act of going, but the initiative was the divine call; his agency is the active response to external initiative rather than self-originated action. Act6:7 — the priests "became obedient to the faith" — their agency exercised in the decisive act of reorientation. 2Cor9:13 — the generous giving that flows from submission to the gospel — agency in action directed by the submission of the will. Agency in submission is real but specifically *responsive* rather than self-originated: the person exercises genuine agency in yielding and in the actions that flow from yielding.

**[CHAR-3]** S — The two-verse corpus does not directly evidence engagement of the agency faculty by contrition. The characteristic is evidenced as a state the person is in rather than a capacity to act. The agency dimension is primarily on God's side in this corpus: God is the one who draws near, saves, dwells, and revives.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes, particularly through okneō (Act9:38). The disciples urge Peter to come "without delay" — the expected quality is the agency that moves immediately and without hesitation. The characteristic expressed through okneō absence is precisely the *prompt, unimpeded exercise of agency* in response to genuine need. Metriopatheō also involves agency: the high priest actively deals gently with the erring — the gentle dealing is an agentive act, not a passive state.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes. 1Ti3:4 — the overseer managing his household "with all dignity" — the agency of household management is exercised through and with the characteristic: the managing is the agentive act; the dignity is the quality with which it is exercised. Tit2:7 — "show integrity, dignity" — the showing is an agentive act that carries the characteristic. Agency is the vehicle through which semnotēs is expressed.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Yes. The freely-moved heart immediately produces the agentive act of bringing: Exo35:5 — "let him bring"; Exo35:22 — "brought brooches and earrings"; 2Ch29:31 — "brought burnt offerings." The willing heart directly enables and produces the agentive act. 1Ch28:21 — "every willing man… will be wholly at your command" — the willing person's agency is fully available for service. Agency in this characteristic is maximally expressed: the willing-hearted person acts fully and freely.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Agency is engaged, but in a distinctive directional form: humility exercises agency *downward* rather than upward. The ka.na corpus evidences the person *initiating* the act of humbling — Josiah humbling himself when he hears the word (2Ch34:27), Manasseh initiating entreaty in distress (2Ch33:12), Hezekiah humbling in response to identified pride (2Ch32:26). These are genuine acts of inner agency — the person does something. Paul's self-lowering in 2Cor11:7 is an agentive choice ("I humbled myself so that you might be exalted"). Phili2:8 — Christ "humbled himself by becoming obedient to the point of death" — the agentic form is striking: Christ is the *subject* who acts downward. Agency in humility is real agency but it is agency in the direction of self-lowering rather than self-assertion or self-elevation.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All six engage agency, but in distinctive directional forms. *Agency downward* (CHAR-1): the person exercises genuine agency in choosing the lower path; Phili2:8 is the supreme instance — the Son's agency moves toward death. *Agency responsive* (CHAR-2, CHAR-4): agency yielding to the authority's claim (CHAR-2) or moving immediately toward the need without self-protective hesitation (CHAR-4 — okneō). *Agency in receiving* (CHAR-3): the person's agency in remaining open to divine reviving rather than fleeing the broken state. *Agency ordering* (CHAR-5): the overseer's agency of household management exercised through and with the characteristic (1Ti3:4). *Agency maximised* (CHAR-6): the willing-hearted person gives more than required (2Ch29:31), serves fully (1Ch28:21), acts immediately — CHAR-6 is the agency-maximising characteristic in the cluster. Cluster-level: CHAR-6 and CHAR-1 represent opposite but complementary forms of agency — CHAR-1's agency chooses the lower path voluntarily; CHAR-6's agency exceeds minimums freely. Together they bound the cluster's agency landscape: voluntary descent (CHAR-1) and voluntary excess in giving (CHAR-6).

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — Agency is fully engaged. Wilful sinning is an act — something done, initiated, made to happen by the person. The verbal grammar of the corpus (cha.ta as action verb — committed, sinned, sins) confirms this. Gen 43:9 and 44:32 (Judah voluntarily assuming agency for Benjamin's safety) show agency in the responsibility-for-another mode. Jos 7:20 (Achan — "this is what I did") shows agency as the defining element of the confession: the act is personally initiated. The deterrence corpus (VCG-03) shows agency being disciplined: Job 31:30 ("I have not let my mouth sin") — the "not let" is an agency-restraint act.

**[CHAR-10]** E — Agency is engaged differently across the three mechanisms. (1) *Enticement*: the enticers of 2Pe 2:14/18 are fully agentive — they deliberately entice, their hearts are trained, they actively target unsteady souls. The enticed person's agency is being captured and redirected. (2) *Hypocrisy*: Gal 2:13 — "acted hypocritically along with him" — the acting-alongside is an agentive choice; Barnabas "was led astray" — his agency was captured by the collective hypocrisy. (3) *Apostasy*: Act 21:21 — "forsake Moses" — the forsaking is an agentive act of departure.

**[CHAR-11]** E — Agency is fully engaged — but the condition operates by redirecting rather than eliminating it. Rom 6:13 — "do not present your members to sin as instruments for unrighteousness" — the agency of presenting the members is real; the person actively presents them (the presenting is a genuine agentive act). The condition captures this agency and deploys it toward sin. Rom 6:16 — "whoever you present yourselves as obedient slaves" — the act of presenting is agentive; the condition's enslavement operates through real agentive presentations, not through the abolition of agency.

**[CHAR-12]** E — Agency is engaged through its distorted form under enslavement. Joh 8:34 — "everyone who practices sin is a slave to sin" — the practice of sinning is an agentive act (the person is doing the sinning); but the agency that generates the enslavement is the very agency that becomes enslaved. The practicing-sinner is agentively sinning while that agency progressively loses its free directional range. Rom 6:1 — "continue in sin" — the continuation is an agentive ongoing state; the enslaved person's agency operates within the sin-domain.

**[CHAR-13]** E — Agency is engaged as both the generator and the addresser of the record. (1) *Agency generating the record*: Isa 5:18 — "who draw sin as with cart ropes" — the active, effortful drawing of sin toward the self is a fully agentive act that creates the record; Isa 30:1 — "who carry out a plan... that they may add sin to sin" — the deliberate agentive execution of plans against God accumulates the record. (2) *Agency addressing the record*: Num 5:7 — "he shall confess his sin that he has committed. And he shall make full restitution" — the agentive confession and restitution are the human side of the record-addressing mechanism.

**[CHAR-14]** E — Agency is engaged through the seeking acts. 2Ch 29:23 — "they laid their hands on them" — the assembly's agentive act of hand-laying; 2Ch 29:24 — "the priests slaughtered them and made a sin offering" — the priestly agentive acts. Act 2:38 — "repent and be baptized" — both repentance (inner agentive turn) and baptism (outer agentive submission) are acts of the person's agency. Exo 32:30/31 — Moses's agentive intercession: "I will go up to the Lord" and his verbal naming of the sin before God.

**[CHAR-15]** E — Yes — through both rebellion and confession. (1) *Agency in rebellion*: Psa 78:17 — "rebelling against the Most High in the desert" — the rebellion is an agentive act against God; (2) *Agency in confession*: 1Ki 8:47 — "turn their heart... and repent and plead" — the turning, repentance, and pleading are all agentive acts through which the community addresses the inherited condition; Jer 8:14 — "we have sinned against the Lord" — the corporate acknowledgment is an agentive speech-act.

**[CHAR-16]** E — Agency is engaged through the sinner's active expression of their identity. Heb 12:3 — "sinners directed such hostility against himself" — the sinner's agency is expressed in active opposition against Christ; the hostility is an agentive act. Jude 15 — "all their deeds of ungodliness... and the harsh things that ungodly sinners have spoken against him" — the deeds and speech are agentive expressions of the sinner-identity. Pro 1:10 — "if sinners entice you" — the sinners are agents actively recruiting others into their identity-pattern.

**[CHAR-17]** E — Agency is engaged through the restitution-demands that guilt recognition generates. Lev 6:4 — "realized his guilt and will restore what he took" — the guilt-recognition produces agentive restitution; Num 5:7 — "he shall confess... shall make full restitution... giving it to him to whom he did the wrong" — the guilt-state drives a series of agentive acts (confession, restitution, giving). 1Sa 25:24 — Abigail's "on me alone, my lord, be the guilt" — a proactive agentive assumption of another's guilt-liability. Jer 3:13 — "only acknowledge your guilt" — the acknowledgment is an agentive act of moral self-declaration.

**[CHAR-18]** E — Agency is engaged through the active expression of iniquity and the active pursuit of its remedy. (1) *Agency in iniquity's enactment*: Isa 59:3 — "your hands are defiled with blood and your fingers with iniquity" — the hands are the active members of iniquity's enactment; Isa 5:18 — "those who draw iniquity with cords of falsehood, who draw sin as with cart ropes" — active, purposeful pursuit of iniquity; (2) *Agency in iniquity's remedy*: Lev 26:40 — "if they confess their iniquity" — the verbal act of confession is an agentive decision; Hos 14:2 — "take with you words and return to the Lord" — the return-initiative requires agentive action.

**[CHAR-19]** E — Agency is engaged through both the transgression's active commission and the active pursuit of its resolution. (1) *Agency in transgression's commission*: Isa 5:18 (CHAR-18 cross, but relevant here) — "those who draw iniquity with cords... sin as with cart ropes" — active, purposeful pursuit; Amos 4:4 — "come to Bethel and transgress" — ironic invitation to purposeful transgressive action; (2) *Agency in transgression's resolution*: Pro 28:13 — "he who confesses and forsakes them" — the forsaking is an agentive act; Eze 18:31 — "cast away from you all the transgressions" — the casting-away is a commanded agentive act of the will.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Agency is fully engaged in the sinning act (the person did something — Lev 4:2; 1Sa 14:33) and in the remedy sequence (the person brings an offering — Num 15:27; Balaam offers to turn back — Num 22:34). The person is the agent of both the inadvertent sin and the remedy. Lev 5:5 ("when he realizes his guilt... and confesses") — the confession is an agency-act: the person is the active subject of both realization and confession.

**[CHAR-20]** E — Agency is engaged through both the commission and the communal extension of faithlessness. (1) *Individual agentive commission*: Eze 17:20 — "for the treachery he has committed against me" — the specific agentive act named as the ground of judgment; 1Ch 10:13 — "he broke faith with the Lord in that he did not keep the command" — the specific agentive choices constituting the faithlessness; (2) *Communal agentive extension*: Num 31:16 — "caused the people of Israel to act treacherously against the Lord in the incident of Peor" — Balaam's agency incited communal faithlessness; Jos 7:1 — Achan's individual agency attributed to all Israel.

**[CHAR-21]** E — Agency is engaged through both active commission and the reversal to passivity. (1) *Active agency*: Pro 6:14 — "devises evil, continually sowing discord" — active agentive commission; Rev 19:2 — "the great prostitute who corrupted the earth with her immorality" — active agentive corruption reaching to cosmic scale; Isa 32:7 — "plans wicked schemes to ruin the poor" — deliberately agentive; (2) *Passive captivity*: 2Pe 2:19 — "slaves of corruption" — the agency is captured; Jude 10 — "destroyed by all that they understand instinctively" — the active agent has become the passive victim of their own instinct.

**[CHAR-22]** E — Agency is central — CHAR-22 is defined by what is *done* toward others. (1) *Active agentive wrongdoing*: Psa 58:2 — "your hands deal out violence on earth"; Rev 19:2 (adjacent) — corrupting the earth; Rev 18:5 — crimes heaped high; (2) *Agentive harm*: Job 29:17 — "I broke the fangs of the unrighteous" — the unjust person as a predatory agent; 2Sa 7:10 — "violent men shall afflict them no more" — the violent as active agents of harm; (3) *Agentive civic injustice*: Mic 3:10 — "who build Zion with blood" — agency deployed toward constructing unjust social structures.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes. Agency is engaged in two ways. (1) *Claiming agency for the sin*: 1Ch 21:17 — "Was it not I who gave command to number the people? It is I who have sinned and done great evil" — the confessor claims their own agency as the source of the sin, refusing to transfer responsibility. 2Sa 24:17 — "Behold, I have sinned, and I have done wickedly. But these sheep, what have they done?" — distinguishing the confessor's agency from the people's non-agency. (2) *Exercising agency in the confession act*: Luk 15:18 — "I will arise and go to my father" — the confession involves a deliberate agentive movement (arising and going) that enacts the inner resolution.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Agency is fully engaged in conscience suppression — the person continues to act, sin, and claim innocence. Jer 2:35 — the person acts on the claim "I am innocent" by assuming divine anger has passed and proceeding accordingly. Ecc 8:12 — the sinner who "does evil a hundred times" is exercising full agency in the sinning. The characteristic is not passivity but active sinning-without-conscience-awareness. Agency is the vehicle through which conscience suppression manifests in the external world.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Agency is fully engaged throughout. The Kings corpus shows kings who continue to act — governing, walking, serving — in the direction of the sinful course: 1Ki 16:31 — Ahab "went and served Baal and worshiped him" — his agency is fully operational, directed toward idolatry. The sinful course does not merely persist by default; agents are actively walking in it (2Ki 13:6 — "walked in them"). Heb 10:26 — "go on sinning deliberately" — the present tense going-on names continuous agentive action.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Agency is fully engaged — the habitually sinning person continues to act, to build, to fear, to pursue. 1Ki 16:31 (adjacent — CHAR-5) and 2Ki 17:7 show the community actively "fearing other gods" — a full exercise of agentive devotion directed toward wrong objects. Hos 8:11 — "Ephraim has multiplied altars" — the multiplying of altars is an agentive act: the community is actively building, investing, and institutionalising the sinning pattern. The habitual sinner's agency is fully operational; it is simply directed toward the sinning course and the structures that support it.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Agency is fully engaged in contagious sin at both ends. Leader's agency: 1Ki 16:2 — "you have walked in the way of Jeroboam and have made my people Israel to sin" — the leader's agentive actions (walking, making-to-sin) are the mechanism of transmission; Jer 32:35 — "they built the high places" — constructive agentive action building the sinning structure. Community's agency: 1Ki 14:22 — "Judah did what was evil in the sight of the Lord, and they provoked him to jealousy with their sins" — the community is agentively sinning, not merely being passive recipients; their agency is active in the transmitted sinning direction.

**[CHAR-8]** E — Agency is fully engaged. The political revolts in the corpus are agentive acts: "Moab rebelled" (2Ki 1:1), "Edom revolted... and set up a king of their own" (2Ki 8:20), "Israel has been in rebellion" (1Ki 12:19) — all name communities as active agents. The constructive act of 2Ki 8:20 — "set up a king of their own" — is particularly agency-rich: not only breaking from but building alternative governance. Political revolt is constitutively agentive.

**[CHAR-9]** E — Agency is fully engaged — sinful speech is an agentive speech-act. Mat 26:65 — "He has *uttered* blasphemy" — the utterance is an agentive act attributed to Jesus (falsely) or to anyone who speaks sinfully. Rev 13:5/6 — "it *opened* its mouth... It *opened* its mouth to utter blasphemies" — the beast's agentive speech-opening is deliberate and sustained. Jude 9 — Michael "did not *presume* to pronounce" — the withholding of agency from the speech-act is what prevents sinful speech.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes. Agency is strongly engaged, primarily in the form of directed harmful action. VCG-03 (pride and directed hostility, 22V) is the primary evidence base: the wicked actively pursue the poor in arrogance (Psa 10:2), plot and gnash teeth against the righteous (Psa 37:12), arm themselves with destructive intent (Psa 37:14), lurk as predatory trappers (Jer 5:26), surround the righteous and pervert justice (Hab 1:4). VCG-09 also shows agency in economic harm: the wicked accepts bribes to pervert justice (Pro 17:23), sweeps others away through violence (Pro 21:7), and covets the spoil of evildoers (Pro 12:12). The agency of the wicked person is consistently productive — they act, initiate, and bring harm into being.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes. Agency is engaged and fully operational in the constitutionally evil person. The characteristic does not impair the capacity to act — it redirects it. Mat 12:35 (vc=14420 — VCG-03): the evil person "brings forth evil" — active originating agency. 3Jo 10 (vc=14454 — VCG-04): Diotrephes "talking wicked nonsense against us, and not content with that, he refuses to welcome the brothers, and also stops those who want to and puts them out of the church" — multiple layered agency acts (speech, refusal, obstruction, expulsion) all expressing the constitutional inner malice. Act 17:5 (vc=14452 — VCG-04): wicked men "formed a mob, set the city in an uproar, and attacked" — organized active agency in service of constitutional inner disposition.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes. Agency is engaged both in the production of abomination and in the called-for response. Deu 25:16 (vc=65936 — VCG-01): "all who act dishonestly" — agency in practice produces abomination. Deu 27:15 (vc=65937 — VCG-04): "makes a carved image" and "sets it up in secret" — active creative-constructive agency producing abomination. Pro 21:27 (vc=1693 — VCG-03): "how much more when he brings it with evil intent" — agency in religious offering compounded by intentional corrupt motivation. Eze 44:6 (vc=66001 — VCG-04): "O house of Israel, enough of all your abominations" — the accumulated acts of the rebellious inner disposition are the corporate agency that has generated the abominable state.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes. Agency is fully engaged and oriented toward idolatrous production and installation. VCG-03 (17V — historical reform narratives) documents the most concentrated agency evidence: Solomon "built a high place" (1Ki 11:7 — vc=65899 — VCG-03 — constructive agency); kings "did according to the abominations of the nations" (2Ki 21:2 — vc=65941 — VCG-03 — comprehensive agency conformity); Josiah "took away all the abominations" (2Ch 34:33 — vc=65946 — VCG-03 — reforming agency). Jer 32:34 (vc=65907 — VCG-04): "they set up their abominations in the house" — deliberate placement as an act of bold agency. Eze 7:20 (vc=65909 — VCG-05): "they made their abominable images" — creative-productive agency.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes. Agency is extensively evidenced and actively engaged in executing iniquity. Mic 2:1 (vc=38217 — VCG-02): "when the morning dawns, they perform it, because it is in the power of their hand" — agency (the power to make things happen) is the executing faculty. Isa 10:1 (vc=38191 — VCG-02): "those who decree iniquitous decrees, and the writers who keep writing oppression" — institutional agency producing systematic harm. Isa 59:7 (vc=38203 — VCG-02): "swift to shed innocent blood" — agency directed toward violent harm. Job 4:8 (vc=38186 — VCG-04): "those who plow iniquity and sow trouble reap the same" — agricultural agency metaphor: iniquity is sown with active effort, like farming.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Yes. Agency is directly engaged through the speech acts. Rev 13:6 (vc=14356 — VCG-01): "opened its mouth to utter blasphemies" — the utterance is an agentive act. Rev 16:9 (vc=14352 — VCG-01): "cursed the name of God" — cursing as an agentive act. Joh 18:30 (vc=14378 — VCG-03): the accusers "delivered him over" — the false charge is part of an agentive process of handing Jesus over to Pilate. Jude 8 (vc=14354 — VCG-01): "blaspheme the glorious ones" — an agentive targeting of specific beings through speech. The characteristic requires agency for its operation: the speech act must be initiated, formulated, and delivered through deliberate agency.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All six characteristics fully engage the agency faculty — confirming M10b as a characteristically agentive cluster. Char 5 (Mic 2:1 — dawn performance of nocturnally devised schemes), Char 4 (VCG-03 — kings institutionalising abominations through royal authority; Josiah purging through royal agency), Char 6 (Rev 13:6 — "opened its mouth" as deliberate agency; Joh 18:30 — accusers delivering Jesus), Char 1 (the wicked person's active pursuit of evil), Char 3 (Pro 16:12 — evil is abomination even for kings who do it — agency acknowledged), Char 2 (the person actively presenting body members to unrighteousness — Rom 6:13). The cluster's agency pattern: M10b characteristics require and deploy full active agency — they are not passive conditions but energetically enacted orientations and acts.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes. Several agency-acts are directly prescribed by the characteristic's normative system: (1) washing: throughout M10c-A, the defiled person must wash clothes and bathe — active agency in pursuit of resolution (Lev 11:25, 15:5, 15:16, etc.); (2) presenting for priestly examination: the person with suspected skin disease must present themselves for assessment (M10c-B-VCG-02 — the examination procedures imply the person's presentation); (3) removing contaminated material: Lev 14:40-45 (M10c-B-VCG-04) — stones and plaster from a diseased house are actively removed; the condemned house is demolished; (4) carrying out the filth from the Holy Place: 2Ch 29:5 (M10c-A-VCG-08) — Levites are commanded to carry out impurity as a deliberate consecration act; (5) self-declaration: Lev 13:45 (M10c-B-VCG-03) — the person bears disease must actively cry out their status. Each of these is an agency-act required by the characteristic.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes, but in a distorted form. Agency — the capacity to act, initiate, and make happen — is engaged through the characteristic's call to cleansing (2Cor 7:1: "let us cleanse ourselves"; 2Cor 6:17: "go out from their midst, and be separate from them"; Isa 52:11: "purify yourselves"). The response to the characteristic requires active agency: the person must act to separate, purify, cleanse. In the negative direction, the characteristic produces a perverted agency: Eph 4:19 (VCG-02) — "greedy to practice every kind of impurity" — the person actively pursues defilement; their agency is intact but misdirected.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes, in both directions — defilement-generating agency and cleansing-agency. Defilement-generating agency: Eze 23:7 (VCG-02) — "she bestowed her whoring upon them... and she defiled herself with all the idols" — active agency in the pursuit of idolatrous defilement. Jer 7:30 (VCG-03) — the sons of Judah "set their detestable things" in God's house — deliberate agency of installation. Isa 30:22 (VCG-02) — "then you will defile your carved idols... you will scatter them as unclean things. You will say to them, 'Be gone!'" — the agency of the will actively declaring and rejecting its former idolatrous attachments. Cleansing-agency: 2Ch 23:19 (VCG-08 context) and Eze 4:14 (VCG-05) — the prophet's lifelong maintained purity through agency of avoidance.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes — the agency faculty is the most directly impaired. Luk 8:29 (VCG-01): "driven by the demon into the desert" — agency is taken over by the spirit; the person does not act, they are acted upon. Luk 9:42 (VCG-01): "the demon threw him to the ground and convulsed him" — the body is the instrument of the spirit's violent agency. Mar 5:13 (VCG-02): the spirits exercise agency (moving from the man to the pigs); during possession the man had no equivalent agency over the spirits.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All four characteristics engage the agency faculty. Characteristic 1 prescribes extensive required agency-acts (washing, presenting for examination, self-declaring, removing contaminated material — the entire remedial system is an agency-act system). Characteristic 2 engages agency through the call to active cleansing (2Cor 7:1 — "let us cleanse ourselves"; 2Cor 6:17 — "go out from their midst") and shows a perverted agency in the advanced state (Eph 4:19 — "greedy to practice every kind of impurity" — fully active but misdirected). Characteristic 3 engages defilement-generating agency (Eze 23:7 — actively pursuing idols; Jer 7:30 — deliberately installing abominations) and cleansing-agency (Isa 30:22 — actively rejecting former idols). Characteristic 4 displaces the person's agency entirely, substituting the spirit's agency for the person's own (Luk 8:29 — "driven by the demon"; Luk 9:42 — "threw him to the ground").

findings.session_b_note:
**Enables and deepens motivation:** Received forgiveness functions as a motivational generator — producing love (Luk 7:47), reverence (Psa 130:4), and hope (Psa 130:5-7) as sustained motivational orientations. The depth of the motivational output is proportional to the depth of forgiveness received ("forgiven much → loved much").

**Impairs motivation (when absent):** The withholder's "poisoned" inner life (OBS-064-001) implies motivational impairment — the retained grievance occupies and distorts the inner motivational field. The unforgiving servant's behaviour (seizing the fellow servant immediately after receiving enormous forgiveness) suggests a motivational failure: the received forgiveness did not generate the expected motivational transformation.

**Does not bypass motivation:** Forgiveness does not operate by overriding or suppressing motivation — it works through it. The commands to forgive (Luk 17:3-4; Mat 18:35; Mar 11:25) address motivation by providing the ground for it (received forgiveness as the reason to extend it).

findings.session_b_note:
**Compassion enables bold and boundary-crossing agency:** As established at T3.6, compassion enables volitional acts that self-protective inner states would not produce. Mark 1:41 — physical touch of a leper; Luke 10:33-35 — the Samaritan's investment of time, money, and care in a stranger from the opposing cultural group; Matt 18:27 — the king releasing an enormous debt. In each case, the compassion-movement enables an act of agency that crosses a social, ritual, financial, or cultural boundary. Compassion expands the scope of what the person's agency will reach.

**Compassion produces urgent and uninhibited agency:** Luke 15:20 — the father runs. The compassion-generated agency is characterised by urgency and the absence of hesitation. The normal social constraints on a father's dignity (running in public, embracing before the son had spoken) are suspended by the compassion-movement. The inner event bypasses social restraints on agency.

**Compassion does not impair agency:** There is no evidence in the data that compassion impairs the agency faculty. The one limiting case — metriopatheō (Heb 5:2), dealing gently rather than acting unchecked — is not impairment of agency but its calibration. The high priest's gentleness is itself an act of agency, shaped by understanding.

findings.session_b_note:
Contrition **transforms the mode of agency** rather than simply impairing it. The person in a contrite condition cannot act from self-sufficiency (that capacity has been broken); but they can act from disclosed need — bringing themselves before God, appealing, offering their broken state. This is a different form of agency: the agency of dependence rather than the agency of power.

The contrast with the hardened posture (Jer 44:10) is instructive: the people who refuse contrition continue in self-directed action (continuing to act in Egypt against God's direction, as the broader context shows) — their assertive agency is intact but directed away from God. The contrite person's assertive agency is broken but a different agency emerges: the agency of appeal, petition, and self-offering before God.

*New finding: contrition does not destroy agency but transforms it from self-powered assertion to God-directed appeal. This is a mode of agency proper to the creaturely-dependent condition — acting from need rather than from strength.*

findings.session_b_note:
**Enabling agency:** Fellowship with the living grounds hope (Ecc 9:4) and enables the mutual-support act of lifting up the fallen (Ecc 4:10). Being in fellowship produces the relational context in which agency is possible that would not be possible in isolation.

**Imparing agency:** Idolatrous joining (Hos 4:17 — *Ephraim is joined to idols; leave him alone*) produces divine abandonment — a condition in which the person's agency is operating in a spiritually abandoned context. The joining to wrong objects ultimately limits the person's effective agency by removing divine engagement and support.

**Bypassing agency:** The constitutional formation mode (Jer 13:23) — indelible character — represents a condition in which prior fellowship has produced character so fixed that the person's effective agency toward change is severely diminished. Wrong fellowship can produce a state in which the person cannot act their way out of what they have become.

findings.session_b_note: Goodness enables and deepens agency. The reconstitution pattern (Q&A-082): Spirit-produced goodness produces a genuine resolve that the human agent executes, with God's power completing it (2Th 1:11). This is not a reduction of agency but an amplification of it — the Spirit-enabled person has a deeper capacity for agentive goodness than the unregenerate person (whose agency is misdirected toward self-direction, Isa 65:2). Col 3:12's "put on" is an agency act — the Spirit's prior transformation is the enabling ground, and the human agentive choice is the expression. Goodness also provides the criterion for agency's proper exercise (Mic 6:8 — doing justice and loving kindness require active choosing and doing). (OBS-067-OBS-039, OBS-067-OBS-040, OBS-067-OBS-027)

findings.session_b_note: Love **enables and extends** agency beyond its natural range. The key evidence: enemy-love (Mat 5:44) produces agency toward those the person would naturally avoid — love extends the agentive reach to include hostile others. Joh 15:13 (OBS-103-125): love produces the maximum agentive act (laying down the soul) that no other motivation could reliably sustain. Ruth's chesed-love (Rut 3:10, OBS-103-089) produces the agentive choice against self-interest — love expands agency by overriding the self-protective constraints that would otherwise limit it. Disordered love produces distorted agency: love-of-money produces the agency of departure from faith (1Ti 6:10); love-of-primacy produces the agency of exclusion (3Jo 9, OBS-103-155). The direction of love determines the direction and quality of agency — love is the inner source from which the person acts outward.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-003: T3 reveals two structurally distinctive findings about compassion's faculty engagement. First, creativity is entirely silent (three S ratings) — the most informative absence in the tier: compassion re…
findings.finding_value: T3 reveals two structurally distinctive findings about compassion's faculty engagement. First, creativity is entirely silent (three S ratings) — the most informative absence in the tier: compassion responds, it does not originate or create. It is the most responsive of the faculties-engaging characteristics. Second, affect and moral action are structurally unified in compassion — not sequentially related but simultaneous. Affect is the mechanism of movement (splanchnizō is both the felt inner event and the cause of the action), not a precursor or accompaniment. This is unique among the characteristics reviewed: in most other registries, affect and volition are distinguishable stages; in compassion, the felt movement is already the morally motivated action beginning. A third distinctive finding: compassion converts moral knowledge into motivated action — it is the motivational ground of conscientiousness, not a product of it. The conscience faculty engagement reveals compassion as conscience-healing: it addresses the pitiable condition that conscience perceives as a moral claim, resolving the tension between moral knowledge and moral incapacity. The three relational modes (building/sustaining — chesed; restoring/repairing — splanchnizō; extending across difference — Good Samaritan) are a new finding not in the instruction typology.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-003: T3 produces four structurally significant findings about grace's faculty engagement. First, grace is agency-constituting rather than agency-replacing: 1Cor 15:10 holds in explicit paradox — "I worked …
findings.finding_value: T3 produces four structurally significant findings about grace's faculty engagement. First, grace is agency-constituting rather than agency-replacing: 1Cor 15:10 holds in explicit paradox — "I worked harder than any of them, though it was not I but the grace of God that is with me." Agency is not displaced but constituted by grace. This relationship holds in paradox that the T3.6 prompt options (enable/deepen/bypass/impair) cannot accommodate — a prompt design limitation noted for catalogue revision. Second, grace produces moral clarity (T3.8 — sharpens moral evaluation rather than bypassing it): the person who recognises grace has made a precise moral evaluation (they know they received what they did not deserve). Third, grace and conscience are mutually necessary: grace is the condition within which conscience can operate fully without destroying the person; conscience without grace produces condemnation; grace without conscience produces presumption (T3.9). Fourth, grace is the primary relational faculty developer in the registry's evidence — it reaches every relational register (vertical access, horizontal forgiving, speech-grace) and enables each one. Creativity (T3.5) is the one genuinely silent faculty — not an impairment but a non-engagement: grace receives and constitutes, it does not create.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-019: T3's agency-constituting finding (grace constitutes rather than replaces agency — 1Cor 15:10) and T4's human-to-God direction (supplication as the human posture of appeal — requiring genuine human age…
findings.finding_value: T3's agency-constituting finding (grace constitutes rather than replaces agency — 1Cor 15:10) and T4's human-to-God direction (supplication as the human posture of appeal — requiring genuine human agency in the act of plea) are structurally aligned. The constituted agency (T3.7) is precisely the agency that supplication requires: the creature must genuinely appeal, not merely receive passively. T3's finding that grace and conscience are mutually necessary (T3.9) corresponds to T4's relational-access finding: grace transforms the threshold of human-to-God approach (prosagōgē — SD035) from impassable to open, which is the relational expression of T3.9's constitutional finding that grace creates the condition within which conscience can operate fully without destruction. T3 names the inner-being event; T4 names the relational consequence of the same event.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-021: T3's faculty findings explain several patterns in T6's co-occurrence landscape. The seeking co-occurrence dominance (R140 — 40 verses) is partly explained by T3.6's agency-constituting finding: seekin…
findings.finding_value: T3's faculty findings explain several patterns in T6's co-occurrence landscape. The seeking co-occurrence dominance (R140 — 40 verses) is partly explained by T3.6's agency-constituting finding: seeking requires the constituted agency that grace provides for its own reception (SD026 — grace giving the capacity for supplication). The power cluster co-occurrences (strength R187 — 15 verses, might R198 — 10 verses) confirm T3.7's agency-constituting finding at the cross-registry level: grace producing agency is registered as co-occurring with power/strength across the corpus. T3.8's moral clarity finding explains the guilt co-occurrence (R073 — 10 verses): the moral clarity grace produces is most visible at the point of moral failure, and the co-occurrence reflects this — grace and guilt appear together because grace produces the moral clarity that accurately names the guilt it addresses.

findings.session_b_note: Covenant both enables and reorders agency. Enabling: covenant gives the person a covenantal framework within which to act with directed purpose — the covenant establishes what the person is called to do (the covenantal obligations) and empowers them to act within that structure. The new covenant specifically enables agency by liberating it from bondage: Gal 4:24-25 (OBS-034-071) — the new covenant produces free children rather than slaves; freed from the constraint of mere letter-keeping, the person exercises genuine moral agency under the Spirit. Reordering: the new covenant reorders the priority of agency — God's agency within (Spirit acting) comes first, enabling human agency as responsive rather than self-originating. This does not impair human agency but subordinates it to divine agency in a way that produces its fullest expression. It does not bypass agency but regrounds it.

findings.session_b_note: Peace enables agency — the peaceful person is constitutionally equipped to act in the world from a stable inner base rather than from reactive anxiety. Evidence: (1) Dan 10:19 — "peace be with you; be strong and of good courage" — the angelic peace-gift produces strength and courage for action; peace precedes and enables Daniel's capacity to act on the vision; (2) Isa 32:17 — "the effect of righteousness will be peace, and the result of righteousness, quietness and trust forever" — the peace condition produces trust, which is the basis for courageous action; (3) Deu 28:65 reverse — the absence of peace produces the "trembling heart" and "languishing soul" that impair agency; fearful and anxious people cannot act decisively. Conversely: complacent ease (H7600 group 413-001) impairs agency by producing false security and contempt for consequences — a corrupted form of "peace" that disengages agency.

findings.finding_value: The faculty engagement pattern (T3) and the formation arc (T5) are directly linked: the faculties engaged by the characteristic are precisely the faculties that are formed through it. Cognition is both constituted by endowing giving (T3.2 — wisdom deposited) and is the target of formation (T5.5 — Spirit given to instruct shapes over time). Memory is engaged by the covenantal mode (T3.3 — narrative-temporal dimension) and is the sustained environment of covenantal formation (T5.5 — the history of received giving shapes identity). Agency is both the bridge between disposition and act (T3.7) and is restored/enabled by eschatological giving (T3.7 Q&A-087 — depressed agency is renewed). Suffering reveals (T5.4 — tests the characteristic) and tests affect, volition, and conscientiousness (T3.4, T3.6, T3.10). What this pair reveals: the characteristic forms the person by engaging and developing the same faculties it requires for its own expression. Formation is circular in this characteristic: it needs faculties to be enacted, and its enactment develops those faculties further.

Agency is engaged across all seven sub-groups, making it co-equal with volition as the most universally engaged faculty in M05. The cluster's characteristics are not merely inner states but characteristically produce outward action. The pattern across all seven: the inner quality generates outward agency. Love generates acts of love; compassion generates the healing, feeding, protecting act; mercy generates the act of showing mercy; goodness generates the doing of good; gentleness defines the mode of all corrective and relational action; comfort generates the act of comforting; fellowship generates sharing, building, and reconciling. The cluster's characteristics are inherently agentic — they cannot remain merely inner without expressing outward.

**[CLUSTER]** E. Righteousness enables and directs agency toward its proper objects (justice, deliverance, truth-speaking). Justification (C) liberates agency from the paralysis of unresolved guilt. Wickedness distorts agency, directing it toward harmful ends (oppression, false condemnation, systemic corruption). The commissioned agent (D: Rom 13:4) shows agency bounded and directed by divine commission — the proper form of human retributive agency.
