**[CHAR-1]** E — Exultation deepens relational capacity: the person who exults in God is most fully alive to the relationship's reality. God's exulting over his people (Zep 3:17) deepens the relational bond — the image of God exulting over Zion with loud singing is a portrait of the fullest divine-human relational delight. The co-exultation of Isa 66:10 (all who love Jerusalem invited to exult with her) shows the characteristic generating relational solidarity.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Joy deepens relational capacity: M04-D (sunchairo) shows Joy as constitutively completing the relational bond — the co-rejoicing body is the rightly-ordered body; 1Jo 1:4 ("that our joy may be complete" through shared fellowship) and 2Jo 12 ("our joy may be complete" through face-to-face meeting) show Joy as the inner experience that reaches its fullness in genuine relational communion. The Pauline joy-in-communities shows that the relational bonds Paul has with specific people are the substance of his deepest Joy — persons are named as his joy (Phili 4:1; 1Th 2:20). Joy without genuine relational capacity (isolated, self-directed) is not fully evidenced as Joy in this corpus.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Suffering-Joy deepens relational capacity by creating a community formed around shared participation in Christ's suffering and anticipated glory (1Pe 4:13; Act 5:41). The communal experience of Suffering-Joy — rejoicing together despite or through shared adversity — creates bonds of peculiar depth and solidarity.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Gladness deepens relational capacity by enabling accurate relational evaluation: the person who can assess relational worth accurately (Rut 4:15; Pro 27:5) has the inner clarity to form and sustain genuine relationships. Gladness's wellbeing register (M04-O-VCG-03) is often relationally produced — good music, good testimony, good deeds — showing that gladness-as-wellbeing flows through relational channels.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Delight deepens genuine relational capacity: 1Sa 19:1 (Jonathan's Delight in David enabling him to protect David against his father's command); Jer 31:20 (God's Delight in Ephraim sustaining the relationship through rebuke — Delight as the relational bond that persists through discipline); 1Th 2:8 (Paul's affectionate desire for the Thessalonians producing self-sharing — Delight as the relational motor for self-giving). Corrupt Delight (M04-P; M04-N-VCG-02) distorts relational capacity into captivation, lust, or predation (Eze 23:12; Rev 13:3) — the relational faculty seized by the wrong object.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Genuine Pleasure deepens relational capacity: 2Sa 1:26's Jonathan-David pleasantness is the relational depth evidenced by David's grief at the loss; the pleasantness of the relationship was constitutive of its depth. Pro 16:24's gracious-word Pleasure actively sustains relationships through speech. Distorted Pleasure impairs relational capacity: Pro 9:17's stolen-bread Pleasure exploits and degrades relationships; Jer 51:34's Nebuchadnezzar consuming Jerusalem's delicacies is destructive of the relational context.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Wonder deepens relational capacity in two registers: (1) **Community-formation** — shared Wonder creates community; the people who together remember and proclaim God's marvellous works are bound by that shared wonder-memory (Psa 78:4); (2) **Depth of relational experience** — 2Sa 1:26's use of pa.la for Jonathan's extraordinary love shows Wonder as the capacity to recognise and be astonished by genuine extraordinary depth in human relationships.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All seven deepen relational capacity in their rightly-directed forms: Joy's sunchairo builds communal solidarity; Delight's relational face enables protective self-giving (1Sa 19:1 — Jonathan's delight in David enabling him to protect David at cost to himself); Wonder's communal proclamation binds the community to shared memory; Gladness enables the generous relational orientation (Psa 112:5 — "it is well with the man who deals generously"); Suffering-Joy produces communal identity under adversity (Act 16:34's whole household). Misdirected forms distort relational capacity: corrupt Delight (M04-P — Eze 23:12's che.med) twists relational capacity into captivation and exploitation; inverted Joy (Eze 25:6 — malice toward those who suffer) corrupts the relational dimension.

**[CHAR-1]** E — In its ordinary wounded form, shame **impairs** relational capacity — withdrawal, face-covering, inability to speak at the gate. In its corrective form, shame is a *relational tool* — it is extended by one person toward another to restore right relationship (2Th 3:14; 1Pe 3:16). In the M07-C mode, shame before God is the precondition for restored relationship: Eze 43:10-11 — only when Israel is ashamed can the temple design (the design of right relationship with God) be disclosed. Shame before God, in the M07-C mode, is not the end of the relational capacity but the gateway to its restoration.

**[CHAR-2]** E — CHAR-2 severely impairs relational capacity. The shaved envoys cannot return to public social life; the silenced man cannot engage in dialogue; the defeated nations cannot sustain former relationships with neighbours (derision replaces respect). 1Cor 15:43's mortal body "sown in dishonor" is in a condition of diminished relational capacity; resurrection glory restores it. CHAR-2's relational dimension is fundamental: it is enacted through the relational field and its primary effect is the disruption of the person's relational standing and capacity.

---

**[CHAR-3]** E — CHAR-3 is constitutively relational — it is the degradation of the relational-capacity in its worth-recognition mode. The judge who "neither fears God nor respects man" (Luk 18:2) has lost the relational-capacity component of appropriate regard for the worth of others. This is CHAR-3's most direct faculty engagement: it is the failure of the relational faculty's worth-recognition mode.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — CHAR-4's evaluative operation in VCG-01 engages the relational capacity through community norms (the social-moral judgments about hair, speech in assembly, financial conduct). The idolatrous-shameful-objects register (VCG-01 — Jer 3:24; 11:13; Hos 9:10) shows CHAR-4 operating in the person's relational capacity with God — the shameful object is what has replaced God in the person's devotional relation.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — CHAR-5 is constitutively relational — it is the contempt-relation between persons, and its damage is in the relational field. The commands against despising (Rom 14:3; 14:10) are specifically about protecting relational capacity within the community: do not despise your brother is a relational-capacity protection instruction. CHAR-5 impairs the relational capacity of the recipient by reducing their standing to zero in the contempt-er's relational field — and by extension, in the community's.

---

**[CHAR-6]** E — CHAR-6 is specifically relational in its function: it is the inner moral condition that enables the relational approach to God (Psa 26:6 — "I wash my hands in innocence and go around your altar"). The relational capacity that CHAR-6 enables is specifically the person-to-God relational approach — worship, petition, covenant engagement. Its absence (Hos 8:5) blocks this relational capacity: the incapacity for innocence bars the approach to God that the covenant relationship requires.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — The relational dimension is the cluster's most consistent primary dimension (evidenced as primary in Chars 2, 3, 5 and as significant in all six). Every M07 characteristic affects the person's relational capacity: shame withdraws relational presence (Chars 1, 2), worth-denial violates the relational field (Char 3), shamefulness makes the person's conduct unacceptable in the relational community (Char 4), contempt-produced shame wounds relational standing (Char 5), and innocence enables the relational approach to God (Char 6). Cluster-level finding: shame is a fundamentally relational phenomenon — it always arises in a relational context and always has consequences for the person's relational capacity. The resolution of shame is also relational: it requires divine vindication (Chars 1, 5), divine abasement of the proud (Char 2), divine correct worth-assignment (Char 3), divine calibration of the conscience (Char 4), and divine confirmation of innocence (Char 6). M07's domain is irreducibly relational — it is constituted by relations and resolved through relations.

**[CHAR-1]** E — CHAR-1 severely impairs relational capacity in both directions. Vertically: the God-directed relational capacity is impaired through forgetfulness (Deu 8:14, vc=34223: heart lifted → God forgotten), perceptive closure (Psa 10:4, vc=34074: "does not seek him"), and the consequent divine relational distance (Psa 138:6, vc=12086: "the haughty he knows from afar"). Horizontally: CHAR-1 substitutes hierarchy and contempt for genuine connection. Genuine horizontal relationship requires acknowledgment of the other's worth and standing — CHAR-1 denies this by elevating the self above all others (Deu 17:20, vc=34231). The result is that CHAR-1 generates predatory interaction (Psa 10:2, vc=33963: "hotly pursues the poor"), contemptuous interaction (Psa 123:4, vc=33953), and violent interaction (Psa 73:6, vc=33959: "pride is their necklace; violence covers them as a garment") rather than genuine relational connection.

**[CHAR-2]** E — CHAR-2 severely impairs relational capacity. It substitutes domination and predation for genuine connection in the horizontal direction: Psa 119:85 (vc=34102) — pitfalls dug for the godly; Psa 119:69 (vc=34100) — lies smearing the psalmist. In the vertical direction, it breaks the human-to-God relational connection by treating God's authority as a constraint to overcome rather than a relationship to honour. Pro 13:10 (vc=34113, M08-B-VCG-02): "by insolence comes nothing but strife" — CHAR-2's relational consequence is universal: it produces conflict in every relational direction.

**[CHAR-3]** E — VCG-01 impairs relational capacity through empty social claims (Pro 25:14 — promising what one cannot deliver) and community corruption (1Cor 5:6). VCG-03 deepens relational capacity: mutual boasting between Paul and his communities (2Cor 7:4; 1Th 2:19; 2Th 1:4) is a relational practice of genuine commendation and joy in the other. CHAR-3 is the most relationally complex of the M08 characteristics: its condemned form (VCG-01) corrupts relational capacity, its examined form (VCG-02) manages it conscientiously, and its God-directed form (VCG-03) deepens it through mutual affirmation.

**[CHAR-4]** E — CHAR-4 severely impairs relational capacity. 1Cor 8:1 (vc=33935): knowledge (without love) inflates — the inflated self-picture prevents the other-directed attention that genuine relationship requires. 1Cor 13:4 (vc=33936): love is not fusioō — the inflation is the direct antithesis of love's self-giving orientation. The conceited mind is too preoccupied with its own inflated self-picture to genuinely perceive, value, and respond to the other.

**[CHAR-5]** E — CHAR-5 severely impairs relational capacity by generating the self-sufficiency conviction that removes the person from the shared community of need. Isa 47:8 (vc=9563): "I am, and there is no one besides me" — the relational isolation of the self-sufficient declaration; the person who believes they need no one cannot genuinely connect with others. Eze 16:49 (vc=33979, M08-E-VCG-01): the proud, ease-dwelling community does not see the neighbour in need — CHAR-5's structural self-sufficiency renders the other invisible as a subject of genuine relational concern.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster comparison reveals that only CHAR-3's VCG-03 form evidences relational capacity being deepened by a form of the boasting-impulse: mutual community boasting (2Cor 7:4, M08-C-VCG-03) deepens the relational bond. All other forms across all five characteristics impair relational capacity. CHAR-4's structural opposition to love (1Cor 8:1; 13:4, M08-D-VCG-01) is the most analytically explicit relational impairment evidence in the cluster.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Submission *enables and forms* genuine relational capacity in the authority-relationship register. 2Cor9:13 — submission to the gospel expressing itself in generous giving and community approval — the genuine submission enables the relational flourishing of the community. 2Cor7:15 — the Corinthians' obedient reception of Titus deepening his affection for them — genuine submission produces deepened relational bond (Titus's deepened affection is the relational fruit of their obedience). Pro30:17 — the absence of filial obedience named as fatal moral failure — the relational capacity for genuine authority-relationship is impaired without the characteristic.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Contrition *enables and opens* the relational capacity for genuine divine encounter. The crushed spirit is one that no longer interposes proud self-assertion between itself and God — it is genuinely open to God's nearness (Psa34:18) and dwelling (Isa57:15). The characteristic removes the relational barrier of self-sufficiency and enables the most intimate divine-human relational encounter in the corpus: God dwelling with the contrite spirit.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Meekness/gentleness *enables and deepens* genuine relational capacity in the contexts of pastoral care and responsive service. Metriopatheō (Heb5:2) enables the high priest to genuinely relate to the erring — without it, the relational encounter degenerates into judgment without compassion. Okneō (Act9:38) enables genuine responsiveness to others' needs without self-protective delay — the relational capacity for genuine availability. Both aspects of the characteristic deepen the person's capacity for genuine other-directed relation.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Semnotēs *enables genuine relational ordering*. 1Ti3:4 — the dignity producing orderly compliance without coercion enables the parent-child relationship to function in appropriate ordered-respect. Tit2:7 — dignity authenticating teaching enables the teacher-learner relationship to function with genuine cognitive reception. 1Ti2:2 — dignified peaceful public life enables civil relationships to function without anxious self-assertion. The characteristic enables each relational context to function according to its appropriate ordering.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Willing-heartedness *enables and deepens* the relational capacity toward God. The freely-moved heart (Exo35:5/22) is one that is genuinely oriented toward God in relation — not transactionally giving under compulsion but freely offering in genuine relational generosity. Psa51:12's willing spirit enables "freely-offered devotion" — the relational quality of the person's engagement with God is enhanced by the willing disposition. Without it (the burdened post-failure state), the relational capacity toward God is impaired in its free-offering dimension.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Humility *enables and is foundational to* relational capacity. The evidence is consistent: the humble person genuinely receives God's mercy (1Ki21:29; 2Ch12:7; Luk18:14), genuinely regards others' worth (Phili2:3), and enables corporate harmony (Eph4:2). Conversely, the proud person is opposed by God (Jam4:6; 1Pe5:5) — the relational capacity toward God is directly impaired by the absence of humility. The self-enclosed state of pride (structural opposite of humility — Pro11:2) is a state of relational closure: the person cannot genuinely connect to God or others because the self-protective screen of self-assertion intervenes. Humility is the structural prerequisite for genuine relation in both directions (divine and human).

**[CLUSTER]** E — All six enable and deepen genuine relational capacity; none impair it. Humility (CHAR-1) is structurally prerequisite for genuine relation — the humble person genuinely receives God's mercy (1Ki21:29; 2Ch12:7; Luk18:14), genuinely regards others' worth (Phili2:3), and enables corporate harmony (Eph4:2); the proud person is constitutionally closed to God (Jam4:6 — God opposes the proud). Submission (CHAR-2) enables genuine relational capacity in the authority-relationship register — 2Cor7:15 (Titus's deepened affection for the Corinthians produced by their obedient reception) confirms that genuine submission produces deepened relational bond rather than diminished relation. Contrition (CHAR-3) enables and opens the relational capacity for genuine divine encounter — the crushed spirit is one that no longer interposes proud self-assertion between itself and God, enabling the most intimate form of divine-human relation (God dwelling with the contrite — Isa57:15). Meekness and Gentleness (CHAR-4) enables genuine relational capacity in pastoral engagement — metriopatheō (Heb5:2) creates the space in which the erring can be genuinely addressed rather than condemned or abandoned. Dignity (CHAR-5) enables genuine relational ordering without coercive force (1Ti3:4 — producing orderly compliance through character gravity). Willing-heartedness (CHAR-6) enables and deepens relational capacity toward God — the freely-moved heart gives in genuine relational generosity (Exo35; 2Ch29:31) rather than transactional compliance.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — Wilful sinning *impairs* relational capacity specifically in the direction of the sin. Sin against God creates estrangement from God (Isa 1:4; 1Ki 8:33/35 — national defeat and drought as relational rupture). Sin against the neighbour creates relational debt requiring forgiveness (Mat 18:15; Luk 17:3). Sin against the self (1Cor 6:18) damages the body through which relational life is lived. The impairment is directional: the relationship sinned against is damaged; other relationships may remain intact. The characteristic does not universally impair relational capacity but specifically ruptures the relation that is sinned against.

**[CHAR-10]** E — (1) *Enticement exploits relational trust*: 2Pe 2:14/18 — the enticers use a relational-authority medium (teaching with "loud boasts") to deliver the enticement to their relational targets; the relational capacity is exploited as the delivery mechanism. (2) *Hypocrisy corrupts relational authenticity*: Gal 2:13 — the collective hypocrisy corrupts the community's relational authenticity; Paul confronts this (implied by the Gal 2:11 context) precisely because the relational fabric of the community has been distorted. (3) *Apostasy severs relational-covenantal bonds*: Act 21:21 — "forsake Moses" — the covenantal community is the relational framework being abandoned.

**[CHAR-11]** E — The condition *severs and blocks* the relational capacity toward God while leaving horizontal relational capacity intact (persons continue to relate to each other under the condition). Joh 8:21 — "you will die in your sin... where I am going, you cannot come" — the condition creates an absolute relational barrier that prevents access to where Jesus goes. Rom 11:27 — "when I take away their sins" — the removal of the condition is constituted as the restoration of covenantal relationship: sin is the barrier; its removal is relational restoration. Heb 1:3 — "after making purification for sins, he sat down at the right hand" — the purification is the prerequisite for the highest relational nearness (right hand of the Majesty) — sin is what prevents that nearness.

**[CHAR-12]** E — Sin's enslaving power *misdirects* the relational capacity: the relational belonging and allegiance capacity that was designed for God-relationship is captured and redirected toward the devil's domain (1Jo 3:8 — "of the devil"). The relational capacity itself remains operative (the person is in relationship — master-slave with sin; belonging to the devil) but the direction of the relational allegiance has been inverted from God-toward to devil-toward.

**[CHAR-13]** E — The record *severs and blocks* relational capacity toward God. Isa 59:2 — separation between person and God; God's face hidden; prayer not heard — the record progressively closes off the relational channels. Jer 5:25 — "your sins have kept good from you" — the record blocks the positive relational provision God would otherwise give. The record's erasure restores relational capacity: Jer 31:34 — when God remembers sins no more, the relational channel is fully restored; 2Ch 6:25/26/27 — forgiveness of the sin enables return to the land and restoration of divine hearing.

**[CHAR-14]** E — Forgiveness received *restores and deepens* relational capacity. 2Cor 5:19 — "not counting their trespasses against them" — the removal of the sin-ledger from the relational account restores the God-relationship's full potential. Act 2:38 — Spirit received — the Spirit's indwelling is the deepest relational-capacity enhancement: the person is now indwelt by God himself, the deepest possible relational proximity. Luk 7:47 — the woman's love for Jesus is the evidence of restored relational capacity: the forgiven person's God-relationship capacity is deepened by the forgiveness received.

**[CHAR-15]** E — The generational pattern *damages and progressively severs* the relational capacity toward God. Jer 8:14's "doomed us to perish" — the God-relationship has deteriorated to a state of divine doom rather than divine provision. Isa 64:5 — "you were angry, and we sinned" — the divine anger and the human sinning form a deteriorating relational cycle. The relational capacity is not eliminated (the community can still address God — 1Ki 8:47 — plead with God) but its normal functioning (blessed God-people relationship) has been severely impaired by the accumulated sinning.

**[CHAR-16]** E — The sinner-identity *restricts* relational capacity. Luk 6:32/33/34 — sinners relate only within reciprocal circles; their relational capacity is real but bounded by self-interest; they cannot extend grace to those outside the reciprocal relationship. Joh 9:31 — "God does not listen to sinners" — the God-relationship channel is impaired. Heb 7:26 — "separated from sinners" — the separation from Christ's holiness names the relational incompatibility. The sinner's relational capacity is genuine within the self-interest radius (Luk 6:32/33/34) but structurally blocked in the God-direction (Joh 9:31) and constrained in the human-beyond-reciprocity direction (Luk 6:32).

**[CHAR-17]** E — Unaddressed guilt *severs* relational capacity; acknowledged guilt *opens* relational restoration. Ezr 9:15 — "none can stand before you because of this" — the guilt-state severs the standing-before-God; Hos 5:15 — God withdraws "until they acknowledge their guilt" — guilt-state severs the God-relationship; only acknowledgment reopens it. Conversely: Num 5:7 — "giving it to him to whom he did the wrong" — guilt acknowledged and restituted restores the damaged human relationship; the guilt-state that drove the restitution enables relational repair.

**[CHAR-18]** E — Accumulated iniquity *progressively severs* relational capacity. Isa 59:2 — "your iniquities have made a separation between you and your God" — the primary relational damage is God-separation; the iniquity acts as a structural barrier. Amo 3:2 — "therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities" — the covenant relationship that uniquely placed Israel before God is the context in which the iniquity is most damaging; intimate relational proximity intensifies rather than excuses accountability. The relational severing is the iniquity's most consequential effect.

**[CHAR-19]** E — Transgression *severs* relational capacity in proportion to its object. Against God: Isa 59:2 (CHAR-18 adjacent) — "iniquities have made a separation between you and your God"; 2Jo 9 — going beyond Christ's teaching means "does not have God" — the God-relationship is severed; Eze 20:38 — "those who transgress against me... shall not enter the land of Israel" — excluded from covenant community. Against persons: Pro 18:19 — "a brother offended is more unyielding than a strong city" — the interpersonal transgression creates the hardest relational barrier.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Unintentional sinning *impairs* the relational bond without impairing the relational capacity of the person. The bond is damaged (the violation occurred); the person's ability to relate is intact (they can confess, bring an offering, seek remedy). The impairment is to the *standing* within the relationship rather than to the *capacity* for relationship. The remedy (atonement, forgiveness — Num 15:28; Lev 19:22) restores the standing, showing that the relational capacity was not damaged — only the relational record.

**[CHAR-20]** E — Faithlessness *severs* relational capacity in proportion to the depth of the prior bond. Eze 39:23 — God hiding his face — the deepest relational severance; Pro 18:19 (CHAR-19 adjacent) — "a brother offended is more unyielding than a strong city" — betrayal of the closest bond creates the hardest barrier. Lam 1:2 — friends becoming enemies — the relational conversion from intimacy to enmity. The relational damage is precisely calibrated to the prior covenant: the deeper the covenant, the more devastating the faithlessness.

**[CHAR-21]** E — Perversion *fractures* relational capacity at every level. Pro 16:28 — "separates close friends" — the perverse person's relational capacity produces the opposite of what relationship requires (trust, honesty); Isa 29:16 — the creator-creature relationship inverted; 1Cor 3:17 — "if anyone destroys God's temple, God will destroy him" — the corruption of the sacred relationship produces divine destruction. Perversion does not merely damage but inverts relational capacity: what should build bonds (wisdom, honesty) is replaced by what destroys them (strife, deceit).

**[CHAR-22]** E — Injustice *destroys* relational capacity from the side of the victim and *corrupts* it from the side of the agent. Lam 1:2 (CHAR-20 adjacent) — those who deal treacherously become enemies; the unjust agent's relational capacity is perverted into harm-relationship. The victim's relational experience is violated — Psa 43:1 — "deliver me from the deceitful and unjust man." The righteous avoid the unjust as an unsuitable relational partner (1Cor 6:1 — don't take grievances before the unrighteous) and find them abominable (Pro 29:27).

**[CHAR-3]** E — Genuine confession *enables and partially restores* relational capacity: by naming the sin that ruptured the relationship, it opens the pathway toward relational repair. Luk 15:21 — the son's confession initiates the restoration of the father-son relationship; 1Sa 7:6 — corporate confession at Mizpah is the beginning of the renewal of the Israel-God relationship under Samuel. Hollow confession (Deu 1:41) does not enable relational restoration — the words are spoken but the will moves independently, leaving the relational rupture unaddressed.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Conscience suppression *impairs* the relational capacity specifically in the *self-knowledge dimension* of relationship: the person cannot accurately assess their own standing in the relationship. Jer 2:35 — "surely his anger has turned from me" — a false assessment of the current relational state with God. Tit 3:11 — the divisive person whose conscience suppression produces relational damage through division while he remains unaware of his own role (he does not recognise himself as "sinful" in this context). The impaired relational self-knowledge prevents the person from taking the steps (confession, repentance) that would actually address the relational problem.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Refusal to repent *impairs* the relational capacity specifically in the *restoration dimension*: the capacity to move toward restored relationship with God is persistently withheld. The person remains capable of relationship (they are not completely cut off — God continues to warn, Neh 9:29) but declines to move toward restoration. Heb 10:26's foreclosure of sacrifice is the most severe relational impairment: the mechanism for relational address is closed, suggesting that sustained refusal eventually impairs the relational capacity at a structural level, not merely in the person's disposition.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Habitual defection *misdirects and impairs* the relational capacity simultaneously: it misdirects the relational allegiance toward wrong objects (2Ki 17:7 — other gods), and it impairs the capacity for the foundational relationship with God (1Jo 3:6 — never seen or known Christ). The misdirection and impairment are related: the more fully the relational capacity is invested in wrong objects, the less capacity remains for the relationship with God that would correct the sinning pattern.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Contagious sin *corrupts* the relational capacity by redirecting the relational bond between leader and community from its designed purpose (forming the community toward God) to its corrupted purpose (forming the community toward sin). The relational bond itself remains operative — the community continues in relationship with the leader — but the moral content transmitted through the bond is the sinning direction. 1Ki 14:22 — Judah provoking God to jealousy — shows that the leader-community relationship has been redirected: instead of the relationship forming the community toward the covenant Lord, it has formed them toward the provocative stance against him.

**[CHAR-8]** E — Political revolt *severs* the governing relational bond: "revolted from the rule of" (2Ki 8:20/22) — the preposition "from" names the directional severance. The relational capacity is deployed in the act of breaking: the bond is not abandoned passively but actively severed through the revolt. The "to this day" permanence markers show the relational bond does not restore; the severance is effective and lasting.

**[CHAR-9]** E — Sinful speech *damages and severs* the relational capacity: slander directed at persons (VCG-01) damages the speaker's relational bond with those slandered. Eph 4:31 — the command to put away slander alongside bitterness and anger is a command to restore the relational environment that these dispositions damage. Blasphemy directed at God (VCG-02/03) damages the relational bond between creature and Creator — the beast's constitutive blasphemy (VCG-03) represents the total severing of the creature-God relational bond through the orientation of defiant speech.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The characteristic impairs and weaponises relational capacity simultaneously. Genuine relational connection requires transparency and goodwill; the characteristic corrupts both. The wicked person speaks peace while harbouring evil (Psa 28:3 — relational transparency impaired), uses words as weapons (Pro 12:6 — relational capacity weaponised), and is structurally unable to approach God in genuine worship (Pro 15:8; Pro 15:29 — vertical relational capacity foreclosed). The social-relational harm documented throughout VCGs 03, 08, and 09 shows the characteristic's comprehensive relational destructiveness.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The characteristic impairs genuine relational capacity while enabling relational harm. The constitutionally evil person can form relationships (2Jo 11 — association; 3Jo 10 — community involvement), but the constitutional condition ensures those relationships are vehicles for harm rather than genuine connection. Luk 11:39 (vc=14407 — VCG-05) shows the Pharisees engaged in social-religious community while "full of greed and wickedness within" — relational participation without relational integrity. The characteristic hollows out relational capacity at the constitutional level: the form of relationship is maintained while its interior quality is corrupted.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The characteristic impairs relational capacity at both the vertical (God-human) and horizontal (human-human) levels. Vertically: Pro 3:32 (vc=1686 — VCG-02) — exclusion from divine confidence; Eze 44:13 (vc=66003 — VCG-04) — barred from sacred service; Pro 15:8 (vc=1678 — VCG-03) — sacrifice rendered unacceptable. Horizontally: Pro 29:27 (vc=65959 — VCG-01) — mutual abomination between unjust and righteous creates relational incompatibility. The characteristic does not impair instrumental relational capacity (the abominable person can still relate socially — Pro 26:25 shows gracious speech) but impairs the genuine relational capacity for authentic covenant connection — with God and with the morally upright.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The characteristic impairs the covenant-relational capacity with God while enabling a false relational attachment to idol-objects. Eze 5:11 (vc=65969 — VCG-05): divine withdrawal — the relational access to God is foreclosed. Eze 6:9 (vc=1697 — VCG-05): the whoring heart has departed from God — the relational departure is the characteristic's defining relational event. Simultaneously, the characteristic enables attachment to idol-objects as pseudo-relational objects (the heart going after them — Eze 11:21 — VCG-05), filling the relational vacuum left by departure from God with idolatrous attachment.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The characteristic impairs the relational capacity for authentic connection while enabling a false relational performance (Psa 28:3 — VCG-03: speech of peace covering inner evil). Genuine relational capacity requires consistency between inner and outer — the characteristic produces a radical inner-outer split that makes authentic relating impossible. The predatory relational mode (Psa 14:4 — VCG-03: eating up the people; Psa 141:9 — VCG-03: laying traps and snares) inverts the relational capacity into a harm-delivery system. The characteristic does not eliminate relational engagement but corrupts it into instrumentalised deception and predation.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The characteristic impairs genuine relational capacity while weaponising the relational-communicative capacity for harmful purposes. The divine-human relational capacity is specifically and comprehensively severed by the characteristic (VCG-01): Rev 16:9 (VCG-01) — people perceive God's power but curse rather than draw near; the blasphemy creates relational hostility where approach should occur. The human-human relational capacity (VCG-02/03) is weaponised: the communicative ability that enables genuine relational connection (speech) is deployed for defamation (1Cor 4:13 — VCG-02) and false accusation (1Pe 2:12 — VCG-03). The relational capacity is impaired for genuine connection and redirected toward hostile relational aggression.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster consistently impairs genuine relational capacity while weaponising the relational-communicative capacity for harmful purposes. All six characteristics impair the vertical divine-human relational capacity (see T3.11.1). The horizontal human-human relational damage takes two forms: (a) predatory relational exploitation (Char 5 — Psa 14:4: eating up the people; Char 6 — false accusation as relational weapon), and (b) deceptive relational performance (Char 5 — Psa 28:3: speaking peace while evil is in the heart; Char 3 — Pro 26:25: gracious speech masking seven inner abominations). The cluster reveals M10b evil as inherently parasitic on relational capacity — using the relational faculties as instruments of harm rather than connection.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The characteristic primarily impairs relational access (exclusion from community and worship) while simultaneously structuring relational responsibility (the duty not to transmit, the public self-declaration). The impairment is temporary and remediable; the responsibility is ongoing. The impairment thus serves a protective relational function: the exclusion of the defiled person preserves the communal sacral integrity for others. This reveals the characteristic as managing individual-community relational boundaries rather than attacking relational capacity as such.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The characteristic impairs relational capacity toward God: Eph 5:5 (VCG-04) — no inheritance in the kingdom; 2Cor 6:17 (VCG-03) — conditional on separation from unclean things. It also bypasses honest horizontal relational capacity: Mat 23:27 (VCG-04) — the outward appearance of relational acceptability conceals the inner defilement, producing a relational persona that does not correspond to the inner condition. The characteristic thus impairs vertical relation (with God) and corrupts horizontal relation (with others) through self-concealment.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The characteristic severely impairs relational capacity at multiple levels: (1) the covenantal marital bond is broken by adultery (Num 5, VCG-01); (2) the corporate covenant with God is severed by idolatry (Eze 20:31 — "I will not be inquired of by you"; Eze 5:11 — divine withdrawal); (3) the community's relationship with its land is corrupted (Mic 2:10 — "no place to rest"); (4) the community's relationship with surrounding nations is reduced to being named "a filthy thing" (Lam 1:17) and expelled (Lam 4:15). The characteristic destroys relational bonds at every level — personal, communal, divine, and spatial.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The characteristic severely impairs relational capacity. The spirit substitutes its own relational agenda for the person's: the inhabited person's voice becomes the spirit's declaration (Mar 3:11; Mar 1:26), not the person's own relational speech. The person cannot give or receive the normal relational communications that constitute community. The restoration (Luk 6:18 — "cured"; Luk 9:42 — "gave him back to his father") restores the relational capacity as a primary feature of healing.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All four characteristics impair relational capacity, but the form and scope of impairment differ. Characteristic 1 temporarily impairs relational access (exclusion from worship and communal life during the defined period) while structuring relational responsibility (the duty not to transmit). The impairment is bounded and remediable. Characteristic 2 impairs vertical relation (with God — Eph 5:5) and corrupts horizontal relation through concealment (Mat 23:27). Characteristic 3 produces the most comprehensive relational impairment in the cluster: it damages every relational bond simultaneously (marital, divine-covenantal, community-land, community-sanctuary, community-nations). Characteristic 4 severs the most immediate relational bonds (family — Luk 9:42; community — Mar 5:2; worship community — Mar 1:23) while generating intense relational response in those who care for the possessed person (Mar 7:25, Act 5:16).

findings.session_b_note:
The relational capacity engagement pattern confirms the dimension classification and adds precision to it:

Forgiveness is not merely a relational characteristic in the sense of occurring within relationships — it is a **relational capacity restorer and enabler**. Its primary function in the inner being is to remove what blocks genuine relational connection (guilt, grievance, withheld claims) and to generate the inner states (love, trust, openness) that make genuine connection possible.

This distinguishes forgiveness from other relational characteristics: where love, compassion, and mercy primarily build and sustain relational connection, forgiveness specifically addresses the **ruptures and blockages** that prevent connection. Its relational function is curative and restorative before it is generative.

The pattern also reveals the **dual direction** of relational capacity in forgiveness: toward God (the primary movement in the OT corpus and in the NT access-postures) and toward other persons (the commanded horizontal movement). Forgiveness uniquely operates both relational directions simultaneously — the same characteristic that restores the human-divine bond calls for the restoration of the human-human bond.

findings.session_b_note:
The instruction note for T3.11 asks for a distinction between characteristics that build/sustain relational connection and those that restore/repair it. The compassion data reveals that compassion does both, but in distinct modes corresponding to the two vocabulary families:

**Building and sustaining:** The chesed vocabulary (steadfast love, covenantal loyalty) describes compassion as the quality that builds and sustains relational bonds across time, through violation, and in the face of unfaithfulness. Chesed builds and sustains relational connection — it is the loyal love that does not withdraw when the other fails.

**Restoring and repairing:** The splanchnizō and chus/eleēmosunē vocabulary describes compassion as a movement toward those who are broken, lost, or in need — it repairs relational rupture and restores those who have been excluded (the leper, the lost son, the wounded stranger). This is compassion as restoring agent rather than sustaining quality.

**Extending (new category):** The Good Samaritan pattern adds a third mode not captured by either building/sustaining or restoring/repairing: extending relational capacity to those with whom no prior relationship exists. This is compassion as relational pioneer — opening new relational territory where none previously existed. This is a *New finding* that may have implications for other registries in the programme.

findings.session_b_note:
The pattern reveals that contrition is **fundamentally relational in character** — but primarily relationally vertical. It is the inner-being condition that positions the person for genuine divine encounter. The relational capacity it engages is not the capacity for equality-based mutuality (as in friendship or love) but the capacity for genuine creature-Creator relationship: the creature disclosed, lowly, and open before the holy God. This relational structure is asymmetric by design — and contrition is the inner-being posture that honours rather than resists that asymmetry.

The gap in horizontal relational engagement is itself revealing: contrition is not primarily about repairing human-to-human relationships (that would be reconciliation, restitution, or forgiveness) but about re-establishing the person's right posture before God. Horizontal relational repair may follow, but it is not the primary constitutive feature of contrition.

*New finding: contrition is constitutively vertically relational — it is the inner-being condition proper to genuine creature-Creator relationship, characterised by asymmetry (creature before Creator) rather than mutuality. This is a clarifying assembly for Session D.*

findings.session_b_note: The relational engagement pattern reveals that goodness in its full expression is essentially outward-directed. The characteristic builds relational capacity in two directions simultaneously: toward God (vertical — walking with God, seeking God, receiving his goodness) and toward others (horizontal — justice, kindness, instruction, community). This dual-directional relational engagement is structurally coherent with the Mic 6:8 definition: the tri-fold good involves both the vertical (walking humbly with God) and the horizontal (doing justice, loving kindness). The relational pattern further reveals that goodness is a characteristic that naturally overflows from the inner being toward others — the person "full of goodness" (Rom 15:14) becomes a relational resource for the community. Goodness therefore builds rather than merely sustains relational connection — it generates new relational capacities in the one who possesses it. (OBS-067-OBS-017, OBS-067-OBS-025, OBS-067-OBS-027)

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-067-021: T3 confirmed that goodness is fundamentally integrating — it engages and aligns every faculty (Q&A-095). T6 confirmed that goodness is centrally connected across the programme's characteristic landsca…
findings.finding_value: T3 confirmed that goodness is fundamentally integrating — it engages and aligns every faculty (Q&A-095). T6 confirmed that goodness is centrally connected across the programme's characteristic landscape — broad co-occurrence, shared anchors at the highest-density synthesis nodes, root-vocabulary sharing across three families. These two findings are structurally related: a characteristic that is internally integrating (T3) is also externally connecting (T6). The Mic 6:8 anchor (T6.6 — shared with 6 registries) integrates justice, kindness, love, humility, compassion, and will in a single verse — this is the structural expression of goodness's integrating faculty-engagement. Gal 5:22 (shared with 5 registries) integrates Spirit-fruit characteristics in a cluster — the same integrating logic. The characteristic that most fully integrates the inner faculties (T3) is also the characteristic most structurally connected to adjacent characteristics (T6). Integration within produces connection without.

findings.session_b_note: The relational capacity pattern reveals love as the relational faculty's constitutive content — not merely an enabler of relationship but what genuine relationship consists of. Joh 15:13 (OBS-103-125): the relational capacity's maximum expression (laying down the soul for friends) is defined in terms of love. 1Th 2:8 (OBS-103-123): sharing the soul is what love produces — the relational capacity at its deepest is the capacity to give the self. This means relational capacity without love is possible but shallow: formal, transactional, or merely social. Love is what makes the relational capacity reach its genuine depth — the capacity becomes what it is constitutively designed to be only when love is operating through it. The programme's account of relational capacity therefore requires love as its primary activating content.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-003: T3 reveals two structurally distinctive findings about compassion's faculty engagement. First, creativity is entirely silent (three S ratings) — the most informative absence in the tier: compassion re…
findings.finding_value: T3 reveals two structurally distinctive findings about compassion's faculty engagement. First, creativity is entirely silent (three S ratings) — the most informative absence in the tier: compassion responds, it does not originate or create. It is the most responsive of the faculties-engaging characteristics. Second, affect and moral action are structurally unified in compassion — not sequentially related but simultaneous. Affect is the mechanism of movement (splanchnizō is both the felt inner event and the cause of the action), not a precursor or accompaniment. This is unique among the characteristics reviewed: in most other registries, affect and volition are distinguishable stages; in compassion, the felt movement is already the morally motivated action beginning. A third distinctive finding: compassion converts moral knowledge into motivated action — it is the motivational ground of conscientiousness, not a product of it. The conscience faculty engagement reveals compassion as conscience-healing: it addresses the pitiable condition that conscience perceives as a moral claim, resolving the tension between moral knowledge and moral incapacity. The three relational modes (building/sustaining — chesed; restoring/repairing — splanchnizō; extending across difference — Good Samaritan) are a new finding not in the instruction typology.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-019: T3's perceptive-trigger finding (compassion is activated by sight — splanchnizō is perceptively dependent) and T4's scope-by-need finding (scope is determined by perceived need, not covenantal standin…
findings.finding_value: T3's perceptive-trigger finding (compassion is activated by sight — splanchnizō is perceptively dependent) and T4's scope-by-need finding (scope is determined by perceived need, not covenantal standing) are the same finding from two analytical perspectives. T3 names the faculty (perception) and its function (triggering compassion by seeing the pitiable condition); T4 names the relational consequence (scope defined by what is seen). The cross-boundary extension in T4 (Nineveh, Samaritan/Jew) is the relational expression of T3's merit-independence: compassion is perceptively dependent (it must see the need) but merit-independent (it does not assess the moral standing of the one seen). The three relational modes in T3.11 (building/sustaining, restoring/repairing, extending across difference) correspond precisely to T4's chesed/splanchnizō/cross-boundary structure.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-003: T3 produces four structurally significant findings about grace's faculty engagement. First, grace is agency-constituting rather than agency-replacing: 1Cor 15:10 holds in explicit paradox — "I worked …
findings.finding_value: T3 produces four structurally significant findings about grace's faculty engagement. First, grace is agency-constituting rather than agency-replacing: 1Cor 15:10 holds in explicit paradox — "I worked harder than any of them, though it was not I but the grace of God that is with me." Agency is not displaced but constituted by grace. This relationship holds in paradox that the T3.6 prompt options (enable/deepen/bypass/impair) cannot accommodate — a prompt design limitation noted for catalogue revision. Second, grace produces moral clarity (T3.8 — sharpens moral evaluation rather than bypassing it): the person who recognises grace has made a precise moral evaluation (they know they received what they did not deserve). Third, grace and conscience are mutually necessary: grace is the condition within which conscience can operate fully without destroying the person; conscience without grace produces condemnation; grace without conscience produces presumption (T3.9). Fourth, grace is the primary relational faculty developer in the registry's evidence — it reaches every relational register (vertical access, horizontal forgiving, speech-grace) and enables each one. Creativity (T3.5) is the one genuinely silent faculty — not an impairment but a non-engagement: grace receives and constitutes, it does not create.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-019: T3's agency-constituting finding (grace constitutes rather than replaces agency — 1Cor 15:10) and T4's human-to-God direction (supplication as the human posture of appeal — requiring genuine human age…
findings.finding_value: T3's agency-constituting finding (grace constitutes rather than replaces agency — 1Cor 15:10) and T4's human-to-God direction (supplication as the human posture of appeal — requiring genuine human agency in the act of plea) are structurally aligned. The constituted agency (T3.7) is precisely the agency that supplication requires: the creature must genuinely appeal, not merely receive passively. T3's finding that grace and conscience are mutually necessary (T3.9) corresponds to T4's relational-access finding: grace transforms the threshold of human-to-God approach (prosagōgē — SD035) from impassable to open, which is the relational expression of T3.9's constitutional finding that grace creates the condition within which conscience can operate fully without destruction. T3 names the inner-being event; T4 names the relational consequence of the same event.

findings.session_b_note: The pattern reveals that covenant is not merely one engagement of relational capacity among others but the constitutional form through which relational capacity is organised and sustained across time. Relational capacity without covenant is vulnerable — episodic, potentially shallow, subject to dissolution. Covenant without relational capacity is empty — a legal form without the living connection it is meant to structure. The pattern shows that covenant is the form of which relational capacity is the content: covenant holds and sustains relational capacity, and relational capacity gives covenant its living inner reality. This reciprocity — covenant as form, relational capacity as content — is the core structural insight of T3.11. It also illuminates why covenant is the primary dimension category of this registry: the Relational Disposition (06) classification is appropriate because covenant's primary inner-being function is to enable, structure, and sustain the relational capacity of the person in their connection to God and others. The pattern of sustained engagement across all covenant traditions confirms that this is not a peripheral function but the constitutional purpose of the characteristic.

It also illuminates why covenant is the primary dimension category of this registry: the Relational Disposition (06) classification is appropriate because covenant's primary inner-being function is to enable, structure, and sustain the relational capacity of the person in their connection to God and others. The pattern of sustained engagement across all covenant traditions confirms that this is not a peripheral function but the constitutional purpose of the characteristic.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-034-003: T3 as a whole reveals that covenant comprehensively engages the inner faculties but with a specific structural bias: the faculties it most deeply and richly engages are those oriented toward the Other…
findings.finding_value: T3 as a whole reveals that covenant comprehensively engages the inner faculties but with a specific structural bias: the faculties it most deeply and richly engages are those oriented toward the Other (relational capacity, memory, cognition as knowing-God, moral evaluation, conscientiousness) rather than those oriented inward (creativity, which is notably absent). This faculty-engagement pattern is coherent with covenant's relational-disposition primary classification — covenant is constitutively Other-oriented and therefore engages the Other-oriented faculties most richly. The deepest T3 finding is the developmental one: the old covenant calls for volition from outside (demands obedience); the new covenant transforms volition from inside (liberates and enables faithfulness through Spirit). This volitional trajectory is confirmed across T3.6 (volition) and T3.7 (agency) and is the faculty-level expression of the same transformation that T2 identified at the constitutional-movement level and T5 identifies at the mechanism level. All three tiers point to the same inner-being reality from different analytical vantage points.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-009: T1 defines covenant as architecturally prior to other characteristics — the structure that makes other inner-being realities possible. T3 reveals which inner faculties this architectural priority enga…
findings.finding_value: T1 defines covenant as architecturally prior to other characteristics — the structure that makes other inner-being realities possible. T3 reveals which inner faculties this architectural priority engages: relational capacity (T3.11 — covenant is form; relational capacity is content), conscientiousness (T3.10 — covenant is the primary structuring reality for conscientious inner life), memory (T3.3 — covenant is constitutively temporal and requires memory to be held active), and volition (T3.6 — covenant calls for volition from within the old structure and transforms volition from within the new). The T1 × T3 synthesis: covenant's architectural character (T1) is instantiated through a specific set of inner faculties (T3) — the faculties it most deeply engages are precisely those that operate in the time-extended, Other-oriented, and morally structured modes that covenant's form requires. The characteristic is defined by the faculties it constitutes.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-019: T3 reveals that the inner faculties covenant most deeply engages are Other-oriented (relational capacity, conscience, moral evaluation, memory). T4 reveals that covenant's relational interfaces are as…
findings.finding_value: T3 reveals that the inner faculties covenant most deeply engages are Other-oriented (relational capacity, conscience, moral evaluation, memory). T4 reveals that covenant's relational interfaces are asymmetric (God initiates; human responds; horizontal is grounded in vertical). The T3 × T4 synthesis: the Other-oriented faculty bias (T3) and the asymmetric relational structure (T4) are coherently related — the inner faculties that covenant engages are precisely those required for the kind of asymmetric responsive relationship that covenant constitutes. The relational capacity (T3.11) is the constitutional equipment for genuine connection; the covenant's relational interfaces (T4) are the actual connections that this capacity enables. The inner posture required for human-to-God covenant movement (T4.2 — Q&A-106: reverent fear, love, all-heart, hearing orientation) corresponds directly to the inner faculties that covenant engages: fear engages moral evaluation (T3.8), love engages affect and relational capacity (T3.4, T3.11), all-heart engages volition (T3.6), and hearing engages perception (T3.1). T3 and T4 are two analytical views of the same responsive inner-being structure.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-021: T3 reveals that covenant is form; relational capacity is content (Q&A-100 — the T3.11 reciprocal finding). T6 reveals that covenant is structurally prior to and produces other characteristics includin…
findings.finding_value: T3 reveals that covenant is form; relational capacity is content (Q&A-100 — the T3.11 reciprocal finding). T6 reveals that covenant is structurally prior to and produces other characteristics including hope, knowing, and faithfulness. The T3 × T5 synthesis: the T3.11 finding (covenant as form; relational capacity as content) generalises to the T6 finding (covenant as architecturally prior to its C17 neighbour characteristics). In both cases, covenant is the structure; other inner-being realities (relational capacity, love/hesed, hope, knowing) are the content that the structure enables and sustains. This generalisation confirms that covenant's architectural character applies at both the faculty level (T3) and the inter-characteristic level (T6) — it is structurally prior at every level of the inner-being analysis.

findings.session_b_note: The relational pattern reveals that peace is constitutionally relational — it cannot be fully described as an inner private condition without reference to the other toward whom it is directed. findings.finding_value: T3 as a whole reveals that this characteristic engages virtually every inner faculty in the programme's 11-faculty model — the only consistent gap is creativity (T3.5, S across three prompts). The pattern of engagement is not uniform: perception is engaged as precondition (God hears before giving); cognition is constituted (wisdom is given, not generated); memory is deepened (the narrative-temporal dimension of covenantal giving); affect is the source of giving (compassion, anger) and the target of transformation (mourning→gladness); volition is called forth and elevated (genuine giving cannot be coerced); agency is the bridge between disposition and act; moral evaluation both produces and is produced by the characteristic; conscience is engaged indirectly through Spirit-forming and prophetic warning; conscientiousness at the human apex is the full integration of all three (moral awareness, will, act). Relational capacity is intrinsic — every mode is two-party. What T3 reveals as a whole: faithfulness-as-giving is not a faculty-specific characteristic but a whole-person characteristic — it recruits and integrates all active faculties into a unified inner-being act. The creativity silence is the only dimension where the data cannot confirm engagement.

findings.finding_value:
M06 characteristics consistently impair, invert, or destroy the relational capacity toward the object of the characteristic. No agent-side M06 characteristic enables or deepens the relational capacity toward the person who is the object of the hostility. The cluster documents the full range of ways the relational capacity can be degraded: organised against (hatred), removed from (contempt), withdrawn from (abhorrence), dominated (cruelty), perverted into pleasure at harm (malice). The horizontal relational capacity is consistently the most damaged faculty in M06. M06-E's intensification of the God-ward relational capacity is the inverse finding: the damage to horizontal relationships drives the person toward the vertical relationship with God.

findings.finding_value:
Relational capacity is one of the most consistently engaged faculties across all four sub-groups of M46. The wealth domain is fundamentally a relational testing ground: whether the person's material condition expands or contracts their relational reach — toward God (M46-A: contracted; M46-D: expanded) and toward others (M46-B: contracted into indifference; M46-D: expanded into giving). The cluster's four sub-groups can be read as four different relational configurations produced by the wealth domain.

[Cluster-level addition — Phase 9 cross-sub-group review] The person's treatment of and orientation toward the poor is the cluster's primary external index of internal wealth-domain condition across all four sub-groups. M46-A: relational capacity toward God closed — the inner-closed person cannot receive from God, and this closure also produces contempt toward the poor (sha.a.nan, Job 12:5). M46-B: relational capacity toward others contracted — hardness toward the poor (Luk 16:19-21; 2Sa 12:4), differential treatment of rich and poor in the assembly (Jam 2:2-6), and the use of the poor as a rhetorical cover for self-interest (Joh 12:6). M46-C: relational equality before God recognised across the wealth differential — the rich and poor equally made by God (Pro 22:2). M46-D: relational capacity expanded toward those the world excludes — giving to the poor is the commanded and paradigmatic act of release (Luk 14:13; Luk 18:22; Luk 19:8). The cluster's consistent witness: how the person with material goods relates to those without is the most visible surface of their inner wealth-domain condition.

findings.finding_value: The pattern reveals that fear is fundamentally a relational characteristic — its presence and direction determine the quality of the person's relationships. Fear of God (M01-A) is the ground of trust, justice, and genuine care in relationships. Social fear (M01-B-VCG-04) is the systematic distorter of relationship — it substitutes management of others' opinions for genuine other-care. The cluster confirms that the question "what does this person fear?" is the most revealing question about the quality of their relational life. Those who fear God relate authentically, justly, and generously; those who fear human opinion relate inauthentically, self-protectively, and with managed surfaces.

The pattern reveals that this characteristic is both produced by relational capacity (because anger requires a relational context — it is always about something or someone in relation to the person) and the primary threat to it (because disordered anger is the primary force that fractures relationship). The cluster is constitutively relational — it is an inner state about relationship — and its governance is the key condition for relational health.

M03 reveals grief as simultaneously the evidence of relational capacity (one grieves because one has genuinely bonded), the expression of relational capacity (grief shared as solidarity deepens bonds), and the restorer of relational capacity (godly grief enabling repentance and restored relationship). The characteristic is among the most relational in the programme — it cannot exist without the relational foundation that generates it, and it reaches its full resolution only through relational restoration or eschatological reversal.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Exultation is constitutively relational — it cannot occur in the absence of an object, and its proper object is God in the divine-human relation. The mutuality of exultation (God exults over his people; his people exult in him) makes this characteristic the affective evidence of the covenant relationship at its fullest.

---

## T4 — Relational Interface

**[CHAR-2]** E — Joy is constitutively relational — it reaches its fullness in and through genuine relational bonds. The M04-D sunchairo evidence is the most concentrated expression of this: co-rejoicing is a distinct inner-being phenomenon because Joy is structurally incomplete without being shared. The pattern reveals that Joy has a relational telos: present partial joy moves toward communal and divine-relational fullness (Joh 15:11; 16:24; 1Jo 1:4; Rev 19:7).

---

**[CHAR-7]** E — Suffering-Joy is constitutively communal in its primary NT register: the agalliao passages consistently show it shared, celebrated, and expressed in community. The characteristic deepens relational bonds precisely because it is a sharing of the paradox — the community that has genuinely rejoiced together through suffering has a bond that shared prosperity cannot produce.

---

*End of Segment 2 (T2–T3). Cumulative: 36 + 64 = 100 of 189 prompts answered for Characteristic 7.*

**[CHAR-3]** E — Gladness and relational capacity are mutually reinforcing in the relational-evaluation sub-register: the person who evaluates relational worth accurately inhabits genuine Gladness in their relationships (Ruth's love is genuinely better; open rebuke is genuinely the better good). And the person formed in genuine Gladness becomes more capable of authentic relational evaluation and engagement.

---

*End of Segment 2 (T2–T3). Cumulative: 36 + 64 = 100 of 189 prompts answered for Characteristic 3.*

**[CHAR-4]** E — Delight is the relational characteristic most closely tied to the motivational structure of relationships: what a person delights in determines who they protect (Jonathan and David), who they cherish (God and Ephraim), who they give themselves to (Paul and the Thessalonians), and who they become dangerously attached to (beast-captivation). The pattern reveals Delight as the relational-motivational engine — it is the inner disposition that drives relational action, making it the most powerful and most dangerous relational capacity in M04.

---

*End of Segment 2 (T2–T3). Cumulative: 36 + 64 = 100 of 189 prompts answered for Characteristic 4.*

**[CHAR-5]** E — Pleasure is the characteristic most directly generated through and sustained by relational bonds in M04. M04-J's entire corpus is relational pleasantness — the quality of what is agreeable between persons. The pattern reveals that the deepest human Pleasure in this corpus is relational (Jonathan-David; the beloved; brotherly unity) rather than material or sensory — relational pleasantness is the characteristic's most profound register.

---

*End of Segment 2 (T2–T3). Cumulative: 36 + 64 = 100 of 189 prompts answered for Characteristic 5.*

**[CHAR-6]** E — Wonder is inherently communal in its primary register: the VCG-01 proclamatory tradition is a community-sustaining practice. The pattern reveals that Wonder cannot remain private — its natural expression is communal declaration. This makes Wonder the most communally-directed characteristic in M04: its characteristic expressive mode is not personal prayer (like Delight) or individual formation (like Gladness through wisdom) but communal proclamation across generational boundaries.

---

*End of Segment 2 (T2–T3). Cumulative: 36 + 64 = 100 of 189 prompts answered for Characteristic 6.*

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster is constitutively relational: all seven characteristics have relational dimensions as either primary or prominent secondary features. This confirms that M04 is not a cluster of private spiritual emotions but of inherently-social, inherently-relational inner states that find their fullest expression in community and covenant. The cluster cannot be individualised without loss: Wonder that is never proclaimed (going against its entire VCG-01 pattern), Joy that is never shared (going against sunchairo), Delight that is never relational (going against M04-N and M04-H-VCG-02) — all would be diminished forms of their proper function.

---

*End of Segment 2 (T2–T3). Cumulative: 36 + 64 = 100 of 189 cluster-scope prompts answered.*

**[CHAR-1]** E — That CHAR-1's relational dimension is among its most theologically significant features. Shame is both the product of relational rupture (unjust wound from enemies, moral failure before God) and the gateway to relational restoration (corrective shame, penitential shame before God). The shame that closes the relationship (face turned away, mouth shut, presence withdrawn) is, when received as corrective, the opening through which relationship can be rebuilt. This makes shame a distinctively relational characteristic — it never operates in isolation from the person's relational field.

---
## T4 — Interfaces

**[CHAR-2]** E — CHAR-2 severely impairs relational capacity. The shaved envoys cannot return to public social life; the silenced man cannot engage in dialogue; the defeated nations cannot sustain former relationships with neighbours (derision replaces respect). 1Cor 15:43's mortal body "sown in dishonor" is in a condition of diminished relational capacity; resurrection glory restores it. CHAR-2's relational dimension is fundamental: it is enacted through the relational field and its primary effect is the disruption of the person's relational standing and capacity.

---

---

## T4 — Interfaces

**[CHAR-3]** E — CHAR-3 is constitutively relational — it is the degradation of the relational-capacity in its worth-recognition mode. The judge who "neither fears God nor respects man" (Luk 18:2) has lost the relational-capacity component of appropriate regard for the worth of others. This is CHAR-3's most direct faculty engagement: it is the failure of the relational faculty's worth-recognition mode.

---

---

## T4 — Interfaces

**[CHAR-4]** E — CHAR-4's evaluative operation in VCG-01 engages the relational capacity through community norms (the social-moral judgments about hair, speech in assembly, financial conduct). The idolatrous-shameful-objects register (VCG-01 — Jer 3:24; 11:13; Hos 9:10) shows CHAR-4 operating in the person's relational capacity with God — the shameful object is what has replaced God in the person's devotional relation.

---

---

## T4 — Interfaces

**[CHAR-5]** E — CHAR-5 is constitutively relational — it is the contempt-relation between persons, and its damage is in the relational field. The commands against despising (Rom 14:3; 14:10) are specifically about protecting relational capacity within the community: do not despise your brother is a relational-capacity protection instruction. CHAR-5 impairs the relational capacity of the recipient by reducing their standing to zero in the contempt-er's relational field — and by extension, in the community's.

---

---

## T4 — Interfaces

**[CHAR-6]** E — CHAR-6 is specifically relational in its function: it is the inner moral condition that enables the relational approach to God (Psa 26:6 — "I wash my hands in innocence and go around your altar"). The relational capacity that CHAR-6 enables is specifically the person-to-God relational approach — worship, petition, covenant engagement. Its absence (Hos 8:5) blocks this relational capacity: the incapacity for innocence bars the approach to God that the covenant relationship requires.

---

---

## T4 — Interfaces
